Ch. 5 · Nodes shrunk to the limit: wireless sensor networks

2 practice · 1 past-examNotes →
B·C quiz
B·C quiz
Past final exam
2025-26 S2Q4(c)5 marks
Topics: communication architecture of a sensor network: multi-hop nodes → sink → task manager node考点：传感器网络的通信架构：节点多跳 → sink → 任务管理节点
Original question (verbatim)

(c) A sensor network is composed of many sensor nodes which are densely distributed to sense the environment. Briefly describe the communication architecture in the sensor networks to support the network operations. Describe briefly the communication architecture and show how the sensor nodes can relay the information back to the manager of the sensor network.

(5 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
① Sensor nodes (notes Part B p.57): a large number of sensor nodes are scattered in the sensor field; each node can collect data and also route data back to the sink. Reason: a single node has very limited power, computing capability and memory (p.56) and can only communicate over short distances, so every node is both a data source and a relay for other nodes.① 传感器节点（讲义 Part B p.57）：大量传感器节点散布在传感区域（sensor field）里，每个节点都能采集数据，也能把数据路由回汇聚节点（sink）。原因：单个节点的功率、计算能力和存储都很有限（p.56），只能做短距离通信，所以每个节点既是数据源，也要帮别人转发。
2
② Multi-hop forwarding to the sink: data is forwarded to the sink node by node in a multi-hop, infrastructureless way. Reason: nodes have a short range, so nodes far from the sink must rely on intermediate nodes as relays; there is no base station in the field, so the network can only be formed ad hoc; and several short hops also use less energy than one long hop.② 多跳转发到 sink：数据以多跳、无基础设施（multi-hop, infrastructureless）的方式，一个节点接一个节点地转发到 sink。原因：节点射程短，离 sink 远的节点必须靠中间节点中继；现场没有基站，只能用 ad hoc 方式组网；几段短距离传输也比一跳长距离传输更省电。
3
③ Sink → manager: the sink then communicates with the task manager node via the Internet or satellite. The manager (user) obtains the data there, and also sends tasks and queries back the other way from there. Reason: the sink is the gateway between the sensor network and external networks, and the user is usually far from the sensor field.③ sink → 管理者：sink 再经互联网或卫星与任务管理节点（task manager node）通信。管理者（用户）在那里获取数据，也从那里反方向下发任务和查询。原因：sink 是传感网与外部网络之间的网关，而用户通常远离传感区域。
4
Sketch: Sensor A → Sensor B → Sensor C → … → Sink → Internet/satellite → task manager node (user). In the drawing, show a chain of nodes with arrows pointing to the sink, and label it "multi-hop".示意：传感器 A → 传感器 B → 传感器 C → … → Sink → Internet/卫星 → 任务管理节点（用户）。作图时画一串节点箭头指向 sink，标上 "multi-hop"。
5
Other factors that support network operation (bonus marks): the design is affected by reliability, scalability, production cost, operating environment, network topology, hardware constraints, transmission media and power consumption (p.57). The protocol stack consists of the physical, data link (MAC), network, transport and application layers, plus three planes (power management, mobility management and task management) that monitor the energy, movement and task allocation of each node (p.59).支撑网络运行的其他要素（加分）：设计受可靠性、可扩展性、生产成本、工作环境、网络拓扑、硬件约束、传输介质和功耗影响（p.57）。协议栈分为物理层、数据链路层（MAC）、网络层、传输层、应用层，外加功耗管理、移动性管理、任务管理三个平面，负责监控各节点的能量、移动和任务分配（p.59）。
Sensor nodes forward over multiple hops → Sink → Internet/satellite → Task manager传感器节点多跳转发 → Sink → Internet/卫星 → Task manager
◆ Key points
What it tests
Communication architecture of a wireless sensor network (Part B p.56–59).无线传感器网络的通信架构（Part B p.56–59）。
Answer points
Sensor nodes scattered in the area → multi-hop, infrastructureless forwarding → sink → Internet or satellite → task manager node (where the user retrieves data and issues tasks).传感器节点散布在区域内 → 多跳、无基础设施地转发 → 汇聚节点 sink → 互联网或卫星 → 任务管理节点（用户在这里取数据、下发任务）。
Bonus points
Design factors: reliability, scalability, cost, operating environment, topology, hardware constraints, transmission media, power consumption; protocol stack of five layers plus three management planes (power, mobility, task).设计因素：可靠性、可扩展性、成本、工作环境、拓扑、硬件约束、传输介质、功耗；协议栈五层加功耗、移动性、任务三个管理平面。
Drawing tip
Draw a chain of nodes with arrows pointing to the sink, then from the sink to the Internet/satellite and the task manager, and label it "multi-hop".画一串节点箭头指向 sink，再从 sink 画到 Internet/卫星和 task manager，标上"multi-hop"。
Concept + Step by step: communication architecture of a sensor network

ConceptWhat a wireless sensor network is

A wireless sensor network (WSN) consists of a large number of small sensor nodes densely deployed in the area to be monitored, collecting data such as temperature and vibration. It borrows techniques from wireless ad hoc networks but has its own features (Part B p.56): the number of nodes is several orders of magnitude larger than in an ad hoc network; nodes are densely deployed and prone to failure, so the topology changes often; nodes communicate by broadcast, whereas ad hoc networks are point-to-point; and nodes have very limited power, computing capacity and memory. These features dictate how it communicates: no infrastructure, multi-hop forwarding.无线传感器网络（WSN，Wireless Sensor Network）由大量小型传感器节点组成，密集地布在要监测的区域里，采集温度、振动等数据。它借用了无线自组网（ad hoc）的技术，但有自己的特点（Part B p.56）：节点数量比 ad hoc 网络多几个数量级；节点密集部署、容易失效，拓扑变化频繁；节点用广播方式通信，而 ad hoc 是点对点；节点的电量、计算能力和存储都很有限。这些特点决定了它的通信方式：没有基础设施、多跳转发。

Step by stepKey points of the communication architecture (Part B p.57–58)

  1. Sensor field: sensor nodes are scattered in the sensor field; each node can both collect data and route data back to the sink.传感区域（sensor field）：传感器节点散布在传感区域里，每个节点既能采集数据，也能把数据路由回汇聚节点。
  2. Sink: all data ends up at the sink. Data is forwarded to the sink node by node in a multi-hop, infrastructureless way. Why multi-hop: each node has limited energy and low transmit power, so its range is short; relaying through neighbours saves energy and still covers a large area.汇聚节点（sink）：所有数据最终送到 sink。数据以多跳、无基础设施（multi-hop, infrastructureless）的方式，一个节点接一个节点地转发到 sink。为什么多跳：每个节点电量有限、发射功率小，覆盖距离短，靠邻居接力既省电又能覆盖大片区域。
  3. Task manager node: the sink communicates with the task manager node via the Internet or satellite. The network's manager (user) gets the data at the task manager node and also sends tasks into the network from there (queries and commands travel back to the nodes in the opposite direction).任务管理节点（task manager node）：sink 通过互联网或卫星与任务管理节点通信。网络的管理者（用户）在任务管理节点获取数据，也从那里向网络下发任务（查询、指令沿相反方向传回节点）。
  4. Path of the information back to the user: sensor A → sensor B → sensor C → … → sink → Internet/satellite → task manager (user).信息回传的路径：传感器 A → 传感器 B → 传感器 C → … → sink → Internet/卫星 → task manager（用户）。

Drawing tip: draw a box for the sensor field with many small dots inside; from some node A draw several arrow segments via B and C to the sink (label them "multi-hop"); put the sink at the edge of the box, then draw an arrow to a cloud (Internet/satellite) and finally to the task manager and the user. The question says "show how", so a diagram plus text is safest.作图提示：画一个方框表示 sensor field，里面画很多小圆点，从某个节点 A 画几段箭头经过 B、C 到 sink（标"multi-hop"）；sink 在方框边上，再画箭头到云（Internet/satellite），最后到 task manager 和 user。题目说 "show how"，画图加文字最稳。

Step by stepBonus points (if time allows)

  • Design factors (p.57): reliability (fault tolerance), scalability, production cost, operating environment, network topology, hardware constraints, transmission media, power consumption.设计影响因素（p.57）：可靠性（容错）、可扩展性、生产成本、工作环境、网络拓扑、硬件约束、传输介质、功耗。
  • Protocol stack (p.59): five layers (physical, data link (MAC), network, transport, application) plus three planes (power management, mobility management, task management). The lecturer said remembering the five layers is enough; power consumption is the most critical factor because nodes mostly run on batteries.协议栈（p.59）：物理层、数据链路（MAC）层、网络层、传输层、应用层五层，加上功耗管理、移动性管理、任务管理三个平面。老师说协议栈记住五层就行，功耗是最关键的因素，因为节点大多靠电池。

PitfallsCommon ways to lose marks

  • Saying each node sends straight to a base station (single hop): the notes stress multi-hop, no infrastructure.写成每个节点直接发给基站（单跳）：讲义强调的是多跳、无基础设施。
  • Leaving out the sink → task manager leg (via the Internet or satellite).漏了 sink 到 task manager 这一段（经 Internet 或卫星）。
  • Only listing the protocol-stack layers without explaining "how the information travels all the way back to the manager", which is the main point of the question.只罗列协议栈各层，没讲"信息怎么一路传回管理者"，题目问的重点是后者。

ExamHow to write it in English

The sensor nodes are scattered in a sensor field. Each sensor node has the capability to collect data and to route data back to the sink. Since the nodes have limited power and short transmission range, data are routed back to the sink through a multi-hop, infrastructureless architecture: each node forwards its data to a neighbouring node, which relays it hop by hop towards the sink.

The sink then communicates with the task manager node via the Internet or a satellite link. The manager (user) obtains the sensed information at the task manager node and can also send tasks/queries back to the sensor nodes in the reverse direction.

[Sketch: sensor node A → B → C → … → Sink → Internet/Satellite → Task manager node → User.]

The design of this architecture is influenced by reliability (fault tolerance), scalability, production cost, operating environment, network topology, hardware constraints, transmission media and power consumption. Each node uses a protocol stack of physical, data link, network, transport and application layers, together with power, mobility and task management planes.

In one line: sensor nodes collect data and relay it multi-hop, without infrastructure, to the sink; the sink sends it via the Internet or satellite to the task manager node, where the manager gets the data and issues tasks.一句话：传感器节点采集数据，多跳、无基础设施地接力转发到 sink，sink 再经 Internet 或卫星送到任务管理节点，管理者在那里取数据、下发任务。

Topics: the two parallel stacks of the simplified IoT architecture · why fog computing is needed考点：简化 IoT 架构的两个并行栈 · 为什么要引入雾计算
Original question (verbatim)

4. (a) For Internet of Things (IoT), the simplified IoT architecture consists of two parallel stacks, i.e., the Management and Compute Stack and Core IoT Functional Stack. Briefly describe the major components in each of the two stacks.

(7 Marks)

(b) Discuss the necessity to introduce Fog Computing into the simplified IoT architecture.

(6 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
(a) Overall framework (notes Part B p.86): the simplified IoT architecture is two three-layer stacks side by side. The Core IoT Functional Stack on the left answers "how does data get from the things to the applications"; the IoT Data Management and Compute Stack on the right answers "where is the data processed". The two stacks correspond layer by layer.(a) 总体框架（讲义 Part B p.86）：简化 IoT 架构是两个并排的三层栈。左边 Core IoT Functional Stack 回答"数据怎么从物体传到应用"，右边 IoT Data Management and Compute Stack 回答"数据在哪里处理"，两栈逐层对应。
2
(a) Core IoT Functional Stack (three layers) (p.89–90):
① "Things" layer (smart objects such as sensors and actuators): the physical devices must fit the constraints of the deployment environment (power, size, mobility) while still delivering the data needed;
② Communications network layer: when objects are not self-contained, they must communicate with outside systems. It has four sublayers: the access network (last mile: 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa, etc.), gateways and backhaul (gather the devices in an area at a gateway, then send their data back to a central station over a long-range link), network transport (IP, UDP/TCP; must be open, standard and scalable to huge numbers of devices) and IoT network management (application protocols such as HTTP and WebSocket that let head-end applications exchange data with the sensors, p.99);
③ Application and analytics layer: processes the collected data, doing data analytics, network analytics and smart decision-making, and in the other direction controls the objects so that they adjust their behaviour or parameters (p.100–101).(a) 核心功能栈（Core IoT Functional Stack，三层）（p.89–90）：
① "Things" 层（传感器、执行器等智能物体）：物理设备要适应部署环境的约束（供电、体积、移动性），同时还要能提供所需的数据；
② 通信网络层：物体不能自给自足时要和外部系统通信，分四个子层——接入网（最后一公里，802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa 等）、网关与回传（把一片区域内的设备汇聚到网关，再用长距离链路送回中心站）、网络传输（IP、UDP/TCP，要开放、标准、能扩展到海量设备）、IoT 网络管理（HTTP、WebSocket 等应用协议，让头端应用和传感器交换数据，p.99）；
③ 应用与分析层：处理收集的数据，既做数据分析、网络分析和智能决策，也反过来控制物体，让它们调整行为或参数（p.100–101）。
3
(a) Data Management and Compute Stack (p.103, p.110–113): decides where data is filtered, aggregated, stored and analysed. Its three levels correspond to the core stack:
① Edge / mist: the most basic filtering and decisions are made on the sensor or device itself (new-generation end devices already have this computing power);
② Fog: real-time processing on network devices close to the end devices, such as gateways and routers;
③ Cloud (data centre): central storage, historical data, big-data analytics.
Division of work: the more real-time the data, the closer to the edge it is processed; data that is not urgent goes to the cloud (p.113).(a) 数据管理与计算栈（Data Management and Compute Stack）（p.103、p.110–113）：决定数据在哪里过滤、汇聚、存储和分析，三个层次对应核心栈：
① 边缘（edge / mist）：在传感器或设备本身做最基本的过滤和判断（新一代终端已有这样的算力）；
② 雾（fog）：在靠近终端的网关、路由器等网络设备上做实时处理；
③ 云（cloud / 数据中心）：集中存储、历史数据、大数据分析。
分工原则：越要求实时的数据越靠近边缘处理，不急的数据送云（p.113）。
4
(b) What goes wrong with cloud only (p.104–105): if all data is sent straight to the cloud for processing:
• the last-mile IoT network has very limited bandwidth and cannot carry the huge volume of data;
• the round-trip delay is large, so real-time response is lost;
• gateway backhaul links often rely on 3G/LTE or even satellite, which is unreliable;
• the data volume on the backhaul is too large for the data centre to receive, store and process;
• big data keeps growing, so real-time analysis and response become almost impossible.(b) 只用云端会出什么问题（p.104–105）：数据全部直接送云处理时——
• 最后一公里 IoT 网络带宽很有限，海量数据挤不进去；
• 来回时延大，失去实时响应能力；
• 网关的回传链路常依赖 3G/LTE 甚至卫星，不可靠；
• 回传上的数据量太大，数据中心难以接收、存储和处理；
• 大数据越来越大，实时分析和响应几乎不可能。
5
(b) How fog computing solves this (p.106–109): data processing is distributed as close to the edge of the IP network as possible (any device with computing, storage and network connectivity can act as a fog node):
• analysis close by → lower latency, real-time reaction;
• only results or summaries are sent upward → offloads the core network, removing much of its traffic, and compresses/reduces the data;
• sensitive data stays in the local network;
• fog nodes are geographically close to the sensors, so they have context/location awareness and form distributed edge control loops without waiting for instructions from the cloud.
Fog and edge do not replace the cloud; they are its "first line of defence", and the three levels work together (p.111).(b) 雾计算怎么解决（p.106–109）：把数据处理分散到尽量靠近 IP 网络边缘的地方（任何有计算、存储和联网能力的设备都能当雾节点）：
• 就近分析 → 降低时延，能实时反应；
• 只把结果或摘要往上送 → 卸载核心网大量流量，压缩/精简数据；
• 敏感数据留在本地网络里；
• 雾节点地理上靠近传感器，有上下文/位置感知，形成分布式的边缘控制回路，不必等云端指令。
雾和边缘不取代云，而是云的"第一道防线"，三层配合工作（p.111）。
Two stacks: Things / communications network (4 sublayers) / application and analytics; Edge / Fog / Cloud. Fog computing solves the problems of bandwidth, latency, backhaul reliability and data volume两栈：Things / 通信网络（4 子层）/ 应用与分析；Edge / Fog / Cloud。雾计算解决带宽、时延、回传可靠性和数据量问题
◆ Key points
What it tests
The two parallel stacks of the simplified IoT architecture; why fog computing is needed (Part B p.86–91, p.103–106).简化 IoT 架构的两个并行栈；为什么需要雾计算（Part B p.86–91、p.103–106）。
Answer points
Core functional stack, three layers: Things / communications network (four sublayers) / application and analytics. Data management and compute stack: edge / fog / cloud.核心功能栈三层：Things / 通信网络（四个子层）/ 应用与分析。数据管理与计算栈：边缘 / 雾 / 云。
Why fog computing
Four problems: limited last-mile bandwidth, large delay to the cloud, unreliable backhaul links, too much data. Four benefits: low latency, offloading the core network, keeping sensitive data local, compressing data before upload.四个问题：最后一公里带宽有限、到云端时延大、回传链路不可靠、数据量太大。四个好处：低时延、卸载核心网、敏感数据留在本地、上传前压缩数据。
Memory aid
Edge is on the device, fog on the gateway / router, cloud in the data centre: each one further from the end device.边缘在设备上，雾在网关 / 路由器上，云在数据中心，离终端越来越远。
Links
The four sublayers of the communications network layer are the exact question in 2024-25 Q4(b) and 2025-26 S2 Q4(d); the features of fog computing are 2025-26 S1 Q4(c).通信网络层四子层是 2024-25 Q4(b)、2025-26 S2 Q4(d) 的原题；雾计算的特征是 2025-26 S1 Q4(c)。
Concept + Step by step: the two stacks of the simplified IoT architecture and fog computing

ConceptSimplified IoT architecture: a pair of parallel three-layer stacks

An IoT system has thousands of sensors, and data must travel all the way from the "things" to the application. To make this clear, the notes (Part B p.86–91) use Cisco's simplified IoT architecture: two parallel three-layer stacks. The lecturer said in class that this part is learned with this simplified framework, which is easier to understand than the other two standards.IoT 系统里有成千上万个传感器，数据要从"物"一路送到应用。为了看清楚，讲义（Part B p.86–91）用 Cisco 的简化 IoT 架构：两个并行的三层栈。老师课上说学这一部分用这个简化框架，比另外两个标准好理解。

Core IoT Functional StackIoT Data Management and Compute Stack
Layer 3: Applications and analytics layerLayer 3：应用与分析层（Applications and analytics）Cloud (data centre)
Layer 2: Communications network layer, with four sublayersLayer 2：通信网络层（Communications network），四个子层Fog (gateways / routers and other network devices)雾（fog，网关 / 路由器等网络设备）
Layer 1: "Things" layer (sensors, actuators)Layer 1："Things" 层（传感器、执行器）Edge / mist (the devices themselves)边缘（edge / mist，设备本身）

The left side answers "how the data is transported", the right side answers "where the data is computed"; the two match layer by layer.左边回答"数据怎么传"，右边回答"数据在哪里算"，两者一层对一层。

Step by step(a) Components of the two stacks (7 marks; for each component write "what it is + what it does")

  1. Things layer: smart objects such as sensors and actuators. They must be designed to fit the constraints of the deployment environment (battery or mains power, fixed or mobile, reporting frequency, data volume, coverage range, density) while still providing the data needed (p.89–91).Things 层：传感器、执行器等智能物体。设计时要适应部署环境的约束（电池或市电、静止或移动、上报频率、数据量、覆盖距离、密度），同时还能提供需要的数据（p.89–91）。
  2. Communications network layer: when objects are not self-contained, they must communicate with external systems. Four sublayers: access network sublayer (last mile, 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa), gateways and backhaul sublayer (aggregates the objects of an area at a gateway, then sends the data back to a central station over a long-range medium), network transport sublayer (IP, UDP/TCP), IoT network management sublayer (application protocols such as HTTP, WebSocket).通信网络层：物体不能自给自足时，要和外部系统通信，分四个子层：接入网子层（最后一公里，802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa）、网关与回传子层（把一片区域的物体汇聚到网关，再用长距离介质送回中心站）、网络传输子层（IP、UDP/TCP）、IoT 网络管理子层（HTTP、WebSocket 等应用协议）。
  3. Applications and analytics layer: processes the collected data, makes intelligent decisions, and in turn controls the "things" or other systems to change their behaviour or parameters.应用与分析层：处理收集到的数据，做智能决策，并反过来控制"物"或其他系统改变行为或参数。
  4. Data management and compute stack: the edge (mist) does the most basic filtering and decisions inside the sensors / devices; the fog does real-time processing on the network devices closest to the end devices; the cloud does central storage, historical data and large-scale analytics. The three complement each other; they do not replace each other (p.110–111).数据管理与计算栈：边缘（mist）在传感器 / 设备里做最基本的过滤和判断；雾在离终端最近的网络设备上做实时处理；云做集中存储、历史数据和大规模分析。三者互补，不是替代（p.110–111）。

Step by step(b) Why fog computing is needed (6 marks: problems first, then benefits)

If all data is sent to the cloud for central processing (whose only advantage is simplicity), notes p.103–105 list these problems:如果所有数据都送到云端集中处理（优点只是简单），讲义 p.103–105 列出的问题：

  • Last-mile IoT networks have very limited bandwidth and cannot carry the huge volume of data;最后一公里的 IoT 网络带宽很有限，海量数据送不上去；
  • Latency is high, so real-time response is lost;时延大，失去实时响应能力；
  • Gateway backhaul often relies on 3G/LTE or even satellite, which is unreliable;网关的回传常靠 3G/LTE 甚至卫星，不可靠；
  • The data volume on the backhaul is too large, and real-time analytics on big data becomes harder and harder.回传上的数据量太大，大数据越来越难做实时分析。

Fog computing (p.106–109) distributes data processing to places as close as possible to the edge of the IP network; any device with computing, storage and network connectivity can be a fog node. Benefits: local analysis reduces latency; it offloads a large amount of traffic from the core network; sensitive data stays in the local network; fog nodes are geographically close to the sensors and are context-aware, so they can form distributed edge control loops that monitor and control devices in real time without waiting for the cloud; data reduction before upload (after preprocessing, the upper layers only need to batch-process part of the data). The lecturer summarised it in class as: distributed processing, fast because there is no wait for a central server, data reduced before upload, real-time processing, and wireless links between fog nodes and end devices.雾计算（p.106–109）把数据处理分散到尽量靠近 IP 网络边缘的地方，任何有计算、存储和联网能力的设备都可以做雾节点。好处：就近分析降低时延；为核心网卸载大量流量；敏感数据留在本地网络；雾节点地理上靠近传感器，有上下文感知，能形成分布式的边缘控制回路，实时监测和控制设备而不必等云端；上传前先做数据精简（预处理后上层只需批处理一部分数据）。老师课上概括为：分布式处理、不用等中心服务器所以快、上传前先精简、能实时处理、雾节点和终端之间用无线连接。

PitfallsWatch out

  • Each stack has three layers; do not count the "four sublayers of the communications network layer" as a fourth and fifth layer.两个栈各三层，别把"通信网络层的四个子层"当成第四、五层。
  • The edge is on the devices, the fog on gateways / routers, the cloud in data centres, each further from the end devices.边缘在设备上，雾在网关 / 路由器上，云在数据中心，距离终端越来越远。
  • In (b), writing only benefits without the problems looks like you did not answer the "necessity"; write the problems first, then how fog solves them.(b) 只写好处不写问题会显得没回答"necessity"；先写问题再写雾怎么解决。

ExamHow to write it in English

(a) The simplified IoT architecture consists of two parallel three-layer stacks.

Core IoT Functional Stack. (1) "Things" layer: sensors, actuators and other smart objects; they must fit the constraints of the deployment environment (power source, mobility, reporting frequency, data volume, range, density) while still providing the required information. (2) Communications network layer, divided into four sublayers: the access network sublayer (the last mile, typically wireless such as IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g and LoRa); the gateways and backhaul sublayer (smart objects in an area are organised around a common gateway, which forwards the data over a longer-range medium to a headend station); the network transport sublayer (open, standard network and transport protocols such as IP, UDP and TCP); and the IoT network management sublayer (application protocols such as HTTP and WebSocket that let headend applications exchange data with the sensors). (3) Application and analytics layer: applications process the collected data, make intelligent decisions and, in turn, instruct the things or other systems to adapt their behaviour or parameters.

Data Management and Compute Stack. It defines where the data is processed: at the edge (mist) inside the sensors and devices themselves for basic filtering and simple decisions; in the fog, on network devices such as gateways and routers close to the endpoints, for real-time processing; and in the cloud (data centre) for centralised storage, historical data and large-scale analytics. These layers complement each other.

(b) If all data were sent to the cloud for centralised processing: the available bandwidth in last-mile IoT networks is very limited; the latency is high, so real-time response is lost; the backhaul from the gateway is often unreliable (3G/LTE or satellite); and the volume of data is too large to transport and to analyse in real time. Fog computing solves these problems by distributing data management as close to the edge of the IP network as possible. Analysing data near where it is collected minimises latency, offloads large amounts of traffic from the core network and keeps sensitive data inside the local network. Because a fog node is geographically close to the sensors it has contextual awareness and can react to events quickly, providing a distributed edge control loop in real time without waiting for the cloud. It also reduces the data (pre-processing) before sending it upstream, so the cloud only needs to handle a subset of the data.

In one line: core functional stack = Things / communications network (four sublayers: access, gateway-backhaul, transport, management) / applications and analytics; compute stack = edge / fog / cloud; fog computing solves four problems: bandwidth, latency, unreliable backhaul and excessive data volume.一句话：核心功能栈 = Things / 通信网络（接入、网关回传、传输、管理四子层）/ 应用分析，计算栈 = 边缘 / 雾 / 云；雾计算是为了解决带宽、时延、回传不可靠和数据量过大四个问题。

Past final exam
2024-25 S2Q4(b)8 marks
Topics: the four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer考点：IoT 通信网络层的四个子层
Original question (verbatim)

(b) Internet of Things (IoT) networks are built around the concept of "things" or smart objects performing functions and delivering new connected services. For the core functional IoT stack, the communication network layer is structured with four sublayers. List down each of these sublayers and briefly describe the each of the features.

(8 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
Place it first: the core IoT functional stack has three layers: Things layer (sensors/actuators) → communications network layer → application and analytics layer (notes Part B p.89–90). The question asks about the middle layer, the communications network layer; its four sublayers are listed in the order the data travels, from the things to the centre.先定位：核心 IoT 功能栈（core IoT functional stack）分三层：Things 层（传感器/执行器）→ 通信网络层 → 应用与分析层（讲义 Part B p.89–90）。题目问的是中间的通信网络层，它的四个子层按数据从物体走向中心的顺序排列。
2
Access network sublayer: the "last mile" of the IoT network, usually a wireless technology such as 802.11ah, 802.15.4g or LoRa; classified by range into PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN and MAN/WAN (notes p.89, p.93–97). Why the choice depends on range, number of objects and cost: most smart objects are battery-powered and send little data, and different scenarios need very different range and power, so no single technology fits all; the topology can be point-to-point or point-to-multipoint (star, clustered star, mesh).接入网子层（Access network）：IoT 网络的"最后一公里"，通常是无线技术，如 802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa；按覆盖范围分 PAN、HAN、NAN、FAN、LAN、MAN/WAN（讲义 p.89、p.93–97）。为什么要按距离、物体数量和成本来选：智能物体大多电池供电、数据量小，不同场景要的距离和功耗差别很大，没有一种技术通吃；拓扑可以是点对点，也可以是点对多点（星形、簇状星形、网状）。
3
Gateways and backhaul sublayer: aggregates the many smart objects in an area into a common gateway, which then forwards the data over a longer-range medium (e.g. cellular, fibre) to the headend central station (notes p.89, p.98). Why it is needed: access technologies have short range and low rates and cannot reach the distant centre directly, so the gateway converts between the two media. The objects may be static or move within a small area; the gateway is usually fixed.网关与回传子层（Gateways and backhaul）：把一片区域内的多个智能物体汇聚到一个公共网关，网关再用更长距离的介质（如蜂窝、光纤）把数据转发到头端中心站（讲义 p.89、p.98）。为什么需要：接入技术距离短、速率低，不能直接连到远处的中心，网关负责两种介质之间的转换。物体可以静止或在小范围内移动，网关通常固定。
4
Network transport sublayer: uses open, standardised network- and transport-layer protocols (IP, UDP/TCP) to connect all kinds of devices and media; it must scale to thousands of sensors and be secure (notes p.90, p.98–99). Why IP: it is flexible and can run over low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss networks; with TCP the network takes care of reliable delivery, with UDP control is left to the application, and you choose whichever is needed.网络传输子层（Network transport）：用开放、标准化的网络层和传输层协议（IP、UDP/TCP）把各种设备和介质连起来；要求能扩展到成千上万个传感器，并保证安全（讲义 p.90、p.98–99）。为什么选 IP：它灵活，能跑在低功耗、低带宽、高丢包的网络上；TCP 由网络负责可靠传送，UDP 把控制交给应用，按需要选。
5
IoT network management sublayer: application-layer protocols that handle the data exchange between the smart objects and the headend applications (notes p.90, p.99), for example HTTP over TCP (the sensor acts as a client that connects to the application), and WebSocket, a lightweight two-way protocol suited to low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss environments. Why it is needed: IP connectivity alone is not enough; the two ends must also agree on how data is packaged and how requests and responses work.IoT 网络管理子层（IoT network management）：应用层协议，负责智能物体与头端应用之间的数据交换（讲义 p.90、p.99），例如基于 TCP 的 HTTP（传感器作为客户端去连应用），以及适合低内存、低功耗、低带宽、高丢包环境的轻量双向协议 WebSocket。为什么需要：光有 IP 连通还不够，两端还要约定数据怎么打包、怎么请求和回应。
Access network / Gateways & backhaul / Network transport / IoT network management
◆ Key points
What it tests
The four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer (Part B p.89–95).IoT 通信网络层的四个子层（Part B p.89–95）。
Answer points
Access network (last-mile wireless: 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa; PAN/HAN/NAN/FAN/LAN/WAN) → gateways and backhaul (aggregate an area, then send the data back to the centre over a long-range medium) → network transport (IP, UDP/TCP; open standards, scalable, secure) → IoT network management (application protocols such as HTTP, WebSocket).接入网（最后一公里无线：802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa；PAN/HAN/NAN/FAN/LAN/WAN）→ 网关与回传（区域汇聚后用长距离介质送回中心）→ 网络传输（IP、UDP/TCP，开放标准、可扩展、安全）→ IoT 网络管理（HTTP、WebSocket 等应用协议）。
Memory aid
Bottom up: "access → aggregation/backhaul → transport (IP) → management (application protocols)".自下而上："接入 → 汇聚回传 → 传输（IP）→ 管理（应用协议）"。
Common mistakes
The network transport sublayer is IP/TCP/UDP; the network management sublayer is HTTP/WebSocket. Do not swap them.网络传输子层是 IP/TCP/UDP，网络管理子层是 HTTP/WebSocket，别放反。
Links
Asked again as 2025-26 S2 Q4(d); 2023-24 Q4(a) asks you to place it within the whole stack.2025-26 S2 Q4(d) 原题重考；2023-24 Q4(a) 要求把它放进整个栈里写。
Concept + Step by step: the four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer

ConceptWhere the communications network layer sits in the IoT stack

The core IoT functional stack has three layers: Things layer → communications network layer → application and analytics layer (notes Part B p.88–90). If smart objects are not self-contained, they must report the information they collect, exchange it with other objects or be controlled by a management platform; all of this relies on the communications network layer. From bottom to top it has four sublayers (p.89–99), which you can think of as "four gates the data passes through on its way from the sensor to the application".核心 IoT 功能栈有三层：Things 层 → 通信网络层 → 应用与分析层（讲义 Part B p.88–90）。智能物体（smart objects）如果不能自给自足，就要把采集到的信息报告出去、和别的物体交换、或接受管理平台控制，这些都靠通信网络层。它由下往上分四个子层（p.89–99），可以理解为"数据从传感器走到应用要过的四道关"。

SublayerRoleTypical technologies
Access networkThe last mile: connects the objects to the network最后一公里，把物体接进网络802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa; PAN/HAN/NAN/FAN/LAN/WAN
Gateways and backhaulAggregates the objects of an area at a gateway, then sends the data over a long distance back to the centre把一片区域的物体汇聚到网关，再长距离送回中心Gateway + cellular / fibre or other long-range links网关 + 蜂窝 / 光纤等长距离链路
Network transportUses open-standard network- and transport-layer protocols to connect different devices and media用开放标准的网络层、传输层协议连接各种设备和介质IP, UDP, TCP
IoT network managementData exchange between head-end applications and sensors头端应用和传感器之间的数据交换HTTP, WebSocket

Step by stepFeatures of each sublayer (why it is designed this way)

  1. Access network sublayer: the last mile of the IoT network, usually wireless. Different technologies differ in range, power and data rate, so they are grouped by range into PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN, WAN, etc.; a technology is directly tied to the topologies it supports (star, mesh, etc.) (p.94–97). The lecturer mentioned in class that a mesh topology has several alternative routes and is more reliable.接入网子层：IoT 网络的最后一公里，通常是无线技术。不同技术的覆盖范围、功耗、速率不同，所以按范围分成 PAN、HAN、NAN、FAN、LAN、WAN 等；技术和它支持的拓扑（星形、网状等）直接相关（p.94–97）。老师课上提到：mesh 拓扑有多条备选路由，更可靠。
  2. Gateways and backhaul sublayer: a common communication system organises several objects in an area around one gateway. The gateway handles "cross-medium" communication and forwards the data over a longer-range medium to the head-end central station. Objects may be fixed or move within a small area; the gateway is usually fixed (p.98).网关与回传子层：一个公共通信系统把某一区域的多个物体组织到一个网关周围，网关负责"跨介质"通信，用更长距离的介质把数据转发到头端中心站。物体可以静止或在小范围内移动，网关一般固定（p.98）。
  3. Network transport sublayer: to support many industries and media, the protocols must be open and standard; they must also scale to thousands or even millions of sensors in one network and be secure. IP meets these needs: it can be embedded in all kinds of objects and runs over low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss networks. On top of it, TCP lets the network control reliable delivery, while UDP leaves control to the application (p.98–99).网络传输子层：要支持多行业、多介质，协议必须开放、标准化；还要可扩展到单个网络里成千上万甚至上百万个传感器，并保证安全。IP 满足这些要求，能嵌入各种物体、跑在低功耗、低带宽、高丢包的网络上；上面的 TCP 由网络控制可靠传输，UDP 则把控制交给应用（p.98–99）。
  4. IoT network management sublayer: application-layer protocols carry data between smart objects and other systems. Examples: HTTP over TCP (the sensor acts as a client connecting to the IoT application); WebSocket is a lightweight Web-derived protocol suited to low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss environments, and it provides a simple two-way connection (p.99).IoT 网络管理子层：应用层协议负责智能物体和其他系统之间的数据传输。例如基于 TCP 的 HTTP（传感器作为客户端连接 IoT 应用）；WebSocket 是轻量的 Web 派生协议，适合低内存、低功耗、低带宽、高丢包环境，提供简单的双向连接（p.99）。

PitfallsWatch out

  • Order from bottom to top: access → gateways/backhaul → transport → management. Write them in this order so the marker can check them easily.顺序自下而上：接入 → 网关回传 → 传输 → 管理，按这个顺序写，阅卷人好对。
  • Network transport is IP/TCP/UDP; network management is HTTP/WebSocket. Do not swap them.网络传输是 IP/TCP/UDP，网络管理是 HTTP/WebSocket，别放反。
  • 8 marks = 4 sublayers × 2 marks: for each sublayer write three things, "name + role + example".8 分 = 4 个子层 × 2 分：每个子层写"名字 + 作用 + 例子"三样。

ExamHow to write it in English

The communications network layer of the Core IoT Functional Stack connects the smart objects to external systems and is divided into four sublayers:

1. Access network sublayer: the last mile of the IoT network, typically wireless technologies such as IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g and LoRa. Technologies are classified by range (PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN, WAN), and each technology supports particular topologies (e.g. star or mesh).

2. Gateways and backhaul sublayer: smart objects in a given area are organised around a common gateway, which performs the inter-medium communication and forwards the collected data over a longer-range backhaul medium (e.g. cellular or fibre) to a headend central station. The objects may be static or mobile within a limited area, while the gateway is usually static.

3. Network transport sublayer: open, standards-based network and transport protocols, mainly IP with UDP or TCP, connect the variety of devices and media. They must be scalable to thousands or millions of sensors and secure. IP can run over low-power, low-bandwidth and lossy networks; TCP lets the network control reliable delivery, while UDP leaves the control to the application.

4. IoT network management sublayer: application protocols that allow the headend applications to exchange data with the sensors, e.g. HTTP over TCP (the sensor acts as a client of the IoT application) and WebSocket, a lightweight web-derived protocol that provides a simple bidirectional connection in low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth and high-loss environments.

In one line: access network (last-mile wireless: 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa) → gateways and backhaul (area aggregation, long-range link back to the centre) → network transport (IP, UDP/TCP) → network management (HTTP, WebSocket).一句话：接入网（最后一公里无线：802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa）→ 网关与回传（区域汇聚、长距离送回中心）→ 网络传输（IP、UDP/TCP）→ 网络管理（HTTP、WebSocket）。

Past final exam
2025-26 S1Q4(b)(c)17 marks
Topics: five challenges of IoT · key features of fog computing考点：IoT 的五个难点 · 雾计算的关键特征
Original question (verbatim)

(b) The Internet of Things (IoT) is the technique that connects all unconnected objects. Discuss five of the potential difficulties and briefly describe each of them in the context of the development of IoT.

(10 Marks)

(c) An outstanding technique that processes data generated by IoT sensors is fog computing. Discuss the key features of fog computing.

(7 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
(b) Challenges ①–③ (notes Part B p.82):
① Scalability: IoT devices can number in the millions, and how the whole system supports so many devices is the key question; at the network layer, IPv6 can give addresses to a huge number of devices (there are not enough IPv4 addresses).
② Security: the more "things" are connected, the larger the attack surface; once a device is compromised, its connectivity becomes a stepping stone for attacking other devices and systems.
③ Privacy: there are more and more sensors, and the collected data often relates to specific individuals and their activities and may contain sensitive information and credentials; how the data is protected, whether it is shared and with whom are all key questions.(b) 难点 ①–③（讲义 Part B p.82）：
① 可扩展性（Scalability）：IoT 设备可达数百万个，整个系统如何支撑这么多设备是关键问题；网络层可用 IPv6 为海量设备分配地址（IPv4 地址不够用）。
② 安全（Security）：联网的“物”越多，攻击面越大；一台设备被攻破后，它的连通性反而成为攻击其他设备和系统的跳板。
③ 隐私（Privacy）：传感器越来越多，采集的数据往往与具体个人及其活动相关，可能包含敏感信息和凭证；数据如何保护、是否共享、与谁共享都是关键问题。
2
(b) Challenges ④–⑤ (p.83):
④ Big data and analytics: huge numbers of sensors generate a flood of data, and only efficient processing turns it into useful information; the difficulty is processing large volumes of data from different sources and in different formats in time.
⑤ Interoperability: many protocols and architectures compete for the market and for standards, some proprietary and some open, so different devices / networks have difficulty working together; new IoT standards help, but in practice many protocols and implementations still coexist.(b) 难点 ④–⑤（p.83）：
④ 大数据与分析（Big data and analytics）：海量传感器产生数据洪流，只有高效处理才能得到有价值的信息；难点在于要及时处理来自不同来源、不同格式的大量数据。
⑤ 互操作性（Interoperability）：各种协议和架构在争夺市场和标准，有的私有、有的开放，不同设备 / 网络难以互通；新的 IoT 标准能缓解，但实际中仍并存多种协议和实现。
3
(c) What fog computing is (p.106): data management and processing are moved as far as possible to the edge of the IP network, close to the sensors; any device with computing, storage and network connectivity can act as a fog node, which in effect adds a "fog layer" to the traditional IT computing model. Why it is needed: IoT generates huge volumes of data, and sending all of it to the cloud causes high latency and congestion in the core network.(c) 雾计算是什么（p.106）：把数据管理和处理尽量放到 IP 网络的边缘、靠近传感器的地方；任何有计算、存储和网络连接能力的设备都可以做雾节点，相当于在传统 IT 计算模型里多出一层“雾层”（fog layer）。为什么需要：IoT 数据量巨大，全部送到云端会带来高时延和核心网拥塞。
4
(c) Key characteristics (p.109):
• Contextual location awareness and low latency: fog nodes do distributed computing as close to the IoT endpoints as possible, so data does not have to travel to the cloud and the response is fast;
• Geographic distribution: the services and applications served by fog nodes need wide, distributed deployment;
• Deployment near large numbers of IoT endpoints: one fog node usually manages many endpoints;
• Wireless communication between fog nodes and endpoints: to connect large numbers of endpoints, wireless access is the easiest way to scale up;
• Use for real-time interactions: data is pre-processed at the fog node, so upper-layer applications only need to batch-process a subset of the data.(c) 关键特征（p.109）：
• 上下文位置感知与低时延：雾节点尽可能靠近 IoT 终端做分布式计算，数据不必绕到云端，反应快；
• 地理分布：雾节点服务的业务和应用需要广泛的分布式部署；
• 部署在大量 IoT 终端附近：一个雾节点通常管理很多终端；
• 雾节点与终端之间用无线通信：要连接大量终端，无线接入最容易实现大规模扩展；
• 用于实时交互：在雾节点预处理数据，上层应用只需对数据子集做批处理。
5
(c) Benefits (p.106, p.108): analysing data close to its source reduces latency, offloads a large amount of traffic from the core network and keeps sensitive data inside the local network; a fog node knows the context of the sensors it manages, so it can respond to events faster than the cloud, forming a distributed edge control loop (real-time monitoring, control and analytics without waiting for the cloud), and it reduces the amount of data that has to be uploaded.(c) 带来的好处（p.106、p.108）：就近分析数据可以降低时延、卸载核心网的大量流量、让敏感数据留在本地网络；雾节点了解所管理传感器的上下文，能比云端更快地响应事件，形成分布式边缘控制回路（实时监测、控制和分析，不用等云端），并减少需要上传的数据量。
(b) Scalability, security, privacy, big data and analytics, interoperability (c) low latency/location awareness, geographic distribution, close to endpoints, wireless access, real-time interaction(b) 可扩展性、安全、隐私、大数据分析、互操作性 (c) 低时延/位置感知、地理分布、靠近终端、无线接入、实时交互
◆ Key points
What it tests
Five challenges of IoT; key features of fog computing (Part B p.82–83, p.109).IoT 的五个难点；雾计算的关键特征（Part B p.82–83、p.109）。
Five challenges
Scalability (millions of devices, IPv6), security (large attack surface, a device can become a stepping stone), privacy (data tied to individuals), big data and analytics (many heterogeneous sources, must be processed in time), interoperability (many competing protocols and standards).可扩展性（数百万设备，IPv6）、安全（攻击面大，可做跳板）、隐私（数据与个人相关）、大数据与分析（多源异构、要及时处理）、互操作性（协议标准林立）。
Fog computing features
Location awareness and low latency; geographic distribution; deployment near many endpoints; wireless links to endpoints; aimed at real-time interaction (fog nodes pre-process, upper layers handle only a subset of the data).位置感知、低时延；地理分布；部署在大量终端附近；与终端无线连接；面向实时交互（雾节点预处理，上层只处理数据子集）。

Challenges: scale, security, privacy, data, interworking.难点：规模、安全、隐私、数据、互通。
Links
2023-24 Q4(b) asks "why fog computing is needed"; memorise it together with these features.2023-24 Q4(b) 问"为什么需要雾计算"，可以和这里的特征对照着背。
Concept + Step by step: five IoT challenges and features of fog computing

ConceptWhy IoT is hard

The IoT (Internet of Things) connects "things" that were never networked before (sensors, actuators, home appliances, cars …). Compared with the traditional Internet, its devices are extremely numerous, very weak (battery-powered, low computing power) and highly diverse, and the data they produce is both huge and sensitive. Part B p.82–83 of the notes groups the resulting obstacles into five: scalability, security, privacy, big data and analytics, interoperability.物联网（IoT，Internet of Things）要把原来不联网的"物"（传感器、执行器、家电、车……）都连起来。和传统互联网相比，它的设备数量极多、能力很弱（电池、低算力）、种类繁杂、产生的数据又多又敏感。讲义 Part B p.82–83 把由此带来的障碍归纳为五个：可扩展性、安全、隐私、大数据与分析、互操作性。

Step by step(b) The five challenges one by one (10 marks, 2 each: name + one or two sentences of explanation)

  1. Scalability: an IoT deployment may reach millions of devices; the key issue is how the whole system (addressing, access, management) can support so many devices. At the network layer, IPv6 can provide addresses for this huge number of devices.可扩展性（Scalability）：IoT 规模可能达到数百万台设备，整个系统（寻址、接入、管理）如何支撑这么多设备是关键问题。网络层可以用 IPv6 给海量设备分配地址。
  2. Security: the more "things" are connected, the larger the attack surface. Once a device is hacked, its connectivity itself becomes a threat: a compromised device can be a stepping stone for attacks on other devices and systems. Many devices have little computing power and cannot run complex security protocols.安全（Security）：联网的"物"越多，被攻击的面越大。一个设备被黑以后，它的连接能力本身就是威胁：被攻破的设备可以成为攻击其他设备和系统的跳板。很多设备算力弱，难以运行复杂的安全协议。
  3. Privacy: as sensors multiply, most of the data they collect relates to specific people and their activities and may contain sensitive information and credentials. How the data is protected, whether it is shared and with whom are the key questions.隐私（Privacy）：传感器越来越多，采集的数据大多和具体的人及其活动有关，可能包含敏感信息和凭证。数据如何保护、是否共享、和谁共享，是关键问题。
  4. Big data and analytics: large numbers of sensors produce a flood of data. Data is useful only if it is processed efficiently; the difficulty is processing huge volumes of data from different sources and in different formats in time.大数据与分析（Big data and analytics）：大量传感器会产生数据洪流。数据只有被高效处理才能提供关键信息；难点在于要及时处理来自不同来源、不同格式的海量数据。
  5. Interoperability: many protocols and architectures compete for market share and standard status; some are based on proprietary components, others are open. New IoT standards help, but real networks still contain many coexisting protocols and implementations, and devices from different vendors find it hard to interwork.互操作性（Interoperability）：各种协议和架构在争夺市场份额和标准地位，有的基于私有组件，有的是开放的。新的 IoT 标准能缓解，但实际网络里仍有多种协议和实现并存，不同厂家的设备难以互通。

Memory hook: scale, security, privacy, data, interworking (Scalability, Security, Privacy, Big data, Interoperability).记忆：规模、安全、隐私、数据、互通（Scalability, Security, Privacy, Big data, Interoperability）。

ConceptWhy fog computing is needed

If all data is uploaded to the cloud for processing, you run into these problems (p.105): last-mile bandwidth is very limited; latency is large, so there is no real-time response; the gateways' backhaul links (3G/LTE or even satellite) are unreliable; the volume of data to backhaul is too large; and as data keeps growing, real-time analysis becomes almost impossible. The solution is to distribute data management as close to the network edge as possible: this is fog computing (p.106). Any device with computing, storage and network connectivity can act as a fog node.如果所有数据都上传到云端处理，会遇到（p.105）：最后一公里带宽很有限；时延很大，做不到实时响应；网关的回传链路（3G/LTE 甚至卫星）不可靠；回传的数据量太大；数据越来越多，实时分析几乎不可能。解决办法是把数据管理分散到尽量靠近网络边缘的地方，这就是雾计算（fog computing）（p.106）。任何有计算、存储和网络连接能力的设备都可以做雾节点（fog node）。

Step by step(c) Key features of fog computing (7 marks)

The five features on notes p.109 (one sentence of explanation each):讲义 p.109 的五个特征（每个写一句解释）：

  1. Contextual location awareness and low latency: fog nodes sit as close as possible to the IoT endpoints and do distributed computing locally; being geographically close, a fog node knows the context of the sensors it manages and can react faster to events in the network (p.108).上下文位置感知和低时延（contextual location awareness and low latency）：雾节点尽可能靠近 IoT 终端，就近做分布式计算；因为地理上靠近，它了解自己管理的传感器的上下文，能更快地对网络里的事件做出反应（p.108）。
  2. Geographic distribution: the services and applications served by fog nodes need widely distributed deployment.地理分布（geographic distribution）：雾节点服务的业务和应用需要大范围分布式部署。
  3. Deployment near IoT endpoints: fog nodes are usually deployed where there are many IoT endpoints.部署在 IoT 终端附近（deployment near IoT endpoints）：雾节点通常部署在有大量 IoT 终端的地方。
  4. Wireless communication between fog nodes and endpoints: one fog node must connect many endpoints, and wireless access is the simplest way to scale to large numbers.雾节点和终端之间用无线通信：一个雾节点要连接大量终端，无线接入是实现大规模可扩展的最简单方式。
  5. Use for real-time interactions: data is preprocessed at the fog node, so upper-layer applications only need to batch-process a subset of the data.用于实时交互（real-time interactions）：在雾节点先做预处理，上层应用只需要对数据的一个子集做批处理。

To get the full 7 marks, add two or three benefits (p.106, p.108): lower latency; less traffic on the core network (no need to send GBs of data upstream); sensitive data stays in the local network; distributed edge control loops allow real-time monitoring and control without waiting for a cloud server; less data overall (data reduction). The benefits the lecturer summarised in class are the same: distributed processing is fast because it does not wait for a central server, data is reduced before upload, processing is real-time, and fog nodes connect to endpoints wirelessly.为了拿满 7 分，再写两三条好处（p.106、p.108）：降低时延；减轻核心网的流量（不用把 GB 级数据都传上去）；敏感数据留在本地网络；提供分布式的边缘控制回路，不用等云端服务器就能实时监控和控制；整体上减少数据量（data reduction）。老师课上总结的好处也是这几条：分布式处理不用等中心服务器所以快、上传前先精简数据、能实时处理、雾节点和终端无线连接。

PitfallsCommon ways to lose marks

  • (b) Listing the five names without explanation: the question says "briefly describe each", so each needs one or two sentences.(b) 只列五个名词不解释：题目要求 "briefly describe each"，每个要有一两句。
  • (b) Writing about IoT applications or advantages instead: that does not answer the question.(b) 写成 IoT 的应用或优点，答非所问。
  • (c) Saying fog computing "replaces cloud computing": notes p.111 say edge and fog are only the first stage of processing and do not replace the cloud.(c) 把雾计算说成"取代云计算"：讲义 p.111 说边缘和雾只是第一道处理，不取代云。

ExamHow to write it in English

(b) Five potential difficulties in the development of IoT:

1. Scalability: IoT may grow to include millions of devices. How the overall system (addressing, access and management) can support such a huge number of devices is a critical issue; IPv6 can provide enough addresses at the network layer.

2. Security: as more "things" are connected with other things and people, the threat surface is greatly expanded. If a device is hacked, its connectivity becomes a major concern, because a compromised device can serve as a launching point to attack other devices and systems.

3. Privacy: much of the data gathered by sensors is specific to individuals and their activities and may contain sensitive information and credentials. How the data are protected, and whether and with whom they are shared, is a critical issue.

4. Big data and analytics: the large number of sensors produces a deluge of data. The data provide useful insights only if they are processed efficiently; the challenge is to evaluate massive amounts of data arriving from different sources in various forms in a timely manner.

5. Interoperability: many protocols and architectures, some proprietary and some open, are competing for market share and standardisation. Devices and networks using different protocols and implementations cannot easily work together.

(c) Fog computing distributes data processing to fog nodes at the edge of the network, close to where IoT data are generated. Its key features are:

1. Contextual location awareness and low latency: the fog node sits as close to the IoT endpoints as possible, so it knows the context of the sensors it manages and can react to events much faster than a remote cloud.

2. Geographic distribution: the services and applications served by fog nodes require widely distributed deployments.

3. Deployment near IoT endpoints: fog nodes are typically deployed where there is a large number of IoT endpoints.

4. Wireless communication between the fog node and the IoT endpoints: since a fog node must handle many endpoints, wireless access is the easiest way to achieve large scalability.

5. Use for real-time interactions: data are pre-processed at the fog nodes, so upper-layer applications only need to perform batch processing on a subset of the data.

As a result, fog computing reduces latency, offloads traffic from the core network and the backhaul, keeps sensitive data inside the local network, reduces the amount of data to be sent, and provides a distributed edge control loop for real-time monitoring and control.

In one line: the five IoT challenges are scalability, security, privacy, big data and interoperability; fog computing moves processing to fog nodes close to the endpoints, and its features are low latency/location awareness, geographic distribution, deployment near endpoints, wireless access and real-time interaction.一句话：IoT 五难是规模、安全、隐私、大数据、互通；雾计算把处理放到靠近终端的雾节点，特征是低时延/位置感知、地理分布、靠近终端、无线接入、实时交互。

2025-26 S2Q4(d)8 marks
Topics: the four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer (same as 2024-25 Q4(b))考点：IoT 通信网络层的四个子层（同 2024-25 Q4(b)）
Original question (verbatim)

(d) In the core Internet of Things (IoT) functional stack, the communication network layer is structured with four sublayers. Describe the features of each of the sublayers.

(8 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
Same question as 2024-25 Q4(b). ① Access network sublayer: the "last mile" of the IoT network, which connects the smart objects to the network, usually with wireless technologies such as IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa (notes Part B p.89). Why there are so many: the choice depends on the range (PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN, MAN, WAN), the number of objects in a collection cell, cost and power consumption (p.95–96); the topology can be point-to-point or point-to-multipoint (star, clustered star, mesh) (p.96–97).和 2024-25 Q4(b) 是同一道题。① 接入网子层（access network sublayer）：IoT 网络的"最后一公里"，把智能物体接进网络，通常是无线技术，如 IEEE 802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa（讲义 Part B p.89）。为什么有这么多种：选哪种取决于通信距离（PAN、HAN、NAN、FAN、LAN、MAN、WAN）、一个采集小区里的物体数量、成本和功耗（p.95–96）；拓扑可以是点到点，或点到多点（星形、簇星、网状）（p.96–97）。
2
② Gateways and backhaul sublayer: several smart objects in an area are aggregated at a common gateway, which then forwards the collected data over a longer-range medium to the headend (central station) (p.89, p.98). Reason: the objects have a short range and low power and cannot connect directly to a distant centre, so a gateway is needed to convert between different media. The objects can be static or move within a small area; the gateway is usually fixed.② 网关与回传子层（gateways and backhaul sublayer）：把一个区域内的多个智能物体汇聚到一个公共网关，网关再通过更长距离的介质把采集到的数据转发到头端中心站（headend）（p.89、p.98）。原因：物体射程短、功耗低，不能直接连到远处的中心，需要网关做不同介质之间的转换。物体可以静止或在小范围内移动，网关通常固定。
3
③ Network transport sublayer: network- and transport-layer protocols (IP, UDP/TCP) connect all kinds of devices over all kinds of media (p.90, p.98–99). The protocols must be open, standardised, scalable to thousands of sensors, and secure. IP meets these requirements: it can be embedded in all kinds of objects and run over low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss networks. With TCP the network guarantees reliable delivery; UDP leaves control to the application.③ 网络传输子层（network transport sublayer）：用网络层和传输层协议（IP，UDP/TCP）把各种设备、各种介质连起来（p.90、p.98–99）。要求协议开放、标准化，能扩展到成千上万个传感器，并且安全。IP 满足这些要求，能嵌入各种物体、跑在低功耗、低带宽、高丢包的网络上；TCP 由网络保证可靠交付，UDP 把控制交给应用。
4
④ IoT network management sublayer: application-layer protocols that let headend applications exchange data with the sensors (smart objects) (p.90, p.99). Examples: HTTP over TCP, with the sensor acting as a client that connects to the IoT application; WebSocket, a lightweight two-way protocol suited to low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth, high-loss environments.④ IoT 网络管理子层（IoT network management sublayer）：应用层协议，让头端应用和传感器（智能物体）交换数据（p.90、p.99）。例：基于 TCP 的 HTTP，传感器作为客户端连到 IoT 应用；WebSocket 是轻量的双向协议，适合低内存、低功耗、低带宽、高丢包的环境。
Access network / Gateways & backhaul / Network transport / IoT network management
◆ Key points
What it tests
The four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer (same as 2024-25 Q4(b)).IoT 通信网络层的四个子层（与 2024-25 Q4(b) 相同）。
Answer points
Access network → gateways and backhaul → network transport (IP, UDP/TCP) → IoT network management (HTTP, WebSocket). For each sublayer, write one sentence on its role plus one example.接入网 → 网关与回传 → 网络传输（IP、UDP/TCP）→ IoT 网络管理（HTTP、WebSocket）。每个子层写一句作用加一个例子。
Memory aid
"Access → aggregate and backhaul → transport (IP) → management (application protocols)"."接入 → 汇聚回传 → 传输（IP）→ 管理（应用协议）"。
Tip
This question has come up twice in four years; you must memorise it.同一道题四年里考了两次，属于必背内容。
Concept + Step by step: the four sublayers of the IoT communications network layer

ConceptThe IoT core functional stack

The notes use Cisco's simplified framework to describe the IoT core functional stack (Part B p.89–90); the lecturer said this framework is the easiest to understand. It has three layers:讲义用 Cisco 的简化框架描述 IoT 的核心功能栈（Part B p.89–90），老师说这个框架最好理解。它有三层：

  • Layer 1, the "things" layer (sensors and actuators): physical devices must fit the constraints of the deployment environment while still providing the required information.第 1 层"物"层（things：传感器和执行器）：物理设备要适应部署环境的限制，同时提供所需的信息。
  • Layer 2, the communications network layer: when smart objects are not self-contained, they must communicate with outside systems, usually wirelessly. This is the layer the question asks about, and it is split into four sublayers.第 2 层通信网络层（communications network layer）：智能物体不能自给自足时，要和外部系统通信，通常用无线技术。本题问的就是这一层，它分成四个子层。
  • Layer 3, the application and analytics layer: processes the collected data, controls the smart objects and makes intelligent decisions.第 3 层应用与分析层：处理采集到的数据，控制智能物体、做智能决策。

Remember the four sublayers by the direction of data flow: "access → aggregation and backhaul → transport (IP) → management (application protocols)": data first enters wirelessly from the objects, is aggregated at gateways and backhauled, is carried through the network with IP/TCP/UDP, and is finally exchanged with headend applications by application protocols.四个子层可以按数据的走向记："接入 → 汇聚回传 → 传输（IP）→ 管理（应用协议）"：数据先从物体无线接入，在网关汇聚后回传，用 IP/TCP/UDP 在网络里传输，最后由应用协议和头端应用交换。

Step by stepThe four sublayers one by one (8 marks, 2 each: name + features/examples)

  1. Access network sublayer (p.89, p.93–97): the "last mile" of the IoT network, usually wireless, e.g. IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa. The choice of technology depends on range (by range: PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN, MAN, WAN), the number of objects and the throughput in one collection unit, and cost and power consumption; the topology can be point-to-point or point-to-multipoint (star, clustered star, mesh).接入网子层（access network sublayer）（p.89、p.93–97）：IoT 网络的"最后一公里"，通常是无线技术，如 IEEE 802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa。选什么技术取决于通信距离（按范围分 PAN、HAN、NAN、FAN、LAN、MAN、WAN）、一个采集单元里的物体数量和吞吐量、成本和功耗；拓扑可以是点对点，也可以是点对多点（星形、簇状星形、mesh）。
  2. Gateways and backhaul network sublayer (p.89, p.98): groups the smart objects in an area onto a common gateway; the gateway handles communication between different media and forwards the collected information over a longer-range medium (e.g. cellular, fibre) to a central headend station. Objects may be static or move within a small area; the gateway is usually fixed.网关与回传子层（gateways and backhaul network sublayer）（p.89、p.98）：把一片区域里的多个智能物体组织到一个公共网关上，网关负责不同介质之间的通信，用更长距离的介质（如蜂窝、光纤）把采集的信息转发到头端中心站。物体可以静止或在小范围内移动，网关通常是固定的。
  3. Network transport sublayer (p.90, p.98–99): successful communication needs network- and transport-layer protocols such as IP and UDP/TCP to support a variety of devices and media. The protocols must be open and standards-based, scale to thousands or even millions of sensors, and be secure. IP meets these requirements and also works on low-power, lossy, low-bandwidth networks; on top of IP, TCP lets the network control reliable delivery, while UDP leaves control to the application.网络传输子层（network transport sublayer）（p.90、p.98–99）：要实现成功的通信，必须有网络层和传输层协议，如 IP 和 UDP/TCP，以支持各种设备和介质。协议要开放、基于标准，能扩展到成千上万甚至数百万个传感器，并保证安全。IP 满足这些要求，也能用于低功耗、高丢包、低带宽的网络；在 IP 之上，用 TCP 由网络控制可靠交付，或用 UDP 把控制交给应用。
  4. IoT network management sublayer (p.90, p.99): additional application-layer protocols that let headend applications exchange data with the sensors. Examples: HTTP over TCP (the sensor acts as a client connecting to the IoT application), and WebSocket, a lightweight, Web-derived protocol suited to low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth, lossy environments, which provides a simple two-way connection between smart objects and external applications.IoT 网络管理子层（IoT network management sublayer）（p.90、p.99）：额外的应用层协议，让头端应用能和传感器交换数据。例如基于 TCP 的 HTTP（传感器作为客户端连接 IoT 应用），以及 WebSocket：一种轻量、源自 Web 的协议，适应低内存、低功耗、低带宽、高丢包的环境，在智能物体和外部应用之间提供简单的双向连接。

This question is the same as 2024-25 Q4(b); it has been tested twice in four years, so memorise it.这道题和 2024-25 Q4(b) 一样，四年里考了两次，属于必背内容。

PitfallsCommon ways to lose marks

  • Answering with the three layers (things, communications network, application and analytics) as if they were the four sublayers: the question asks for the four sublayers inside the communications network layer.把三层（物、通信网络、应用分析）当成四个子层来答：题目问的是通信网络层里面的四个子层。
  • Giving only the names without features, or no example for each sublayer (802.11ah/LoRa, IP/UDP/TCP, HTTP/WebSocket).只写名称不写特点，或者每个子层不举例子（802.11ah/LoRa、IP/UDP/TCP、HTTP/WebSocket）。
  • Muddled order: writing them as "access → gateway/backhaul → transport → management" is clearest.顺序乱：按"接入 → 网关回传 → 传输 → 管理"写最清楚。

ExamHow to write it in English

The communications network layer of the core IoT functional stack has four sublayers:

1. Access network sublayer: the last mile of the IoT network, typically made up of wireless technologies such as IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g and LoRa. The choice of technology depends on the communication range (PAN, HAN, NAN, FAN, LAN, MAN, WAN), the number of objects and throughput per collection cell, cost and power consumption. Topologies can be point-to-point or point-to-multipoint (star, clustered star, mesh).

2. Gateways and backhaul network sublayer: multiple smart objects in a given area are organised around a common gateway, which is in charge of the inter-medium communication and forwards the collected information through a longer-range medium (backhaul) to a headend central station. The smart objects may be static or mobile within a limited area, while the gateway is usually static.

3. Network transport sublayer: network and transport layer protocols such as IP and UDP/TCP are implemented to support the variety of devices and media. The protocol must be open and standards-based, scalable to thousands or millions of sensors, and secure. IP meets these requirements, even over low-power, lossy, low-bandwidth networks; TCP or UDP is chosen depending on whether the network or the application controls the delivery.

4. IoT network management sublayer: additional application protocols allow the headend applications to exchange data with the sensors, for example HTTP over TCP (the sensor acting as a client) and WebSocket, a lightweight web-derived protocol that provides a simple bidirectional connection in low-memory, low-power, low-bandwidth and high-loss environments.

In one line: the four sublayers of the communications network layer are access network (last-mile wireless: 802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa), gateways and backhaul (aggregate, then send over long range to the headend), network transport (IP + UDP/TCP; open, scalable, secure) and IoT network management (application protocols such as HTTP and WebSocket).一句话：通信网络层四子层是接入网（最后一公里无线：802.11ah、802.15.4g、LoRa）、网关与回传（汇聚后长距离送到中心）、网络传输（IP + UDP/TCP，开放、可扩展、安全）、IoT 网络管理（HTTP、WebSocket 等应用协议）。

Past final exam
2025-26 S2Q4(b)8 marks
Topics: the four types of handoff in MEO/LEO satellite systems考点：MEO/LEO 卫星系统的四种切换
Original question (verbatim)

(b) In a satellite system with Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) or Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, there could also be handovers in the system if the satellite acts as a base station. Briefly describe the 4 different types of handovers that can occur in this type of satellite system.

(8 Marks)

Show solution and key points (try it yourself first)
1
Background: MEO/LEO are not geosynchronous orbits, so the satellites move fast relative to the ground. When a satellite acts as the base station, handover is triggered not only by the user's movement but also by the satellite's own movement, so there are 4 types in total (notes Part C p.40).背景：MEO/LEO 不是同步轨道，卫星相对地面高速运动。卫星充当基站时，除了用户移动，卫星自己移动也会触发切换，所以共有 4 种（讲义 Part C p.40）。
2
① Intra-satellite handover: the user moves from one sector (spot beam) to another within the coverage area of the same satellite. Reason: a satellite covers the ground with several spot beams and each beam acts like a cell, so crossing beams is like crossing cells in a cellular network.① 星内切换（intra-satellite handover）：用户在同一颗卫星的覆盖区内，从一个扇区（点波束，spot beam）移到另一个扇区。原因：一颗卫星用多个点波束覆盖地面，每个波束相当于一个小区，跨波束就像蜂窝网里跨小区。
3
② Inter-satellite handover: the user moves from one satellite's coverage area into another's, or the satellite itself moves away and the connection must be handed to the next satellite. LEO orbits are low and move fast relative to the ground, so communication between two points usually has to pass the signal from one satellite to another (p.17); each satellite is visible to a user for only about 15–20 minutes, so this handover is very frequent. MEO orbits are higher, so there are far fewer handovers (p.39).② 星间切换（inter-satellite handover）：用户从一颗卫星的覆盖区移到另一颗卫星的覆盖区，或者卫星自己飞走了，连接要交给下一颗卫星。LEO 轨道低、相对地面运动快，两地之间的通信通常要把信号从一颗卫星交给另一颗（p.17）；每颗星对一个用户只可见约 15–20 分钟，所以这种切换很频繁；MEO 轨道高，切换少得多（p.39）。
4
③ Gateway handover: as the satellite moves, it leaves the ground gateway it is currently connected to, and the link between the satellite and the terrestrial network must switch to another gateway. Reason: gateways are fixed ground stations, while the satellite is moving.③ 网关切换（gateway handover）：卫星移动后离开了当前连接的地面网关（gateway），卫星与地面网络之间的链路要换到另一个网关。原因：网关是固定的地面站，卫星在动。
5
④ Inter-system handover: handover between the satellite system and a terrestrial cellular system, decided by signal strength and QoS; it is a vertical handover between different types of network. Example: when the user enters an area with terrestrial cellular coverage, the call switches from the satellite to the cellular network, and switches back to the satellite when the user leaves that coverage area.④ 系统间切换（inter-system handover）：在卫星系统和地面蜂窝系统之间切换，根据信号强度和 QoS 决定，属于不同类型网络之间的垂直切换（vertical handover）。例：用户进入有地面蜂窝覆盖的地区时从卫星切到蜂窝网，离开覆盖区时再切回卫星。
Intra-satellite, inter-satellite, gateway and inter-system (vertical) handoff星内、星间、网关、系统间（垂直）切换
◆ Key points
What it tests
The four types of handoff in MEO/LEO satellite systems (Part C p.40).MEO/LEO 卫星系统的四种切换（Part C p.40）。
Answer points
Intra-satellite handoff (between spot beams / sectors of the same satellite); inter-satellite handoff (change of satellite; each LEO satellite is visible for only 15–20 minutes, so it is very frequent); gateway handoff (the satellite leaves the current ground gateway); inter-system handoff (vertical handoff between satellite and terrestrial cellular).星内切换（同一颗卫星的不同点波束 / 扇区之间）；星间切换（换卫星，LEO 每颗只可见 15–20 分钟，很频繁）；网关切换（卫星离开当前地面网关）；系统间切换（卫星与地面蜂窝之间的垂直切换）。
Memory aid
From small to large: "beam → satellite → gateway → system".从小到大："波束 → 卫星 → 网关 → 系统"。
Common mistakes
Inter-satellite handoff is not only caused by the user moving; the satellite flying away also triggers it. Inter-system handoff is called "vertical handoff".星间切换不只是用户移动造成的，卫星自己飞走也会触发；系统间切换叫"垂直切换"。
Concept + Step by step: the four handovers in LEO/MEO satellite systems

ConceptWhy LEO/MEO satellite systems have handovers

A GEO (geostationary orbit) satellite is fixed relative to the ground, so a ground user always sees the same satellite. MEO (medium Earth orbit) and LEO (low Earth orbit) satellites move fast relative to the ground; a LEO satellite is visible from a given spot for only about 10–20 minutes. If the satellite itself acts as a base station (it carries base-station functions), handovers are caused not only by user movement but also by the satellite's own motion (Part C p.40). The notes list 4 types; remember them from smallest to largest scope: beam → satellite → gateway → system. The lecturer said the satellite part was covered only briefly, but this is exactly the question that has appeared in the final.GEO（地球静止轨道）卫星相对地面不动，地面用户一直看到同一颗卫星。MEO（中轨）和 LEO（低轨）卫星相对地面高速运动，一颗 LEO 卫星对某个地点只可见十几分钟。如果卫星本身充当基站（卫星上载有基站功能），那么除了用户移动，卫星自己的运动也会引起切换（Part C p.40）。讲义列出 4 种，按范围从小到大记：波束 → 卫星 → 网关 → 系统。老师说卫星这部分讲得少，但期末考过的就是这一题。

Step by stepThe four handovers one by one (8 marks, 2 each: name + cause/mechanism)

  1. Intra-satellite handover: a satellite uses multiple spot beams to divide its coverage into several sectors (like cells in a cellular system). When the user moves from one sector to another within the coverage of the same satellite, the call switches to another beam (new frequency/channel); the satellite stays the same.星内切换（intra-satellite handover）：一颗卫星用多个点波束把覆盖区分成多个扇区（类似蜂窝的小区）。用户在同一颗卫星的覆盖范围内从一个扇区移到另一个扇区时，换到另一个波束（换频率/信道），卫星不变。
  2. Inter-satellite handover: the user moves from one satellite's coverage to another's, or the satellite itself moves away, so the call must be handed to the next satellite. LEO satellites move fast and each is visible only briefly, so this handover is frequent.星间切换（inter-satellite handover）：用户从一颗卫星的覆盖区移到另一颗卫星的覆盖区，或者卫星自己飞走了，通话要转给下一颗卫星。LEO 卫星运动快、每颗可见时间短，这种切换很频繁。
  3. Gateway handover: the satellite reaches the terrestrial network through a ground gateway. When the satellite moves away from the gateway it is currently connected to, it must switch to another gateway (even if the user has not moved).网关切换（gateway handover）：卫星通过地面网关（gateway）接入地面网络。卫星移动后离开了当前连接的网关，就要换到另一个网关（即使用户没有动）。
  4. Inter-system handover: handover between the satellite system and a terrestrial cellular system. For example, when the user enters a city where the terrestrial cellular signal is better, the call switches from satellite to cellular, and vice versa. It is based on signal strength and QoS performance, and it is a vertical handover (between different types of network).系统间切换（inter-system handover）：在卫星系统和地面蜂窝系统之间的切换。例如用户进入城市、地面蜂窝信号更好时，从卫星切到蜂窝；反之亦然。依据是信号强度和 QoS 性能，它是一种垂直切换（vertical handover，不同类型网络之间）。

PitfallsCommon ways to lose marks

  • Writing only the four names: give the cause of each (user movement or satellite movement).只写四个名字：每个都要写起因（用户移动还是卫星移动）。
  • For inter-satellite handover, writing only "user movement" and missing "the satellite moves away", the cause specific to satellite systems.星间切换只写"用户移动"，漏了"卫星飞走"这个卫星系统特有的原因。
  • For inter-system handover, write "vertical handover" and "based on signal strength and QoS".系统间切换要写出"垂直切换"和"依据信号强度和 QoS"。

ExamHow to write it in English

In MEO/LEO systems the satellites move relative to the earth, so if a satellite acts as a base station, handovers are caused not only by the movement of the users but also by the movement of the satellites. Four types of handover can occur:

1. Intra-satellite handover: caused by the movement of a mobile user within the coverage of one satellite from one sector (spot beam) to another. The user is switched to another beam/channel of the same satellite.

2. Inter-satellite handover: caused by the movement of a user from the coverage of one satellite to that of another, or by the satellite moving away. The connection is handed over to the next satellite. This is frequent in LEO systems because each satellite is visible for only a short time.

3. Gateway handover: caused by the movement of the satellite away from the current ground gateway, so the satellite link has to be switched to another gateway, even if the user does not move.

4. Inter-system handover: a handover between the satellite system and a terrestrial cellular system, based on signal strength and QoS performance. This is a vertical handover between two different types of network.

In one line: intra-satellite (same satellite, new beam), inter-satellite (new satellite; the user moves or the satellite moves away), gateway (the satellite leaves the current gateway), inter-system (vertical handover between satellite and terrestrial cellular).一句话：星内（同一卫星换波束）、星间（换卫星，用户动或卫星飞走）、网关（卫星离开当前网关）、系统间（卫星与地面蜂窝之间的垂直切换）。
→ Back to the learning page: Part C Ch. 6 Satellite networks: how data is routed and how users are handed off→ 回到讲解：Part C 第六章 卫星网络：数据怎么路由，用户怎么切换

B·C random quiz (10 questions)

Concept + Step by step: how far a WLAN reaches

ConceptThree key numbers for a WLAN

A wireless LAN (WLAN) replaces the last segment of a wired LAN with a wireless link: terminals such as laptops have antennas and talk over the air to an access point (AP). Notes Part B p.6 gives three numbers: coverage is medium range, 50–500 m; each cell has only one physical channel, so all transmitters and receivers, uplink and downlink, share one frequency; data rates range from 1 Mbps to 54 Mbps.无线局域网（Wireless LAN, WLAN）就是把有线 LAN 的最后一段换成无线：笔记本等终端带天线，和接入点（Access Point, AP）之间走无线链路。讲义 Part B p.6 给了三个数：覆盖中等距离 50–500 m；每个小区只有一个物理信道，所有收发方、上行和下行共用一个频率；速率从 1 Mbps 到 54 Mbps。

Option by optionWhich network each range belongs to

  • A. 5–50 m: wrong. This is the scale of personal / home networks: a Bluetooth PAN covers a few metres, a ZigBee or BLE HAN a few tens of metres (p.95).A. 5–50 m：错。这是个人 / 家庭网络的尺度：蓝牙 PAN 几米，ZigBee、BLE 的 HAN 几十米（p.95）。
  • B. 50–500 m: correct, notes p.6 verbatim: "Radio coverage: medium 50-500 meters".
  • C. 0.5–5 km: wrong. This is the order of a metropolitan area network, MAN (a few km) (p.95).C. 0.5–5 km：错。这是城域网 MAN（几公里）的量级（p.95）。
  • D. 5–50 km: wrong. This is the order of a wide area network (WAN) or a cellular macrocell; Wi-Fi transmit power cannot reach that far.D. 5–50 km：错。这是广域网 WAN、蜂窝宏小区的量级，Wi-Fi 的发射功率到不了。

PitfallsThe notes give two different numbers

  • The IoT part, p.95, says LAN (IEEE 802.11) is "up to 100 m". When asked about WLAN coverage, answer 50–500 m from p.6; use the p.95 ranges only when classifying IoT networks by distance.IoT 部分 p.95 写 LAN（IEEE 802.11）"up to 100 m"。问 WLAN 覆盖按 p.6 答 50–500 m；只有在 IoT 按距离分类时才用 p.95 的分档。
In one line: choose B: a WLAN covers a medium range of 50–500 m, a cell shares one frequency, rates are 1–54 Mbps (p.6).一句话：选 B：WLAN 覆盖中等距离 50–500 m，一个小区共用一个频率，速率 1–54 Mbps（p.6）。
Concept + Step by step: BSS, ESS, AP, DS

ConceptThe four building blocks of the 802.11 architecture (p.10)

NameWhat it isAnalogy
BSS (Basic Service Set)A group of stations competing for the same wireless channel, i.e. one cell; it can be isolated or connect to the DS through an AP一群竞争同一无线信道的站点，就是一个小区；可以孤立，也可以经 AP 接到 DSA classroom
AP (access point)A device that acts as a bridge and performs the central coordination function一个设备，当网桥用，承担中心协调功能The teacher at the classroom door教室门口的老师

Option by option

  • A. IBSS: wrong. (Beyond the slides: this abbreviation does not appear in the notes.) IBSS = independent BSS, i.e. the "isolated" BSS mentioned on p.10: no DS, no AP, stations talk directly. It is exactly the opposite of "several BSSs interconnected through a DS".A. IBSS：错。（课外补充：讲义没出现这个缩写。）IBSS = 独立 BSS，就是 p.10 说的"孤立"BSS，不接 DS、没有 AP，站点直接对话，正好和"多个 BSS 经 DS 互联"相反。
  • B. ESS: correct, as defined on p.10.

  • D. DSSS: wrong. This is direct-sequence spread spectrum at the physical layer; its DS means direct sequence, not distribution system. It is a wording trap.D. DSSS：错。这是物理层的直接序列扩频，里面的 DS 是 direct sequence，不是 distribution system，是个字面陷阱。

Lecturer's emphasis: in the 802.11 family, remember a and b: b uses DSSS at 2.4 GHz, a uses OFDM at 5 GHz.老师课上强调：802.11 家族里要记住 a 和 b：b 在 2.4 GHz 用 DSSS，a 在 5 GHz 用 OFDM。

Option by option

  • A: wrong. "5 GHz, OFDM, 54 Mbps" are the parameters of a, attached to b.A：错。"5 GHz、OFDM、54 Mbps"是 a 的参数，被安到了 b 身上。
  • B: wrong. The reverse: b's "2.4 GHz, DSSS, 11 Mbps" is attached to a.B：错。反过来，把 b 的"2.4 GHz、DSSS、11 Mbps"安到了 a 身上。

Concept + Step by step: the four WLAN applications

ConceptWhy WLANs exist

A wired LAN is fast and stable, but needs cables: wiring a large space is expensive, digging trenches between two buildings is hard, and people on the move cannot carry a network cable. The four WLAN applications (notes Part B p.7–8) match exactly these four "cabling is awkward" situations. Memorise them in order of distance from near to far and from fixed to mobile: extension → cross-building → nomadic → ad hoc.有线 LAN 速度快、稳定，但要拉线：大空间布线贵，两栋楼之间不好挖沟，人走动时也没法带着网线。WLAN 的四类应用（讲义 Part B p.7–8）正好对应这四种"拉线不方便"的场景。记的时候按距离从近到远、从固定到移动排：扩展 → 楼间 → 游牧 → 自组。

Step by stepThe four points one by one

  1. LAN Extension: the wireless LAN is attached to a wired LAN on the same premises. The wired part is the backbone and connects servers and fixed workstations; the wireless part covers large open areas such as factory floors, stock exchange trading floors and warehouses. Why: these areas are large and their layout changes often, so cabling does not pay off.LAN 扩展（LAN Extension）：无线 LAN 接在同一场所的有线 LAN 上。有线部分做骨干，接服务器和固定工作站；无线部分覆盖大的开放空间，如厂房、证券交易大厅、仓库。为什么：这些地方面积大、布局常变，拉线不划算。
  2. Cross-Building Interconnect: a point-to-point wireless link connects the LANs of neighbouring buildings; the devices at each end are usually bridges or routers. Why: digging trenches and laying cable between buildings is costly.楼间互联（Cross-Building Interconnect）：用点对点无线链路把相邻建筑的 LAN 连起来，两头的设备通常是网桥或路由器。为什么：楼之间挖沟埋线成本高。
  3. Nomadic Access: within a medium-range area such as a campus, you carry a laptop around and stay online and transfer data while moving.游牧接入（Nomadic Access）：在校园这种中等距离范围内，带着笔记本边走边上网、传数据。
  4. Ad Hoc Networking: a temporary peer-to-peer network set up for an immediate need, with no AP; example: employees link their laptops into a temporary network during a meeting, and it breaks up when the meeting ends.自组网（Ad Hoc Networking）：为眼前的需要临时搭一个对等网络，没有 AP；例：员工开会时把笔记本连成临时网络，会开完就散。

Pitfalls

  • Cross-building interconnect is "point-to-point link + bridge/router", not ordinary user access; do not mix it up with nomadic access.楼间互联是"点对点链路 + 网桥/路由器"，不是普通用户接入，别和游牧接入混。
  • The question asks for "one example each", so every item needs an example; giving only the names loses marks.题目要"各举一个例子"，每条都要有例子，只写名称会丢分。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) LAN extension: a wireless LAN is linked into a wired LAN on the same premises. The wired backbone supports servers and stationary workstations, while the wireless part serves stations in large open areas, e.g. manufacturing plants, stock-exchange trading floors and warehouses.

(2) Cross-building interconnect: a point-to-point wireless link connects the LANs in nearby buildings; the connected devices are typically bridges or routers.

(3) Nomadic access: supports mobile computing within a medium distance, e.g. a student moving around the campus with a laptop.

(4) Ad hoc networking: a temporary peer-to-peer network set up to meet an immediate need, e.g. employees with laptops linking their computers for the duration of a meeting.

In one line: the four WLAN applications are LAN extension, cross-building interconnect, nomadic access and ad hoc networking, each with an example (p.7–8).一句话：WLAN 四类应用：LAN 扩展、楼间互联、游牧接入、自组网，每类配一个例子（p.7–8）。
Concept + Step by step: two-frame / four-frame exchange

ConceptWhy a frame exchange protocol is needed

A wireless channel has many bit errors and collisions, so sending a frame does not mean it was received. 802.11 uses a frame exchange protocol to ensure reliable delivery (p.16): the receiver checks the CRC (frame check sequence, FCS) and replies with an acknowledgement (ACK) only if there is no error; if the sender gets no ACK, it assumes failure and retransmits.无线信道误码多、还会冲突，发出去不等于收到了。802.11 用帧交换协议（frame exchange protocol）保证可靠传输（p.16）：接收方用 CRC（帧校验序列 FCS）检查，没错才回确认（ACK）；发送方等不到 ACK 就认为失败、重传。

Hidden node: A sends to B, and C is within B's range but outside A's range (p.48). C cannot hear A, thinks the channel is idle, transmits, and collides at B. ACKs alone cannot solve this: after a collision you can only retransmit, and the collisions keep repeating.隐藏节点（hidden node）：A 发给 B，C 在 B 的范围内、A 的范围外（p.48）。C 听不到 A，以为信道空，一发就在 B 处撞车。只靠 ACK 解决不了：撞了只能重传，还会反复撞。

Beyond the slides: wired Ethernet can listen while sending and stop as soon as it detects a collision (CSMA/CD); a wireless station's own signal is too strong while transmitting for it to hear others, so it can only "avoid first, confirm afterwards".课外补充：有线以太网可以边发边听、发现冲突就停（CSMA/CD）；无线发射时自己的信号太强，听不到别人，所以只能"先避让、后确认"。

Step by stepThe two procedures and NAV

Two-frame: source → DATA; destination checks CRC → ACK; no ACK received → retransmit
Four-frame: source → RTS; destination → CTS; source → DATA; destination → ACK两帧：源 → DATA；目的检查 CRC → ACK；没收到 ACK → 重传
四帧：源 → RTS；目的 → CTS；源 → DATA；目的 → ACK
  1. RTS (request to send) and CTS (clear to send) both carry a duration (how long the following data + ACK will take) (p.17).RTS（请求发送）和 CTS（允许发送）都带持续时间（后面的数据 + ACK 要占多久）（p.17）。
  2. Nearby nodes read this duration and set their own timer, the NAV (network allocation vector); they do not transmit until the NAV reaches zero.周围节点读到这个时长，设置自己的计时器 NAV（网络分配向量），在 NAV 归零前不发送。
  3. Key point: hidden node C cannot hear A's RTS, but it can hear B's CTS, so it also sets its NAV and stays quiet. This is exactly the sentence the lecturer stressed in class.关键：隐藏节点 C 听不到 A 的 RTS，但听得到 B 的 CTS，于是也设 NAV、闭嘴。老师课上强调的就是这一句。
  4. Cost: the overhead of two extra short frames, so the four-frame exchange buys reliability.代价：多了两个短帧的开销，所以四帧交换换来的是可靠性。

The lecturer said in class that you will not be asked to draw the RTS/CTS timeline; understanding the process is enough.老师课上说 RTS/CTS 的时间线不会让画，理解过程即可。

ExamHow to write it in English

Two-frame exchange: the source transmits a data frame; the destination checks the frame check sequence (CRC) and replies with an ACK if the frame is received correctly; if the source does not receive the ACK, it retransmits the frame.

Four-frame exchange: RTS → CTS → DATA → ACK. Both RTS and CTS carry the duration of the coming data/ACK transmission, so all surrounding nodes set their NAV and defer. A hidden node, which cannot hear the RTS from the source, can still hear the CTS from the destination and defers, so collisions at the destination are avoided.
