The four-frame exchange improves robustness and solves the hidden node problem.

In one line: two-frame = DATA + ACK; four-frame = RTS + CTS + DATA + ACK, where the CTS makes hidden nodes that cannot hear the sender also set their NAV and back off.一句话：两帧 = DATA + ACK；四帧 = RTS + CTS + DATA + ACK，靠 CTS 让听不到发送方的隐藏节点也设 NAV 避让。
Concept + Step by step: ordering SIFS, PIFS, DIFS

ConceptInterframe space = priority

The interframe space (IFS) is how long a station must still wait after the channel becomes idle before it may transmit (p.20). Everyone who sees the channel go idle has to wait, and whoever has the shortest wait gets the channel first, so the shorter the space, the higher the priority.帧间间隔（Interframe Space, IFS）是信道空闲后必须再等多久才能发（p.20）。大家看到信道空了都要等，谁要等的时间短，谁先抢到，所以间隔越短、优先级越高。

SpacingLengthUsed by
SIFS (Short IFS)ShortestImmediate responses such as ACK, CTS and poll responsesACK、CTS、轮询应答这类立即响应
PIFS (PCF IFS)MiddleAP sending polls in PCF, ahead of normal contentionPCF 里 AP 发轮询，优先于普通竞争
DIFS (DCF IFS)LongestMinimum wait before ordinary asynchronous data frames contend普通异步数据帧竞争前的最短等待

Option by option

  • A: wrong, the whole order is reversed; DIFS is the longest.A：错，整个顺序反了，DIFS 是最长的。
  • B: wrong, PIFS must be shorter than DIFS so that the AP can win over normal contention and start the CFP (p.29).B：错，PIFS 必须比 DIFS 短，AP 才能压过普通竞争开始 CFP（p.29）。
  • C: correct, SIFS < PIFS < DIFS (p.29 verbatim).
  • D: wrong, SIFS is the shortest, because the ACK must go out first.D：错，SIFS 是最短的，ACK 必须最先发出。

Memory hook: S-P-D: Short is shortest, Point is in the middle, Distributed is longest. Priority: ACK > time-bounded packets > non-time-bounded data (p.29). Beyond the slides: in the standard, PIFS = SIFS + 1 slot and DIFS = SIFS + 2 slots.记忆：S-P-D：Short 最短，Point 居中，Distributed 最长。优先级 ACK > 有时限分组 > 无时限数据（p.29）。课外补充：标准里 PIFS = SIFS + 1 个时隙，DIFS = SIFS + 2 个时隙。

In one line: choose C: SIFS < PIFS < DIFS; the shorter, the higher the priority.一句话：选 C：SIFS < PIFS < DIFS，越短越优先。
Concept + Step by step: how DCF and PCF relate

ConceptThe two sublayers of the 802.11 MAC (p.18)

The 802.11 MAC is called DFWMAC and has two layers: DCF (distributed coordination function) is the base; it contends with CSMA/CA and suits bursty data. PCF (point coordination function) is optional, coexists with DCF and is built on top of DCF; the AP polls stations and provides connection-oriented, contention-free, time-bounded service. The lecturer stressed in class that the key word for PCF is "contention-free".802.11 的 MAC 叫 DFWMAC，分两层：DCF（分布式协调功能）是基础，用 CSMA/CA 竞争，适合突发数据；PCF（点协调功能）是可选的，与 DCF 共存、建在 DCF 之上，由 AP 轮询，提供面向连接、无冲突、有时限的服务。老师课上强调 PCF 的关键词是"无竞争"（contention-free）。

Option by option(this question asks for the FALSE statement)

  • A: true statement. DCF uses CSMA/CA and suits asynchronous, bursty traffic.A：正确描述。DCF 用 CSMA/CA，适合异步、突发业务。
  • B: true statement. In PCF the AP polls; it is contention-free and time-bounded.B：正确描述。PCF 由 AP 轮询，无冲突、有时限。
  • C: false statement, so this is the answer. PCF cannot work on its own: superframe = CFP + CP, and in the CP everyone still contends with DCF (p.28); the AP also starts the CFP through DCF's interframe-space mechanism, seizing the channel with PIFS.C：错误描述，是答案。PCF 不能单独工作：超帧 = CFP + CP，CP 里大家还是用 DCF 竞争（p.28）；AP 开始 CFP 也是靠 DCF 的帧间间隔机制，用 PIFS 抢信道。
  • D: true statement, p.18 verbatim: "Optional, coexist with DCF and built on DCF".D：正确描述，p.18 原话 "Optional, coexist with DCF and built on DCF"。

Memory hook: DCF is the foundation and PCF is an extra floor built on it; without the foundation you cannot build the floor.记忆：DCF 是地基，PCF 是加盖的楼层，没有地基盖不了楼。

In one line: choose C: PCF is optional, built on top of DCF, and cannot work on its own.一句话：选 C：PCF 是可选的，建立在 DCF 之上，不能单独工作。
Concept + Step by step: mean binary exponential backoff

ConceptBinary exponential backoff (p.22)

A failed transmission (no ACK received) means the channel is congested. The idea of binary exponential backoff (BEB): each time a transmission fails, double the waiting range, so that stations spread out their retransmission times and collide less. The rules in the notes:站点发送失败（没收到 ACK）说明信道太挤。二进制指数退避（Binary Exponential Backoff, BEB）的思路：每失败一次，把等待的范围翻倍，让大家的重发时间散开，减少再次碰撞。讲义规则：

  • The backoff time is chosen uniformly at random between 0 and CW − 1 slots; CW is called the contention window.退避时间在 0 到 CW − 1 个时隙之间均匀随机选，CW 叫竞争窗口（contention window）。
  • On the 1st attempt CW = CWmin; CW doubles after each failure; once it reaches CWmax it stops growing.第 1 次尝试 CW = CWmin；每失败一次 CW 翻倍；到 CWmax 后不再增大。
  • The notes recommend CWmin = 32, CWmax = 256.

As a formula: on the k-th attempt CWk = min(CWmin × 2k−1, CWmax). For integers uniformly distributed from 0 to N, the mean = (0 + N) / 2, so the mean backoff = (CW − 1) / 2. The lecturer stressed in class that the DCF flowchart is important; binary exponential backoff is what handles heavy load.写成公式：第 k 次尝试 CWk = min(CWmin × 2k−1, CWmax)。0 到 N 的整数均匀分布，平均值 = (0 + N) / 2，所以平均退避 = (CW − 1) / 2。老师课上强调 DCF 流程图很重要，二进制指数退避就是用来应对重负载的。

Step by stepCount it step by step

  1. First convert "number of failures" into "attempt number": after 3 failures the station is preparing its 4th attempt, and CW has doubled 3 times.先把"失败次数"换成"第几次尝试"：失败 3 次后准备的是第 4 次尝试，CW 翻倍了 3 次。
  2. Work out CW attempt by attempt and compare with the cap:逐次算 CW，并和上限比较：
1st attempt: CW = 32
2nd attempt: CW = 32 × 2 = 64
3rd attempt: CW = 64 × 2 = 128
4th attempt: CW = 128 × 2 = 256 (= CWmax, just reaching the cap)
Possible values: 0, 1, …, 255, 256 in total
Mean = (0 + 255) / 2 = 127.5 slots第 1 次尝试：CW = 32
第 2 次尝试：CW = 32 × 2 = 64
第 3 次尝试：CW = 64 × 2 = 128
第 4 次尝试：CW = 128 × 2 = 256（= CWmax，刚好到顶）
可选值：0, 1, …, 255，共 256 个
平均 = (0 + 255) / 2 = 127.5 个时隙

Check: the mean should be slightly below CW / 2 = 128, because the largest value is 255, not 256; 127.5 is reasonable.验算：平均值应略小于 CW / 2 = 128，因为最大值是 255 不是 256；127.5 合理。

Pitfalls

  • The range is 0 to CW − 1, not 0 to CW; using (0 + 256)/2 = 128 is wrong.范围是 0 到 CW − 1，不是 0 到 CW；用 (0 + 256)/2 = 128 就错了。
  • The number of failures and the attempt number differ by 1. Here the cap is reached, so miscounting by one happens not to change the result; but with only 2 failures (3rd attempt) the correct answer is CW = 128, mean (0 + 127)/2 = 63.5, and miscounting would give 127.5.失败次数和尝试次数差 1。本题因为碰到上限，数错一次结果碰巧不变；但若只失败 2 次（第 3 次尝试），正确是 CW = 128、平均 (0 + 127)/2 = 63.5，数错就会得 127.5。
  • Beyond the slides: real 802.11b (DSSS) uses CWmin = 31, CWmax = 1023; in the exam use the notes' 32 / 256.课外补充：实际 802.11b（DSSS）用 CWmin = 31、CWmax = 1023；考试按讲义的 32 / 256 算。

ExamHow to write it in English

CW starts at CWmin = 32 and is doubled after each unsuccessful attempt, up to CWmax = 256. After 3 failures, the 4th attempt uses CW = 32 × 23 = 256 = CWmax. The backoff is uniformly chosen from 0 to CW − 1 = 255 slots, so the mean backoff = (0 + 255)/2 = 127.5 slots.

In one line: on the 4th attempt CW = 256, the backoff is uniform over 0–255, mean 127.5 slots.一句话：第 4 次尝试 CW = 256，退避在 0–255 均匀取，平均 127.5 个时隙。
Concept + Step by step: CW stops growing at the cap

ConceptCWmax is the ceiling

Notes p.22: "CW stops increase when it reaches its maximum value CWmax". The doubling rule only goes up to CWmax: on the k-th attempt CWk = min(32 × 2k−1, 256). Why cap it: if the window doubled without limit, a station that failed a few times would wait extremely long, which gives unacceptable delay and is also unfair.讲义 p.22："CW stops increase when it reaches its maximum value CWmax"。翻倍规则只到 CWmax 为止：第 k 次尝试 CWk = min(32 × 2k−1, 256)。为什么要封顶：窗口无限翻倍，一个站失败几次后就要等非常久，时延不可接受，也不公平。

Step by step

  1. In the previous question the 4th attempt already had CW = 256. Two more failures → 6th attempt.上题第 4 次尝试已是 CW = 256。又失败 2 次 → 第 6 次尝试。
  2. Without the cap the formula gives 1024; then apply the cap:按公式不封顶会算到 1024，再取上限：
Without cap: 32 × 25 = 1024
With cap: CW6 = min(1024, 256) = 256
Mean backoff is still (0 + 255) / 2 = 127.5 slots不封顶：32 × 25 = 1024
封顶：CW6 = min(1024, 256) = 256
平均退避仍是 (0 + 255) / 2 = 127.5 个时隙

Pitfalls

  • Writing 1024 or 512 directly means you forgot the cap.直接写 1024 或 512 就是忘了上限。
  • Beyond the slides: in the standard, CW is reset to CWmin after a successful transmission, and a frame is discarded once retransmissions exceed the retry limit; notes p.22 does not say this, so mention it only if the question asks.课外补充：标准里发送成功后 CW 重置回 CWmin，重传超过上限次数就丢弃该帧；讲义 p.22 没写，题目问到再提。

ExamHow to write it in English

CW is doubled after each failure but stops increasing at CWmax. For the 6th attempt, 32 × 25 = 1024 > 256, so CW = CWmax = 256.

In one line: CW is capped once it reaches CWmax = 256, so the 6th attempt still uses 256.一句话：CW 到 CWmax = 256 就封顶，第 6 次尝试仍是 256。
Concept + Step by step: what the three parties do in RTS/CTS

ConceptChannel reservation (p.24–25)

RTS/CTS works like "book the table, then serve the food": the sender books the channel with a short RTS frame, the receiver confirms with a CTS, and everyone nearby reads from these two frames how long the channel will be busy and stays out of the way. Two spacings are used: DIFS (long, the wait before normal contention) and SIFS (short, used between responses within the same exchange). Inside one exchange the gaps are only SIFS, while other stations must wait at least DIFS, so nobody can cut in halfway.RTS/CTS 就是"先订座、再上菜"：发送方先用短帧 RTS 订下信道，接收方用 CTS 确认，周围的人从这两个帧里读出要占用多久，自觉让开。用到两个间隔：DIFS（长，普通竞争前要等的）和 SIFS（短，同一次交换里的应答之间用）。同一次交换内部只隔 SIFS，别的站至少要等 DIFS，所以中途没人插得进来。

Step by stepIn time order

Sender: senses the channel idle for DIFS → sends RTS
Receiver: waits SIFS → replies CTS
Sender: receives CTS, waits SIFS → sends data
Receiver: after receiving the data, waits SIFS → replies ACK
Other stations: read the duration in RTS/CTS → set NAV → wait NAV + DIFS → back off, then contend again发送方：侦听到信道空闲 DIFS → 发 RTS
接收方：等 SIFS → 回 CTS
发送方：收到 CTS，等 SIFS → 发数据
接收方：收完数据，等 SIFS → 回 ACK
其他站：读 RTS/CTS 的持续时间 → 设 NAV → 等 NAV + DIFS → 退避后再竞争
  1. The sender first waits DIFS: to make sure the channel is really idle, and to let higher-priority frames (those using SIFS or PIFS) go first.发送方先等 DIFS：确认信道真的空了，且让高优先级的帧（用 SIFS、PIFS 的）先走。
  2. The receiver waits only SIFS before replying CTS and ACK: responses have the highest priority and must be sent as fast as possible.接收方只等 SIFS 就回 CTS、ACK：应答优先级最高，要最快回。
  3. Other stations use virtual carrier sensing: they read the duration field in the frame to set their NAV, defer for "NAV + DIFS", and then still go through a backoff (p.24 "Backoff after defer"), so that they do not all rush in at once.其他站点做虚拟载波侦听：读出帧里的 duration 字段设置 NAV，推迟"NAV + DIFS"，之后还要走一次退避（p.24 "Backoff after defer"），避免大家同时冲出来。

The lecturer said in class that you will not be asked to draw the timeline, but you must be able to write each party's actions in order.老师课上说时间线不会让画，但要能按顺序写出每一方的动作。

Pitfalls

  • The sender's initial wait is DIFS, not SIFS; only the responses in the middle use SIFS.发送方开头等的是 DIFS 不是 SIFS；中间的应答才用 SIFS。
  • Other stations defer for NAV + DIFS and then back off; do not leave out the backoff.其他站点推迟的是 NAV + DIFS，最后还有退避，别漏。

ExamHow to write it in English

Sender: senses the channel free for a DIFS interval, transmits an RTS to reserve the channel; once a CTS is received, waits for an SIFS and then sends the data packet.

Receiver: on receiving the RTS, waits for an SIFS and responds with a CTS; once the packet has been received, waits for an SIFS and responds with an ACK.

All other stations: listen to the channel, read the duration field and set their NAV, defer access for the NAV time plus DIFS, and then back off.

In one line: sender DIFS → RTS, receiver SIFS → CTS, sender SIFS → data, receiver SIFS → ACK; bystanders set NAV, wait NAV + DIFS, then back off.一句话：发送方 DIFS → RTS，接收方 SIFS → CTS，发送方 SIFS → 数据，接收方 SIFS → ACK；旁人设 NAV，等 NAV + DIFS 再退避。
Concept + Step by step: NAV and virtual carrier sensing

ConceptTwo ways to "listen" to the channel

Physical carrier sensing: actually measure whether there is a signal on the channel. Drawback: a hidden node cannot hear the sender, so it measures "idle". Virtual carrier sensing (p.23): every frame carries a duration field saying how long this transmission (including following fragments and the ACK) will take; nearby nodes use it to update their timer, the NAV (Network Allocation Vector). Before transmitting, a node checks its NAV: if it is not zero, it treats the channel as busy and waits for it to count down to zero.物理载波侦听：真的去测信道上有没有信号。缺点：隐藏节点听不到发送方，测出来是"空"。虚拟载波侦听（virtual carrier sense，p.23）：每个帧带一个持续时间（duration）字段，说明这次传输（含后续分片和 ACK）要占多久；附近节点据此更新自己的计时器 NAV（Network Allocation Vector）。要发送前先看 NAV：不为零就当信道忙，等它数到零。

Option by option

  • A. Physical carrier sensing: wrong. That measures RF energy; the NAV reads a number from the frame.A. 物理载波侦听：错。那是测射频能量，NAV 是读帧里的数字。
  • B. Virtual carrier sensing: correct, p.23 verbatim: "Collision Avoidance is achieved by a virtual carrier sense mechanism".B. 虚拟载波侦听：对，p.23 原话 "Collision Avoidance is achieved by a virtual carrier sense mechanism"。
  • C. Power control: wrong. The NAV does not change transmit power.C. 功率控制：错。NAV 不改发射功率。
  • D. Frequency-hopping synchronisation: wrong. Frequency hopping (FHSS) is a physical-layer matter and has nothing to do with the NAV.D. 跳频同步：错。跳频（FHSS）是物理层的事，和 NAV 无关。

Memory hook: physical sensing is "pricking up your ears"; virtual sensing is "reading the booking schedule others have posted". The lecturer said the fields to remember in the frame format are the address fields and the duration field, and the latter is exactly where the NAV comes from.记忆：物理侦听是"竖起耳朵听"，虚拟侦听是"看别人贴出的占用时间表"。老师说帧格式里要记的就是地址字段和 duration 字段，后者正是 NAV 的来源。

In one line: choose B: the NAV counts down using the duration field in the frame, which implements virtual carrier sensing.一句话：选 B：NAV 根据帧里的 duration 字段计时，实现虚拟载波侦听。
Concept + Step by step: PCF polling and the superframe

ConceptPCF is the AP calling the roll

In DCF everyone grabs the floor; in PCF (point coordination function) the AP acts as chairperson and calls on stations one by one, so it is contention-free and time-bounded (p.26). While polling, the AP holds the channel, all asynchronous traffic is locked out, and DCF is suspended.DCF 是大家抢着说，PCF（点协调功能）是 AP 当主持人、挨个点名，所以无冲突、有时限（p.26）。点名期间 AP 占住信道，异步业务全部锁住，DCF 暂停工作。

Superframe (p.28): the time between two DTIM beacons (Delivery Traffic Indication Message, which provide synchronisation and timing) = CFP (contention-free period, AP polls) + CP (contention period, everyone uses DCF). The CFP length varies with the traffic load, because stations send frames of different lengths.超帧（superframe，p.28）：两个 DTIM 信标（Delivery Traffic Indication Message，提供同步和定时）之间的时间 = CFP（无竞争期，AP 轮询）+ CP（竞争期，大家用 DCF）。CFP 的长度随业务量变，因为各站发的帧长不同。

Step by stepThe three parts one by one

  1. Polling process (p.27): the AP sends a CF-Poll to a node; when the AP itself has data, it piggybacks the data and the CF-Poll in one frame. The polled node replies with Data+CF-ACK (if it has data) or CF-ACK (if not). After finishing with this node, the AP polls the next one. When all nodes have been polled or the CFP time is up, the AP broadcasts CF-End to announce the end of the CFP.轮询过程（p.27）：AP 给某个节点发 CF-Poll；AP 自己有数据时，把数据和 CF-Poll 捎带（piggyback）在一帧里。被点到的节点回 Data+CF-ACK（有数据）或 CF-ACK（没数据）。和这个节点交换完，AP 点下一个。所有节点点完或 CFP 时间到，AP 广播 CF-End 宣布 CFP 结束。
  2. Superframe structure: CFP + CP, started by a DTIM beacon. The AP broadcasts the actual CFP duration in the beacon, and every node sets its NAV accordingly; at the end of the CFP all nodes reset their NAV to zero, and until the next DTIM everyone contends with DCF (p.29).超帧组成：CFP + CP，由 DTIM 信标开始。AP 在信标里广播实际 CFP 时长，各节点据此设 NAV；CFP 结束时所有节点把 NAV 清零，之后到下一个 DTIM 前都用 DCF 竞争（p.29）。
  3. Why the CFP cannot be interrupted by the CP: because SIFS < PIFS < DIFS. The AP seizes the channel with PIFS while ordinary stations must wait the longer DIFS, so the AP always gets it first; inside the CFP responses are separated only by SIFS, so ordinary stations cannot cut in. Priority: ACK > time-bounded packets > non-time-bounded data (p.29).为什么 CFP 不会被 CP 打断：因为 SIFS < PIFS < DIFS。AP 用 PIFS 抢信道，普通站点要等更长的 DIFS，AP 一定先拿到；CFP 内部的应答只隔 SIFS，普通站点插不进来。优先级：ACK > 有时限分组 > 无时限数据（p.29）。

Pitfalls

  • CF-End is broadcast by the AP, not sent by the last polled station.CF-End 是 AP 广播的，不是最后一个被轮询的站发的。
  • The reason for "not interrupted" must come down to the IFS lengths; writing only "PCF has higher priority" is not enough."不被打断"的原因要落到 IFS 长短上，只写"PCF 优先级高"不够。

ExamHow to write it in English

Polling is started by the AP sending a CF-Poll frame to a node; if the AP has pending data, it piggybacks the CF-Poll on a data frame. The polled node responds with Data+CF-ACK or CF-ACK. The AP then polls the next node in its list. When all nodes have been polled or the CFP duration has expired, the AP broadcasts a CF-End frame.

A superframe consists of a contention-free period (CFP), in which the AP polls the nodes, followed by a contention period (CP), in which nodes contend using DCF; it starts with a DTIM beacon.

A CFP cannot be interrupted by a CP because SIFS < PIFS < DIFS: the AP seizes the channel with PIFS, which is shorter than the DIFS used by contending stations, so the CFP has higher priority.

In one line: the AP sends CF-Polls to call on stations one by one and finally broadcasts CF-End; superframe = CFP + CP; PIFS is shorter than DIFS, so the CFP cannot be interrupted.一句话：AP 发 CF-Poll 挨个点名、最后广播 CF-End；超帧 = CFP + CP；PIFS 比 DIFS 短，所以 CFP 不会被打断。
Concept + Step by step: the foreshortened superframe

ConceptThe AP must seize the channel at the end of the CP (p.29)

The nominal superframe length is fixed by the DTIM beacon interval. At the end of the CP, the AP contends for the channel with PIFS: if the channel is idle, the AP gets it, the CP ends and a new CFP starts; if the channel is busy (a station's frame is still being sent), the AP can only wait until it becomes idle, so the CFP starts late and the superframe of the next cycle is shortened, which the notes call a "foreshortened superframe".超帧的标称长度由 DTIM 信标的间隔定好。CP 末尾，AP 用 PIFS 竞争信道：信道空闲，AP 拿到信道，CP 结束、新的 CFP 开始；信道正忙（某站的帧还没发完），AP 只能等它变空，于是 CFP 晚开始，下一周期的超帧被压短，讲义叫 "foreshortened superframe"。

Option by option

  • A: wrong. 802.11 has no mechanism for "interrupting others"; PIFS only lets the AP go first once the channel is idle, and a frame already being sent is allowed to finish.A：错。802.11 没有"打断别人"的机制，PIFS 只是让 AP 在信道空闲后先抢，正在发的帧要让它发完。
  • B: correct, notes verbatim: "resulting in a foreshortened superframe for the next cycle".
  • C: wrong. The notes say nothing about "cancelling the CFP"; it just starts a little later.C：错。讲义没有"取消 CFP"，只是晚一点开始。
  • D: wrong. The NAV is reset at the end of the CFP (p.29), which is unrelated to this situation.D：错。NAV 清零发生在 CFP 结束时（p.29），和这里的情况无关。

Memory hook: the bell rings but the previous speaker has not finished; the teacher has to wait for them before calling the roll, so the lesson is a bit shorter.记忆：上课铃响了，前一个人话还没说完，老师得等他说完再点名，这节课就短了一截。

In one line: choose B: the AP can only start the CFP once the channel is idle, so the next cycle's superframe is shortened.一句话：选 B：AP 等信道空闲才能开始 CFP，下一周期的超帧被缩短。
Concept + Step by step: scanning, authentication, association

ConceptThree steps for a new node to join a BSS (p.31–32)

  1. Scanning: first find an AP and obtain synchronisation information. Passive scanning: wait for the beacon frames sent by the AP; active scanning: send a Probe Request and wait for the AP's Probe Response.扫描（scanning）：先找到 AP、拿到同步信息。被动扫描：等 AP 发的信标帧（Beacon）；主动扫描：自己发 Probe Request，等 AP 回 Probe Response。
  2. Authentication: the AP and the node exchange information, and each proves it knows the agreed password.认证（authentication）：AP 和节点交换信息，双方证明自己知道约定的密码。
  3. Association: exchange capability information between the node and the BSS, and tell the distribution system (all APs) where the node now is. Data frames can be sent and received only after association.关联（association）：交换节点和 BSS 的能力信息，并告诉分布系统（所有 AP）这个节点现在在哪。关联完成后才能收发数据帧。

The lecturer specifically mentioned the authentication step in class and reminded everyone to always set a password; this was tested in 2025-26 S1 Q4(a).老师课上特别提到认证这一步，提醒大家一定要设密码；这一题 2025-26 S1 Q4(a) 考过。

Option by option

  • A: wrong. Before an AP has been found, who would you authenticate with?A：错。还没找到 AP，跟谁认证？
  • B: wrong. Authentication must come before association; you cannot register before your identity is confirmed.B：错。认证必须在关联之前，没确认身份不能登记。
  • C: correct.
  • D: wrong. Association is the last step.D：错。关联是最后一步。

Memory hook: find the door (scanning) → check ID (authentication) → register your address (association).记忆：找门（扫描）→ 验身份（认证）→ 登记住址（关联）。

ExamHow to write it in English

Scanning: the node gets synchronization information from the AP, either passively by waiting for a beacon frame, or actively by sending probe request frames and waiting for a probe response. Authentication: the AP and the node exchange information to prove that each side knows a given password. Association: they exchange information about the node and BSS capabilities, and the distribution system is informed of the node's current position. Only after association can the node transmit and receive data frames.

In one line: choose C: scanning → authentication → association; data can be sent and received only after association.一句话：选 C：扫描 → 认证 → 关联，关联完才能收发数据。
Concept + Step by step: the three types of MAC frame

ConceptMAC frames come in three types (p.33)

TypePurposeExample
Data framesCarry dataOrdinary data frames; the FCS at the end is a 32-bit CRC (p.34)普通数据帧，末尾 FCS 是 32 位 CRC（p.34）
Control framesReserve the channel, acknowledge receipt预约信道、确认收到RTS, CTS, ACK
Management framesAssociation / disassociation with the AP, timing synchronisation, security control与 AP 关联 / 解除关联、定时同步、安全控制Beacon, Probe, authentication, association信标、Probe、认证、关联

The Frame Control field in the frame format indicates which type the frame is (p.34).帧格式里的帧控制（Frame Control）字段标明这是哪一类（p.34）。

Option by option

  • A. Data frame: wrong, it only carries data.A. 数据帧：错，只负责传数据。
  • B. Control frame: wrong, it handles channel reservation and acknowledgement: "traffic control", not "paperwork".B. 控制帧：错，管的是信道预约和确认，是"交通指挥"不是"行政手续"。
  • C. Management frame: correct, the three items in the question are the three lines for management frames on p.33.C. 管理帧：对，题干三项就是 p.33 管理帧的三条原文。
  • D: wrong. Beacon frames handle synchronisation (p.31) and are themselves management frames, so "all frames other than beacons" makes no sense.D：错。信标帧负责同步（p.31），本身就属于管理帧，"信标以外的所有帧"说不通。

Memory hook: management frames = paperwork (joining, time sync, security); control frames = traffic control (RTS/CTS/ACK).记忆：管理帧 = 办手续（入网、对时、安全）；控制帧 = 指挥交通（RTS/CTS/ACK）。

In one line: choose C: association, synchronisation and security control are all jobs of management frames.一句话：选 C：关联、同步、安全控制都是管理帧的活。
Concept + Step by step: EDCA in 802.11e

Concept802.11e gives traffic priorities (p.39–40)

Original DCF treats all frames the same, so voice and video get no guarantees. 802.11e adds two modes: EDCA (enhanced distributed channel access) is DCF with priorities; HCCA is similar to PCF, with a hybrid coordinator (HC) scheduling contention-free transmission opportunities according to the load of each traffic class.原始 DCF 对所有帧一视同仁，语音、视频得不到保证。802.11e 加了两种模式：EDCA（增强分布式信道接入）是带优先级的 DCF；HCCA 类似 PCF，由混合协调器 HC 按各业务类的负载调度无竞争发送机会。

How EDCA works (notes verbatim: "eight traffic classes"): 8 traffic classes, each with its own queue inside the node and its own backoff parameters, plus an arbitration interframe space, AIFS (Arbitration IFS). The classes first contend inside the node for a "virtual channel", and the winning frame then contends for the real channel just as in the original DCF. A class with a short AIFS and a small contention window waits less and so has higher priority, the same idea as "the shorter the spacing, the higher the priority" in b6.EDCA 的做法（讲义原话 "eight traffic classes"）：8 个业务类，每类在节点内有自己的队列和独立的退避参数，再加一个仲裁帧间间隔 AIFS（Arbitration IFS）。各类先在节点内部竞争一个"虚拟信道"，胜出的帧再像原来的 DCF 一样竞争真正的信道。AIFS 短、竞争窗口小的类，等得少，就更优先，和 b6 里"间隔越短越优先"是同一个道理。

Option by option

  • A. 4, using different channels: wrong. The number does not match the notes; also all classes share the same channel and differ in their parameters, not in their channels.A. 4 个，靠不同信道：错。数量和讲义不符；而且各类共用同一个信道，靠的是参数不同，不是信道不同。
  • B. 8, using their own backoff parameters and AIFS: correct, per the notes.B. 8 个，靠各自的退避参数和 AIFS：对，按讲义。
  • C. 8, using AP polling: wrong. Polling is how HCCA (and PCF) work; EDCA is contention-based.C. 8 个，靠 AP 轮询：错。轮询是 HCCA（和 PCF）的做法，EDCA 是竞争式的。
  • D. 16, using QCI: wrong. QCI is the QoS class identifier of an LTE bearer (p.71), not a WLAN concept.D. 16 个，靠 QCI：错。QCI 是 LTE 承载的 QoS 标识（p.71），不是 WLAN 的。

Beyond the slidesThe standard actually has 4 access categories

The 802.11e standard has 8 user priorities (0–7), mapped to 4 access categories (ACs): background AC_BK, best effort AC_BE, video AC_VI, voice AC_VO, each AC with one queue and its own AIFS and CW. The notes say 8 traffic classes, so in the exam choose 8 as in the notes; in short answers also write "eight traffic classes" as in the notes.802.11e 标准中是 8 个用户优先级（0–7），映射成 4 个接入类别 AC：背景 AC_BK、尽力而为 AC_BE、视频 AC_VI、语音 AC_VO，每个 AC 一个队列、一套 AIFS 和 CW。讲义写的是 8 个业务类，考试按讲义选 8；简答题也照讲义写 "eight traffic classes"。

In one line: choose B: EDCA has 8 traffic classes (as the notes put it), each with its own queue, backoff parameters and AIFS.一句话：选 B：EDCA 有 8 个业务类（讲义说法），每类独立队列、独立退避参数和 AIFS。
Concept + Step by step: what a MANET is

ConceptA network without infrastructure

Mobile ad hoc network (MANET): a set of wireless mobile nodes that, where there is no infrastructure (no AP, no base station), freely and dynamically organise themselves into a temporary network of arbitrary shape (p.42). It is a peer-to-peer network: no fixed controller is needed; the controller is dynamically elected among the nodes or distributed over all nodes; the network is self-creating, self-organizing and self-administering (p.43).移动自组网（Mobile Ad Hoc Network, MANET）：一组无线移动节点，在没有基础设施（没有 AP、没有基站）的地方，自由、动态地自己组织成临时的、任意形状的网络（p.42）。它是对等（peer-to-peer）网络：不需要固定控制器，控制器由节点动态选举或分散在所有节点上；网络自建、自组织、自管理（self-creating, self-organizing, self-administering，p.43）。

WLAN with APMANET
InfrastructureAP + distribution systemNone
ctrlCentralised coordination by the APDynamically elected or distributed动态选举或分布式
RetransmitEverything goes through the AP, single hop to the AP都经过 AP，单跳到 APNodes relay for each other, multi-hop possible节点互相转发，可多跳

Step by stepPoints to include in your answer

  1. Definition: write the three key phrases "no infrastructure, self-organising, temporary topology".定义：写出"无基础设施、自组织、临时拓扑"三个关键词。
  2. Main difference: every node must be able to act as a router on demand (p.45). When there is no direct wireless channel between A and C, intermediate node B relays, which is multi-hop. The chosen path must be loop free to count as a route.最大区别：每个节点都必须能按需当路由器（p.45）。A 和 C 之间没有直接无线信道时，由中间节点 B 中继，这就是多跳（multi-hop）。选的路径必须无环（loop free），才叫路由。
  3. You can add: 802.11 is simple, suits single-hop ad hoc networks, and can also build multi-hop networks covering several square kilometres; Bluetooth can form body / personal area networks with a radius of about 10 m (p.43).可以补一句：802.11 很简单，适合做单跳自组网，也能搭几平方公里的多跳网；蓝牙可以组半径约 10 m 的体域网 / 个域网（p.43）。

Pitfalls

  • Answering only "no AP" is not enough; state that "every node is a router and relays over multiple hops".只答"没有 AP"不够，要点出"每个节点都是路由器、多跳中继"。

ExamHow to write it in English

A MANET is a system of wireless mobile nodes that freely and dynamically self-organize into arbitrary and temporary network topologies, so that devices can be connected in areas without infrastructure. No fixed controller is required: a controller is dynamically elected or distributed among the nodes, and the network is self-creating, self-organizing and self-administering. The key difference from an infrastructure WLAN is that every node must be able to act as a router on demand: when two nodes have no direct radio channel, intermediate nodes relay the packets (multi-hop), instead of all traffic going through an AP.

In one line: a MANET is a temporary, self-organising network without infrastructure; its main difference from a WLAN is that every node must act as a router and forward over multiple hops.一句话：MANET 是无基础设施、自组织的临时网络；和 WLAN 最大的区别是每个节点都要当路由器、多跳转发。
Concept + Step by step: where the hidden node is

ConceptCollisions happen at the receiver

For wireless collisions, look at the receiver: as soon as B receives two signals at once, B cannot decode properly. Hidden node (p.48) = node C that is within range of destination B but outside range of sender A. C cannot hear A, senses the channel as "idle", transmits, and collides with A's data at B, causing low utilisation. Solution: RTS/CTS; although C cannot hear A's RTS, it can hear B's CTS, so it sets its NAV and defers (p.17).无线冲突要看接收端：只要 B 同时收到两路信号，B 就收不好。隐藏节点（hidden node，p.48）= 在目的端 B 范围内、在发送端 A 范围外的节点 C。C 听不到 A，侦听结果是"信道空"，一发就在 B 处和 A 的数据撞车，造成低利用率。解决：RTS/CTS，C 虽听不到 A 的 RTS，却能听到 B 的 CTS，于是设 NAV 推迟（p.17）。

Option by option

  • A. Within A's range, outside B's range: wrong. It can hear A and will back off by itself, so it is not a hidden node. (Beyond the slides: such a node is called an exposed node; when it wants to send to someone else, A blocks it unnecessarily.)A. 在 A 范围内、B 范围外：错。它听得到 A，会主动避让，不是隐藏节点。（课外补充：这种节点叫"暴露节点" exposed node，它想发给别人时会被 A 不必要地挡住。）
  • B. Within B's range, outside A's range: correct.B. 在 B 范围内、A 范围外：对。
  • C. Within range of both: wrong. It can hear A, so carrier sensing is enough.C. 同时在两人范围内：错。它能听到 A，载波侦听就够用了。
  • D. Within range of neither: wrong. Its signal cannot reach B, so it causes no collision.D. 不在任何人范围内：错。它的信号到不了 B，不会造成冲突。

Memory hook: "hidden" out of the sender's sight, yet standing right next to the receiver.记忆："藏"在发送方的视线外，却站在接收方身边。

In one line: choose B: the hidden node is within the destination's range but outside the sender's range.一句话：选 B：隐藏节点在目的端范围内、发送端范围外。
Concept + Step by step: ad hoc routing protocols

ConceptFour kinds of routing (p.51–53)

ClassWhen routes are foundCost
Proactive (table-driven)周期性（表驱动）Exchanged periodically all the time, whether used or not一直周期交换，不管用不用A route is always ready, but it costs bandwidth随时有路，但耗带宽
On-demandRoute discovery only when there is data to send; maintained during communication有数据要发才做路由发现，通信期间维护Saves bandwidth; the first packet waits for discovery省带宽，首包要等发现
HybridPeriodic within the local zone, on-demand globally本地区域用周期性，全局用按需Compromise
Location-basedOnly needs the positions of itself, the destination and its neighbours只需自己、目的和邻居的位置No routing table stored, but needs an accurate location service不存路由表，但要准确的位置服务

The lecturer said in class: on-demand routing does route discovery only when needed, activates only the relevant nodes, and does not waste bandwidth.老师课上说：按需路由只在需要时做路由发现，只激活相关节点，不浪费带宽。

Option by option

  • A. Periodic: wrong, exactly the opposite: routes are maintained all the time.A. 周期性：错，正好相反，平时一直在维护。
  • B. On-demand: correct, p.52 verbatim: "create routes only when necessary".
  • C. Hybrid: wrong, it still maintains routes periodically within the local zone.C. 混合：错，它在本地区域仍周期维护。
  • D. Location-based: wrong, it does not build routes at all; it forwards hop by hop based on position.D. 基于位置：错，它根本不建路由，靠位置逐跳转发。

Beyond the slides: common examples: AODV and DSR are on-demand, DSDV and OLSR are table-driven, ZRP is hybrid.课外补充：常见例子 AODV、DSR 是按需，DSDV、OLSR 是表驱动，ZRP 是混合。

In one line: choose B: on-demand protocols do not maintain routes in idle time; they start route discovery only when there is data to send.一句话：选 B：按需协议平时不维护路由，有数据要发才发起路由发现。
Concept + Step by step: combinatorial stability

ConceptThe topology keeps changing: can the updates keep up?

In an ad hoc network, "who can connect directly to whom" (reachability) changes over time, because nodes move, batteries run out, and software or hardware fails (p.47). Every change requires topology updates, and these updates eat bandwidth that was meant for user data.自组网里"谁能直接连到谁"（可达关系）会随时间变化，原因是：节点移动、电池耗尽、软件或硬件故障（p.47）。每次变化都要发拓扑更新，这些更新会吃掉本来给用户数据的带宽。

Combinatorial stability: within a given time window, if the topology changes slowly enough that all necessary topology updates can be propagated successfully, the network is combinatorially stable during that window. "Combinatorial" refers to the connections between nodes (which links exist); stable means this connection graph changes no faster than the network can absorb the updates.组合稳定性（combinatorial stability）：在给定的时间窗内，如果拓扑变化足够慢，慢到所有必要的拓扑更新都能成功传播出去，这个网络在这段时间内就是组合稳定的。"组合"指的是节点之间的连接关系（哪些边存在），稳定就是这张连接图的变化速度不超过网络消化更新的速度。

Step by stepWhat determines it

  1. Network connectivity: how fast and how drastically the connections themselves change.网络的连通性：连接关系本身变得多快、多剧烈。
  2. Complexity of the routing protocol: the more complex the protocol, the more messages one update needs and the slower it propagates.路由协议的复杂度：协议越复杂，一次更新要交换的消息越多、传播越慢。
  3. Instantaneous computing power of the nodes: slow nodes process updates slowly.节点的瞬时计算能力：节点算得慢，处理更新就慢。

The notes stress that it "does not only depend on connectivity", so write all three factors; writing only "speed of movement" loses marks.讲义原话强调"不仅取决于连通性"，所以三个因素都要写，只写"移动速度"会丢分。

Pitfalls

  • "Causes of topology change" (movement, battery, failure) and "factors that determine stability" (connectivity, protocol complexity, computing power) are two different lists; do not mix them in your answer."拓扑变化的原因"（移动、电池、故障）和"稳定性的决定因素"（连通性、协议复杂度、计算能力）是两组东西，别混在一起答。

ExamHow to write it in English

The reachability relations among nodes change with time because of node mobility, battery depletion and software or hardware failures, and the resulting topology updates consume bandwidth. Given a specific time window, an ad hoc network is combinatorially stable if and only if the topology changes occur sufficiently slowly to allow successful propagation of all necessary topology updates. Combinatorial stability is determined not only by the connectivity properties of the network, but also by the complexity of the routing protocol in use and the instantaneous computational capacity of the nodes.

In one line: if the topology changes slowly enough for all updates to propagate, the network is combinatorially stable; this depends on connectivity, routing protocol complexity and node computing power.一句话：拓扑变化慢到所有更新都能传播完就叫组合稳定，取决于连通性、路由协议复杂度和节点计算能力。
Concept + Step by step: four differences between WSNs and ad hoc networks

ConceptWhat a sensor network is

Wireless sensor network (WSN): a large number of low-cost, low-power small nodes (sensing + data processing + communication), densely deployed inside or near the phenomenon being observed; they can be scattered randomly in inaccessible terrain or disaster areas; the protocols must be self-organising and the nodes must cooperate (p.76). It is built with ad hoc network techniques, but existing ad hoc protocols are not necessarily suitable, because of four differences (p.56).无线传感器网络（Wireless Sensor Network, WSN）：大量低成本、低功耗的小节点（感知 + 数据处理 + 通信），密集地部署在被测现象内部或附近，可以随机撒在难以到达的地方或灾区；协议必须能自组织，节点要相互协作（p.76）。它要用自组网技术实现，但自组网已有的协议不一定适合，因为有四点不同（p.56）。

AspectGeneral ad hoc networkSensor network
Number of nodesFewerSeveral orders of magnitude more多几个数量级
Deployment and topologyTopology can changeDense deployment, prone to failure, topology changes very frequently部署密集、易失效，拓扑变化非常频繁
CommunicationPoint-to-pointBroadcast
ResourcesLaptops, phones, relatively ample笔记本、手机，较充足Power, computing capacity and memory all very limited功率、计算能力、内存都很有限

Step by stepWhy each point matters

  1. Large numbers → protocols must scale; not every node can store routes for the whole network.数量大 → 协议要能扩展，不能每个节点都存全网路由表。
  2. Dense, failure-prone, frequently changing topology → routing must heal itself quickly.密集、易坏、拓扑常变 → 路由要能快速自愈。
  3. Broadcast → the MAC must minimise collisions with neighbours' broadcasts (p.59).广播 → MAC 要尽量减少和邻居广播的冲突（p.59）。
  4. Limited resources → saving energy comes first; the lecturer said in class that power consumption is the most critical factor, because most nodes run on batteries.资源有限 → 一切以省电为先；老师课上说功耗是最关键的因素，因为节点大多靠电池。

Conclusion: ad hoc protocols cannot be copied directly to sensor networks.结论：自组网的协议不能直接照搬到传感器网络。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) The number of sensor nodes is huge, up to several orders of magnitude higher than in an ad hoc network. (2) Sensor nodes are densely deployed and prone to failures, so the topology changes very frequently. (3) Sensor nodes use a broadcast communication paradigm, while ad hoc networks are based on point-to-point communications. (4) Sensor nodes are limited in power, computational capacity and memory. Therefore protocols designed for ad hoc networks may not fit sensor networks well.

In one line: WSNs have orders of magnitude more nodes, are dense and failure-prone with frequently changing topology, use broadcast, and are limited in power, computing and memory.一句话：WSN 节点多几个数量级、密集易坏拓扑常变、用广播、功率计算内存都受限。
Concept + Step by step: the three planes of the sensor protocol stack

ConceptFive layers + three planes (p.59)

The five layers from the bottom up: physical layer (simple but robust modulation, transmission and reception), MAC layer (must save power and minimise collisions with neighbours' broadcasts), network layer (routes the data supplied by the transport layer), transport layer (maintains the data flow), application layer. In addition, three management planes run vertically through all layers and monitor, across the nodes:五层自下而上：物理层（简单而稳健的调制、收发）、MAC 层（要省电、尽量减少与邻居广播的冲突）、网络层（给传输层交来的数据选路）、传输层（维持数据流）、应用层。另有三个管理平面纵向贯穿各层，监控节点之间的：

  • Power management: how a node uses its energy, e.g. forwarding less when its battery is low.功率管理：节点怎么用电，比如电量低时少转发。
  • Mobility management: node movement, keeping track of who the neighbours are.移动管理：节点的移动，记住邻居是谁。
  • Task management: distributing sensing tasks among nodes.任务管理：在节点间分配感知任务。

The lecturer said in class that for the protocol stack it is enough to remember the five layers, and that power consumption is the most critical factor.老师课上说协议栈记住五层就行，功耗是最关键的因素。

Option by option

  • A. Power, mobility, task: correct, p.59 verbatim: "power, mobility, and task management planes".A. 功率、移动、任务：对，p.59 原话 "power, mobility, and task management planes"。
  • B. Security, QoS, billing: wrong, the sensor protocol stack in the notes has none of these.B. 安全、QoS、计费：错，讲义的传感器协议栈没有这三项。
  • C. Clock, routing, storage: wrong, routing is a network-layer job, not a plane.C. 时钟、路由、存储：错，路由是网络层的事，不是平面。
  • D. Frequency, power, coding: wrong, frequency and coding belong to the physical layer.D. 频率、功率、编码：错，频率和编码属于物理层。

Memory hook: sensors are short of power, move around and must share the work, so the three planes are "power, motion, tasks".记忆：传感器最缺电、会挪动、要分工，所以是"电、动、活"三个平面。

In one line: choose A: the three management planes are power, mobility and task.一句话：选 A：三个管理平面是功率、移动、任务。
Concept + Step by step: the two main parts of the EPS

ConceptThe two halves of the LTE system (p.61–62)

LTE is 3GPP's evolution after UMTS (3G); its goal is seamless IP connectivity between the terminal (UE) and the packet data network (PDN). The whole system is called the Evolved Packet System (EPS) and consists of two halves:LTE 是 3GPP 在 UMTS（3G）之后的演进，目标是终端 UE 和分组数据网 PDN 之间无缝的 IP 连接。整个系统叫演进分组系统 EPS（Evolved Packet System），由两半组成：

PartWhich project it comes fromWhat it contains
EPC (Evolved Packet Core)EPC 演进分组核心网SAE (System Architecture Evolution)SAE（系统架构演进）Many logical nodes, e.g. MME, S-GW很多逻辑节点，如 MME、S-GW
E-UTRAN (Evolved UTRAN, the radio access network)E-UTRAN 演进的无线接入网LTEEssentially only one type of node: the eNodeB基本只有一种节点：eNodeB

Option by option

  • A. UTRAN + GSM core network: wrong. UTRAN is the access network of 3G UMTS; LTE uses the "evolved" E-UTRAN, with an extra E in front.A. UTRAN + GSM 核心网：错。UTRAN 是 3G UMTS 的接入网，LTE 用的是"演进的"E-UTRAN，名字前多个 E。
  • B. EPC + E-UTRAN: correct.
  • C. eNodeB + MME: wrong. These are one node from each side, not the two main parts.C. eNodeB + MME：错。这是两边各一个节点，不是两大组成部分。
  • D. S1 + X2: wrong. These are interfaces, not network parts.D. S1 + X2：错。这是接口，不是网络部分。

Memory hook: SAE handles the "core" (Core → EPC), LTE handles the "radio" (Radio → E-UTRAN).记忆：SAE 管"核心"（Core → EPC），LTE 管"无线"（Radio → E-UTRAN）。

In one line: choose B: EPS = core network EPC + access network E-UTRAN.一句话：选 B：EPS = 核心网 EPC + 接入网 E-UTRAN。
Concept + Step by step: the X2 and S1 interfaces

ConceptA flat access network (p.63)

The E-UTRAN consists of many eNodeBs, with no central controller for normal user traffic. eNodeBs are connected sideways to each other by the X2 interface; upwards, each eNodeB connects to the EPC core network by the S1 interface, which is split into two:E-UTRAN 由许多 eNodeB 组成，普通用户业务没有集中控制器。各 eNodeB 之间用 X2 接口横向相连；eNodeB 向上用 S1 接口连核心网 EPC，S1 又分两条：

  • S1-MME: to the mobility management entity (MME), carries signalling (control plane).S1-MME：接移动性管理实体 MME，走信令（控制面）。
  • S1-U: to the serving gateway (S-GW), carries user data (U = user plane).S1-U：接服务网关 S-GW，走用户数据（U = user plane）。

Between the eNodeB and the UE run the air signaling (AS) protocols (the wording of notes p.63: "air signaling (AS) protocols"; beyond the slides: in the 3GPP standard AS stands for Access Stratum).eNodeB 和 UE 之间跑的是空中接口信令（AS）协议（讲义 p.63 原话 "air signaling (AS) protocols"；课外补充：3GPP 标准里 AS 指接入层 Access Stratum）。

Option by option

  • A. S1; X2: wrong, exactly reversed.
  • B. X2; S1: correct, p.63 verbatim.
  • C. Uu; S1: wrong. (Beyond the slides: Uu is the air interface between the UE and the eNodeB, not between eNodeBs.)C. Uu；S1：错。（课外补充：Uu 是 UE 和 eNodeB 之间的空中接口，不是 eNodeB 之间的。）
  • D. X2; Gi: wrong. (Beyond the slides: Gi is the 3G core network's interface to external data networks; its LTE counterpart is SGi, and it does not connect to eNodeBs.)D. X2；Gi：错。（课外补充：Gi 是 3G 核心网连外部数据网的接口，LTE 里对应 SGi，不连 eNodeB。）

Memory hook: X looks like a cross, linking siblings sideways; S1 goes up to the core network, with MME carrying signalling and U carrying user data.记忆：X 像交叉，横着连兄弟；S1 往上连核心网，MME 走信令、U 走用户数据。

In one line: choose B: X2 between eNodeBs, S1 to the core network (S1-MME to the MME, S1-U to the S-GW).一句话：选 B：eNodeB 之间是 X2，到核心网是 S1（S1-MME 到 MME，S1-U 到 S-GW）。
Concept + Step by step: functions of the E-UTRAN

ConceptEverything radio belongs to the eNodeB

The E-UTRAN is responsible for all radio-related functions (p.64). Because the access network has only one type of node, the eNodeB, and no central controller (p.63), all these functions are integrated in the eNodeB. Beyond the slides: 3G has a centralised radio network controller (RNC); LTE removes it and uses a flat architecture, giving shorter paths and lower latency.E-UTRAN 负责所有和无线有关的功能（p.64）。因为接入网只有 eNodeB 一种节点、没有集中控制器（p.63），这些功能全部集成在 eNodeB 里。课外补充：3G 里有集中的无线网络控制器 RNC，LTE 把它去掉、做成扁平结构，路径更短、时延更低。

Step by stepThe four groups of functions, each with the reason

  1. Radio Resource Management: all functions related to radio bearers: radio bearer control, radio admission control, radio mobility control, and scheduling and dynamic resource allocation in uplink and downlink. Why: air-interface resources (time, frequency) are limited and must be allocated to the UEs as needed.无线资源管理（Radio Resource Management）：与无线承载有关的全部功能：无线承载控制、无线接纳控制、无线移动性控制、上下行的调度和动态资源分配。为什么：空口资源（时间、频率）有限，要按需分给各 UE。
  2. Header Compression: compresses IP packet headers to reduce overhead. Why: for small packets such as voice, the IP header takes a large share, so compressing it makes the air interface more efficient.包头压缩（Header Compression）：压缩 IP 包头，减少开销。为什么：语音等小包的 IP 头占比大，压缩后空口效率更高。
  3. Security: all data sent over the air interface is encrypted. Why: anyone can receive a radio signal.安全（Security）：空中接口上发送的所有数据都加密。为什么：无线信号谁都能收到。
  4. Connectivity to the EPC: the signalling path to the MME and the bearer path to the S-GW, i.e. S1-MME and S1-U.连接 EPC（Connectivity to the EPC）：到 MME 的信令和到 S-GW 的承载路径，也就是 S1-MME 和 S1-U。

Pitfalls

  • Write all four sub-items under radio resource management (bearer control, admission control, mobility control, scheduling); these details earn marks.无线资源管理下的四个小项（承载控制、接纳控制、移动控制、调度）要写全，这是得分细节。
  • Do not list core-network functions (such as the MME's mobility-management signalling) as E-UTRAN functions.别把核心网的功能（如 MME 的移动性管理信令处理）写成 E-UTRAN 的。

ExamHow to write it in English

The E-UTRAN is responsible for all radio-related functions: (1) radio resource management, i.e. all functions related to radio bearers, including radio bearer control, radio admission control, radio mobility control, and scheduling and dynamic allocation of resources to UEs in both uplink and downlink; (2) header compression of IP packet headers to reduce overhead; (3) security: all data sent over the radio interface is encrypted; (4) connectivity to the EPC: the signalling towards the MME and the bearer path to the S-GW. All these functions reside in the eNodeBs; there is no centralized controller.

In one line: the E-UTRAN handles radio resource management, header compression, air-interface encryption and connectivity to the EPC, all done in the eNodeB.一句话：E-UTRAN 管无线资源管理、包头压缩、空口加密、连接 EPC，全部做在 eNodeB 里。
Concept + Step by step: key E-UTRA targets

ConceptFour groups of targets (p.65)

MetricFigure in the notes
Scalable bandwidth1.4 MHz to 20 MHz
High data rateDownlink peak above 300 Mbps (4×4 MIMO); uplink peak 86 Mbps下行峰值超过 300 Mbps（4×4 MIMO）；上行峰值 86 Mbps
High mobilityOptimised for low speeds below 15 km/h, supports up to 350 or even 500 km/h针对 15 km/h 以下的低速优化，最高支持 350 甚至 500 km/h
Scalable coverageFrom femtocells to 100 km cells毫微微小区（femtocell）到 100 km 小区

The lecturer said in class that LTE bandwidth can be chosen flexibly between 1.4 and 20 MHz, unlike 1G, where every channel had a fixed bandwidth.老师课上说 LTE 带宽可以在 1.4–20 MHz 之间灵活选，不像 1G 那样每个信道带宽固定。

Option by option(this question asks for the statement that does NOT match)

  • A: matches.
  • B: matches, provided 4×4 MIMO is used.
  • C: matches.
  • D: does not match, so this is the answer. The two numbers are swapped: LTE is optimised for 15 km/h (walking, low speed), while 350 km/h is the highest "supported" speed (high-speed rail).D：不符，是答案。两个数对调了：优化的是 15 km/h（步行、低速），350 km/h 是最高"支持"的速度（高铁）。

Memory hook: optimise for most people (walking, 15), support the extreme cases (high-speed rail, 350/500).记忆：优化给大多数人（走路 15），支持到极端情况（高铁 350/500）。

In one line: choose D: LTE is optimised for below 15 km/h and supports up to 350 or even 500 km/h.一句话：选 D：LTE 针对 15 km/h 以下优化，最高支持 350 甚至 500 km/h。
Concept + Step by step: how many slots are in an LTE frame

ConceptFDD frame structure (p.66)

LTE divides time into three levels: radio frame 10 ms → subframe 1 ms → slot 0.5 ms. In FDD (frequency division duplex) mode, a frame has 10 subframes and each subframe has 2 slots. In TDD mode the frame is also 10 ms, but split into two 5 ms half-frames, which may contain special subframes with DwPTS, GP and UpPTS; this question is about FDD.LTE 在时间上分三级：无线帧（radio frame）10 ms → 子帧（subframe）1 ms → 时隙（slot）0.5 ms。FDD（频分双工）模式下，一帧 10 个子帧，每个子帧 2 个时隙。TDD 模式帧长也是 10 ms，但分成两个 5 ms 半帧，里面可能有含 DwPTS、GP、UpPTS 的特殊子帧，本题问的是 FDD。

Step by stepTwo methods that check each other

By hierarchy: 10 subframes × 2 slots/subframe = 20 slots
By duration: 10 ms ÷ 0.5 ms = 20 slots按层级：10 个子帧 × 2 个时隙/子帧 = 20 个时隙
按时长：10 ms ÷ 0.5 ms = 20 个时隙

Beyond the slides: the 1 ms subframe is LTE's basic scheduling time unit (TTI); one slot is the time length of a resource block (see b28).课外补充：1 ms 的子帧是 LTE 调度的基本时间单位（TTI）；一个时隙是资源块在时间上的长度（见 b28）。

Pitfalls

  • Do not mistake subframes (10) for slots (20).别把子帧（10 个）当成时隙（20 个）。

ExamHow to write it in English

In FDD mode, each 10 ms radio frame consists of 10 subframes of 1 ms, and each subframe consists of 2 slots of 0.5 ms. Hence one radio frame contains 10 × 2 = 20 slots (check: 10 ms / 0.5 ms = 20).

In one line: a 10 ms frame = 10 subframes of 1 ms = 20 slots of 0.5 ms.一句话：10 ms 帧 = 10 个 1 ms 子帧 = 20 个 0.5 ms 时隙。
Concept + Step by step: resource elements in a resource block

ConceptThe resource grid (p.67)

The LTE downlink uses OFDMA, and its resources form a "time × frequency" grid.LTE 下行用 OFDMA，资源是一张"时间 × 频率"的网格。

  • Resource element (RE): 1 subcarrier × 1 OFDM symbol, the smallest cell of the grid.资源单元 RE（Resource Element）：1 个子载波 × 1 个 OFDM 符号，网格里最小的一格。
  • Resource block (RB): 12 subcarriers in frequency × 1 slot (0.5 ms) in time.资源块 RB（Resource Block）：频域 12 个子载波 × 时域 1 个时隙（0.5 ms）。
  • The number of OFDM symbols in a slot depends on the cyclic prefix (CP): 7 with normal CP, 6 with extended CP (used in large cells, see b29).一个时隙里有几个 OFDM 符号取决于循环前缀 CP：常规 CP 是 7 个，扩展 CP 是 6 个（大小区用，见 b29）。

The lecturer also mentioned in class that each resource block has 12 subcarriers.老师课上也提到每个资源块 12 个子载波。

Step by step

Normal CP: RE = 12 subcarriers × 7 symbols = 84
Extended CP: RE = 12 subcarriers × 6 symbols = 72常规 CP：RE = 12 子载波 × 7 符号 = 84 个
扩展 CP：RE = 12 子载波 × 6 符号 = 72 个

Beyond the slides: the LTE subcarrier spacing is 15 kHz, so one RB is 12 × 15 = 180 kHz wide; the RB pair over the two slots of a 1 ms subframe has 2 × 84 = 168 REs.课外补充：LTE 子载波间隔 15 kHz，所以一个 RB 宽 12 × 15 = 180 kHz；一个 1 ms 子帧里两个时隙的 RB 对共 2 × 84 = 168 个 RE。

Pitfalls

  • An RB spans 1 slot in time, not 1 subframe; do not multiply 12 × 14.RB 在时间上是 1 个时隙，不是 1 个子帧，别乘成 12 × 14。
  • If the question says "normal cyclic prefix", use 7; if it does not say, assume normal CP and state the assumption.题目写"常规循环前缀"就用 7；没说明时按常规 CP 算，并注明假设。

ExamHow to write it in English

A resource block spans 12 subcarriers in the frequency domain and one slot in the time domain. With the normal cyclic prefix there are 7 OFDM symbols per slot, and a resource element is one subcarrier × one OFDM symbol, so one RB contains 12 × 7 = 84 REs (72 with the extended CP).

In one line: RB = 12 subcarriers × 7 symbols = 84 REs (72 with extended CP).一句话：RB = 12 子载波 × 7 符号 = 84 个 RE（扩展 CP 为 72）。
Concept + Step by step: when to use the extended CP

ConceptThe cyclic prefix absorbs echoes

The cyclic prefix (CP) copies a short piece from the end of an OFDM symbol to its front as a guard interval. Multipath signals travel different paths, and late echoes spill into the next symbol and cause interference; as long as the guard interval is no shorter than the maximum delay spread, the echoes fall inside the CP and the receiver simply discards the CP. The condition in Part 2 Ch. 7 p.17: guard interval TG ≥ maximum delay spread TD.循环前缀（Cyclic Prefix, CP）是把 OFDM 符号末尾的一小段复制到符号前面，当保护间隔。多径信号走不同的路，晚到的回波会拖进下一个符号造成干扰；只要保护间隔不短于最大时延扩展，回波就落在 CP 里，接收机丢掉 CP 即可。Part 2 第 7 章 p.17 的条件：保护间隔 TG ≥ 最大时延扩展 TD。

Notes Part B p.67: "The extended CP is used when the cell size is large." Large cell → longer reflection paths, echoes arrive later → larger delay spread → longer CP needed. Cost: the slot length is fixed at 0.5 ms, so with the longer CP only 6 symbols fit (7 with normal CP), and the overhead grows.讲义 Part B p.67："The extended CP is used when the cell size is large."小区大 → 反射路径长、回波来得更晚 → 时延扩展大 → 要更长的 CP。代价：时隙长度固定 0.5 ms，CP 变长后只放得下 6 个符号（常规 7 个），开销变大。

Option by option

  • A. Very small cell: wrong, a small cell has a small delay spread and the normal CP is enough.A. 小区很小：错，小区小时延扩展小，常规 CP 就够。
  • B. Very large cell: correct, p.67 verbatim.B. 小区很大：对，p.67 原文。
  • C. In the uplink: wrong, the CP length depends on delay spread, not on uplink vs downlink.C. 上行时：错，CP 长短看时延扩展，不看上下行。
  • D. TDD mode: wrong, both FDD and TDD have normal and extended CP.D. TDD 模式：错，FDD 和 TDD 都有常规 / 扩展两种 CP。

Beyond the slides: the normal CP is about 4.7 μs, corresponding to a path difference of 4.7 μs × 3×10⁸ m/s ≈ 1.4 km; the extended CP is about 16.7 μs, corresponding to about 5 km, so it tolerates the more distant echoes in large cells.课外补充：常规 CP 约 4.7 μs，对应路程差 4.7 μs × 3×10⁸ m/s ≈ 1.4 km；扩展 CP 约 16.7 μs，对应约 5 km，所以能容忍大小区里更远的回波。

In one line: choose B: large cells have a large delay spread and use the extended CP, at the cost of only 6 symbols per slot.一句话：选 B：大小区时延扩展大，用扩展 CP，代价是每时隙只剩 6 个符号。
Concept + Step by step: GBR and non-GBR bearers

ConceptWhat a bearer is

LTE is all-IP and uses EPS bearers to carry IP traffic from the PDN gateway to the UE: a bearer is an IP packet flow with a defined QoS between the gateway and the UE, i.e. a logical connection (p.68). Every bearer has one QCI and one ARP (p.69). By the QoS they provide there are two types; the lecturer said in class that remembering these two types is enough.LTE 全 IP，用EPS 承载（bearer）把 IP 业务从 PDN 网关送到 UE：一个承载就是网关和 UE 之间一条有确定 QoS 的 IP 分组流，是一条逻辑连接（p.68）。每个承载都有一个 QCI 和一个 ARP（p.69）。按提供的 QoS 分两类，老师课上说记住这两类就行。

GBR bearerNon-GBR bearer
Rate guaranteeGuaranteed minimum bit rate (GBR)有最低保证速率 GBRNo rate guaranteed不保证任何速率
ResourcesDedicated resources permanently allocated at setup (or modification)建立（或修改）时永久分配专用资源Not permanently allocated
Upper limitCan exceed the GBR when resources are spare, up to the MBR资源富余时可超过 GBR，上限是 MBR—
SuitsVoIP, voiceWeb browsing, FTP

Step by stepPoints to include in your answer

  1. Difference: write it along the three rows of the table above: guaranteed or not, whether resources are permanently allocated, typical services. Mentioning the MBR for GBR makes it more complete.区别：按上表三行写：保证不保证、资源是否永久分配、典型业务。GBR 提一句 MBR 更完整。
  2. Default bearer: must be non-GBR; it is set up as soon as the UE attaches to the network and is used for initial connectivity (p.70). Why: a UE that has just switched on does not yet know what services it will run, so it should not permanently hold resources from the start.默认承载（default bearer）：必须是 non-GBR，UE 一接入网络就建立，用于初始连接（p.70）。为什么：UE 刚开机还不知道要跑什么业务，不能一上来就永久占资源。
  3. Dedicated bearer: can be GBR or non-GBR; it is set up only when there is a new service with different QoS requirements.专用承载（dedicated bearer）：可以是 GBR 也可以是 non-GBR，有新业务、QoS 要求不同时才建立。

Pitfalls

  • GBR does not mean "fixed rate": when resources are spare it can exceed the GBR, up to the MBR.GBR 不是"速率固定"：资源有富余时可以超过 GBR，最多到 MBR。

ExamHow to write it in English

A GBR bearer has a minimum guaranteed bit rate, for which dedicated transmission resources are permanently allocated at bearer establishment or modification; it is used for applications such as VoIP. A bit rate higher than the GBR may be allowed if resources are available, up to the maximum bit rate (MBR). A non-GBR bearer does not guarantee any particular bit rate and no bandwidth resources are allocated permanently; it is used for web browsing or FTP. The default bearer, created when the UE connects to the network, must be a non-GBR bearer; a dedicated bearer can be either GBR or non-GBR.

In one line: GBR guarantees a minimum rate and permanently holds resources (VoIP); non-GBR guarantees nothing (web browsing); the default bearer must be non-GBR.一句话：GBR 保证最低速率、永久占资源（VoIP），non-GBR 不保证（网页）；默认承载必须是 non-GBR。
Concept + Step by step: the roles of ARP and QCI

ConceptTwo QoS parameters per bearer

ARP (Allocation and Retention Priority, p.74) is used for call admission control and pre-emption: under radio congestion it decides whether a new bearer is set up; when a new bearer request arrives it decides whether it may pre-empt others; when the system is overloaded it decides which connections are dropped first so that high-priority ones are kept. Once a bearer has been set up, ARP no longer affects packet forwarding.ARP（Allocation and Retention Priority，分配与保持优先级，p.74）用于呼叫接纳控制和抢占：无线拥塞时决定新承载建不建；新承载请求来时决定能不能抢占别人；系统过载时决定先断哪些连接，保住高优先级连接。承载建立成功后，ARP 不再影响分组转发。

QCI (QoS Class Identifier, p.71–73) is characterised by priority, packet delay budget and acceptable packet loss rate. It decides how the eNodeB handles packets: scheduling, queue management, rate-shaping policy and RLC mode; bearers with strict loss requirements use RLC acknowledged mode (AM). Forwarding treatment is decided by QCI, GBR and MBR.QCI（QoS Class Identifier，p.71–73）由优先级、分组时延预算、可接受丢包率刻画，决定 eNodeB 怎么处理分组：调度、队列管理、限速策略和 RLC 模式；丢包要求严的承载用 RLC 确认模式（AM）。转发处理由 QCI、GBR、MBR 决定。

Option by option

  • A: wrong. This is exactly what the notes say ARP does not handle; that is the job of QCI, GBR and MBR.A：错，正好是讲义说 ARP 不管的事，那是 QCI、GBR、MBR 的职责。
  • B: correct. The three points on p.74: admission, pre-emption, and which bearer to drop under overload.B：对，p.74 的三条：接纳、抢占、过载时断谁。
  • C: wrong. The modulation scheme belongs to link adaptation (listed as an open issue on p.75) and has nothing to do with ARP.C：错，调制方式属于链路自适应（p.75 列为开放问题），与 ARP 无关。
  • D: wrong. The RLC mode is decided by QCI (p.73).D：错，RLC 模式由 QCI 决定（p.73）。

Memory hook: ARP guards the "door" (who gets in, who gets kicked out); QCI manages the "road" (how packets queue, how they are delivered).记忆：ARP 管"门口"（进不进、踢谁走），QCI 管"路上"（怎么排队、怎么送）。

In one line: B. ARP decides, under congestion, whether a bearer is admitted, whether it can pre-empt, and which bearer is dropped first under overload; once the bearer is set up, forwarding depends on QCI.一句话：选 B：ARP 决定拥塞时接不接纳、能否抢占、过载先断谁；建好后转发看 QCI。
Concept + Step by step: five IoT challenges

ConceptWhat makes IoT hard

The Internet of Things (IoT) connects objects that were never networked before, so that they can communicate and interact with people and with other objects (p.78). More devices, more data and more standards bring five challenges (p.82–83). This was tested in the final, 2025-26 S1 Q4(b).物联网（Internet of Things, IoT）就是把原来不联网的物体连起来，让它们能和人、和其他物体通信交互（p.78）。设备一多、数据一多、标准一多，就带来五个挑战（p.82–83）。这一题 2025-26 S1 Q4(b) 期末考过。

Step by stepFive points, each with "what it is + why it is hard"

  1. Scalability: the system must grow to millions of devices, and how the whole system supports that is the key question; at the network layer, IPv6 can give devices a huge number of addresses.可扩展性（Scalability）：规模要扩到数以百万计的设备，整个系统怎么支撑是关键问题；网络层可以靠 IPv6 给设备分配海量地址。
  2. Security: as more and more "things" are connected, the attack surface grows sharply; once a device is hacked, its connections become a problem, and a compromised device can be used as a stepping stone to attack other devices and systems.安全（Security）：越来越多的"物"互相连接，攻击面大大扩大；一个设备被黑，它的连接就成了问题，被攻破的设备可以当跳板攻击其他设备和系统。
  3. Privacy: with more and more sensors, much of the collected data relates to specific people and their activities and may contain sensitive information and credentials; how the data is protected, whether it is shared and with whom are the key questions.隐私（Privacy）：传感器越来越多，采到的数据很多和具体的人及其活动有关，可能含敏感信息和凭据；数据怎么保护、要不要共享、和谁共享是关键问题。
  4. Big data and analysis: huge numbers of sensors produce a flood of data; the difficulty is processing large volumes of data from different sources and in different formats in time to extract useful information.大数据与分析（Big data and analysis）：海量传感器带来数据洪流；难点是要及时处理来自不同来源、不同格式的海量数据，才能得到有价值的信息。
  5. Interoperability: many protocols and architectures compete for the market and for standardisation, some proprietary and some open; new standards help, but there are still many different implementations.互操作性（Interoperability）：各种协议和架构争夺市场和标准，有的专有、有的开放；新标准能缓解，但实现方式仍然很多。

Pitfalls

  • "Big data and analysis" counts as one point. Do not split it into two and then miss interoperability."大数据与分析"算一点，不要拆成两点再漏掉互操作性。
  • Write one sentence of explanation for each point; listing the five terms alone will not get full marks.每点要写一句解释，只列五个名词拿不全分。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) Scalability: the IoT may grow to millions of devices, and how the overall system supports such a huge number of devices is a critical issue; IPv6 can provide the addresses. (2) Security: the threat surface is greatly expanded, and a compromised device can serve as a launching point to attack other devices and systems. (3) Privacy: much of the sensed data is specific to individuals and their activities and may contain sensitive information; how it is protected and with whom it is shared is critical. (4) Big data and analysis: the deluge of data from many sources in various forms must be evaluated in a timely and efficient manner. (5) Interoperability: various proprietary and open protocols and architectures compete for market share and standardization.

In one line: the five IoT challenges are scalability, security, privacy, big data and analysis, and interoperability.一句话：IoT 五大挑战：可扩展性、安全、隐私、大数据与分析、互操作性。
Concept + Step by step: how many layers in the IoTWF reference architecture

ConceptTwo standards + one simplified framework (p.84–86)

ArchitectureProposed by, whenFeatures
oneM2METSI M2M Technical Committee, 2012ETSI 的 M2M 技术委员会，2012Aims at a common service layer目标是一个公共服务层
IoTWFIoT World Forum Architecture Committee, 20147-layer reference model, including edge computing, data storage and access; data flows up from the edge to the centre7 层参考模型，含边缘计算、数据存储和访问；数据从边缘往上流到中心
Simplified framework (used in the notes)简化框架（讲义采用）Cisco textbookTwo parallel three-layer stacks: Core IoT Functional Stack + Data Management and Compute Stack两个并行的三层栈：核心 IoT 功能栈 + 数据管理与计算栈

The lecturer said in class to use the simplified framework when studying; it is easier to understand than the other two standards.老师课上说学习时用简化框架，比另外两个标准好理解。

Option by option

  • A. 3 layers: wrong. 3 is the number of layers in each stack of the simplified framework.A. 3 层：错，3 层是简化框架里每个栈的层数。
  • B. 5 layers: wrong. That is the number of layers in the sensor network protocol stack (p.59); do not mix them up.B. 5 层：错，那是传感器网络协议栈的层数（p.59），别串。
  • C. 7 layers: correct. p.85: "seven-layer IoT architectural reference model".
  • D. Two three-layer stacks: wrong. That is the simplified framework in the notes, not IoTWF.D. 两个三层栈：错，这是讲义的简化框架，不是 IoTWF。

Beyond the slides: the seven IoTWF layers, from bottom to top, are physical devices and controllers, connectivity, edge (fog) computing, data accumulation, data abstraction, application, and collaboration and processes.课外补充：IoTWF 七层自下而上是物理设备与控制器、连接、边缘（雾）计算、数据积累、数据抽象、应用、协作与流程。

In one line: C. IoTWF has 7 layers; it is the simplified framework in the notes that has two three-layer stacks.一句话：选 C：IoTWF 是 7 层；讲义的简化框架才是两个三层栈。
Concept + Step by step: the core functional stack and its four sublayers

ConceptCore IoT Functional Stack (p.88–90)

The simplified framework has two parallel stacks. This question asks about the Core IoT Functional Stack, which describes how the "things" get their information to the applications:简化框架有两个并行栈，这题问的是核心 IoT 功能栈（Core IoT Functional Stack），它描述"物"怎么把信息送到应用：

  1. "Things" layer (sensors and actuators): the physical devices; they must cope with the constraints of the environment they are deployed in and still provide the required information."物"层（Things：传感器和执行器）：物理设备，既要适应部署环境的限制，又要提供所需信息。
  2. Communications network layer: when smart objects are not self-contained, they must communicate with outside systems; this layer has four sublayers.通信网络层（Communications network layer）：智能物体不能自给自足时，要和外部系统通信，分四个子层。
  3. Application and analytics layer: processes the collected data, controls the smart objects when needed, and makes intelligent decisions based on the data.应用与分析层（Application and analytics layer）：处理采集的数据，必要时控制智能物体，并据此做智能决策。

This is a frequent final-exam topic: 2024-25 S2 Q4(b) and 2025-26 S2 Q4(d) both asked for the four sublayers of the communications network layer, and 2023-24 S2 Q4(a) asked you to describe the two parallel stacks.这一部分是期末高频题：2024-25 S2 Q4(b) 和 2025-26 S2 Q4(d) 两次考了通信网络层的四个子层，2023-24 S2 Q4(a) 要求描述两个并行栈。

Step by stepThe four sublayers of the communications network layer, bottom up

SublayerWhat it doesExample
Access networkThe "last mile" of the IoT networkIoT 网络的"最后一公里"802.11ah, 802.15.4g, LoRa
Gateways & backhaulGroups the smart objects in an area around a common gateway, which forwards the data over a longer-range medium to the headend station把一片区域的智能物体汇聚到公共网关，再经更远距离的介质送到中心站The gateway is usually fixed网关通常固定
Network transportNetwork- and transport-layer protocols; must be open, standard, scalable and secure网络层和传输层协议，要开放、标准、可扩展、安全IP, UDP/TCP
IoT network managementApplication protocols that let headend applications exchange data with the sensors让中心应用和传感器交换数据的应用协议HTTP, WebSocket

Memory hook: "access → gather and backhaul → transport (IP) → management (application protocols)".记忆："接入 → 汇聚回传 → 传输（IP）→ 管理（应用协议）"。

Pitfalls

  • The network transport sublayer is IP/UDP/TCP; the network management sublayer is HTTP/WebSocket. Do not swap them.网络传输子层是 IP/UDP/TCP，网络管理子层是 HTTP/WebSocket，别放反。
  • "Three layers" refers to the functional stack, not to the data management and compute stack (edge / fog / cloud)."三层"问的是功能栈，不是数据管理与计算栈（边缘 / 雾 / 云）。

ExamHow to write it in English

The Core IoT Functional Stack has three layers: (1) the "things" layer of sensors and actuators; (2) the communications network layer; (3) the application and analytics layer. The communications network layer is divided into four sublayers: (a) the access network sublayer, the last mile of the IoT network, typically wireless technologies such as IEEE 802.11ah, 802.15.4g and LoRa; (b) the gateways and backhaul network sublayer, where smart objects in an area are organized around a common gateway that forwards the collected information over a longer-range medium to a headend station; (c) the network transport sublayer, which implements network and transport protocols such as IP, UDP and TCP; (d) the IoT network management sublayer, which uses application protocols such as HTTP and WebSocket so that headend applications can exchange data with the sensors.

In one line: three layers = things, communications network, application and analytics; the four sublayers of the communications network layer = access network, gateways and backhaul, network transport, IoT network management.一句话：三层 = 物、通信网络、应用与分析；通信网络层四子层 = 接入网、网关与回程、网络传输、IoT 网络管理。
Concept + Step by step: networks classified by range

ConceptClasses by communication range (p.95)

The first parameter in choosing an IoT access technology is the distance between the smart object and the information collector. The notes classify by scenario:选 IoT 接入技术的第一个参数是智能物体和信息采集器之间的距离。讲义按场景分档：

ClassScopeExample
PAN (personal area network)A few metresBluetooth
HAN (home area network)Tens of metresZigBee, BLE
NAN (neighbourhood area network)Hundreds of metres802.11 mesh
FAN (field area network)Tens to hundreds of metres, open outdoor areas几十到几百米，户外开阔区—
LANAbout 100 m802.11
MAN / WANA few km / beyond a few km几公里 / 超过几公里—

Option by option

  • A. PAN: wrong. The notes' PAN example is classic Bluetooth; BLE is placed under HAN.A. PAN：错，讲义 PAN 的例子是经典蓝牙；BLE 被放在 HAN。
  • B. HAN: correct. p.95: "such as ZigBee and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)".
  • C. NAN: wrong. The NAN example is 802.11 mesh.
  • D. WAN: wrong. ZigBee and BLE are both short-range, low-power technologies.D. WAN：错，ZigBee、BLE 都是短距、低功耗技术。

Pitfalls: the notes put Bluetooth (PAN) and BLE (HAN) in different classes. Do not pick A just because both are called Bluetooth.易错：蓝牙（PAN）和 BLE（HAN）在讲义里分在不同档，别因为都叫蓝牙就选 A。

In one line: B. ZigBee and BLE belong to HAN, tens of metres.一句话：选 B：ZigBee 和 BLE 属于 HAN，几十米。
Concept + Step by step: what decides the access technology

ConceptThree deciding factors (p.95–96)

  1. Communication range: how far the smart object is from the information collector; this decides the class (PAN, HAN, ...).通信距离：智能物体到信息采集器有多远，决定选哪一档（PAN、HAN……）。
  2. Number of target devices in one collection cell: together with the transmission range and the required throughput, this parameter decides the cell size.单个采集小区里的目标设备数量：结合传输距离和所需吞吐量，这个参数决定小区大小。
  3. Technology cost.

Usually cost, range, power consumption and available bandwidth are weighed together. These are all questions of "can the network connect, how many devices, at what cost".通常要把成本、距离、功耗和可用带宽综合考虑。这些都是"网络能不能连上、连多少、花多少"的问题。

Option by option(this question asks for the one that is "not included")

  • A. Communication range: included, the first factor.A. 通信距离：包括，第一因素。
  • B. Number of devices: included, the second factor.B. 设备数量：包括，第二因素。
  • C. Technology cost: included, the third factor.C. 技术成本：包括，第三因素。
  • D. Screen resolution: not included; this is the answer. Most sensors have no screen at all; it is a property of a terminal's display and has nothing to do with the access network.D. 屏幕分辨率：不包括，是答案。大多数传感器根本没有屏幕，这是终端显示属性，与接入网络无关。

Memory hook: how far, how many, how expensive.记忆：远不远、多不多、贵不贵。

In one line: D. The three factors are range, number of devices per cell and cost; screen resolution is irrelevant.一句话：选 D：前三个因素是距离、单小区设备数量、成本，屏幕分辨率无关。
Concept + Step by step: why fog computing is needed

ConceptSending everything to the cloud: pros and problems

The obvious approach is to send all data to the cloud for central processing. The advantage is simplicity: the objects only need to connect to one central application, which can see every node and do all the analysis (p.103). But IoT data volumes are huge, so bandwidth management becomes a problem: the network must carry the traffic, and the servers must take in, store and process the data (p.104).最自然的做法是把数据全送到云端集中处理，好处是简单：物体只要连上一个中心应用，它能看到所有节点、做所有分析（p.103）。但 IoT 数据量太大，带宽管理成问题：网络要扛得住流量，服务器要吞得下、存得下、算得动（p.104）。

Step by stepPart 1: five problems (p.105)

  1. Very little bandwidth in the last mile: the access network is mostly low-power wireless and cannot carry huge amounts of raw data.最后一公里带宽很小：接入网多是低功耗无线，传不了海量原始数据。
  2. Long latency: a round trip to the cloud rules out real-time response.时延大：来回一趟云端，做不到实时响应。
  3. Unreliable backhaul: gateway backhaul often relies on 3G/LTE or even satellite.回程不可靠：网关的回程常靠 3G/LTE 甚至卫星。
  4. Too much data on the backhaul to handle.回程上数据量太大，处理不过来。
  5. Big data keeps getting bigger: real-time analysis and response become almost impossible.大数据越来越大：实时分析和响应几乎不可能。

Step by stepPart 2: how fog computing solves this (p.106–108)

  • Approach: distribute data management throughout the IoT system, as close to the edge of the IP network as possible. Any device with compute, storage and network connectivity can act as a fog node, adding a "fog layer".思路：把数据管理分布到整个 IoT 系统里，尽量靠近 IP 网络的边缘。任何有计算、存储和联网能力的设备都可以当雾节点（fog node），多了一个"雾层"。
  • Benefits: analysing data close to where it is generated → minimum latency; large amounts of traffic offloaded from the core network; sensitive data kept inside the local network.好处：在数据产生处附近分析 → 时延最小；把大量流量从核心网卸掉；敏感数据留在本地网络。
  • Also: fog nodes are close to the sensors and have contextual awareness, so they react to events faster, forming distributed edge control loops; they reduce the data before sending it upstream (p.108).还有：雾节点离传感器近，有上下文感知，能更快对事件作反应，形成分布式的边缘控制回路；上传前先做数据精简（p.108）。

The lecturer stressed the benefits of fog computing in class: distributed processing with no need to wait for a central server, so it is fast; data is reduced before upload; real-time processing is possible.老师课上强调雾计算的好处：分布式处理，不用等中心服务器，所以快；上传前先精简数据；能实时处理。

Pitfalls

  • Fog computing does not replace the cloud; the two complement each other (p.111). Do not write "the cloud is no longer needed".雾计算不取代云，二者互补（p.111）；别写成"不用云了"。

ExamHow to write it in English

Sending all IoT data to the cloud is a problem because: the bandwidth of last-mile IoT networks is very limited; latency can be very high, so real-time response is lost; the backhaul from the gateway can be unreliable, often depending on 3G/LTE or even satellite links; the volume of data on the backhaul is too high; and big data keeps growing, making real-time analysis almost impossible.

Fog computing distributes data management throughout the IoT system, as close to the network edge as possible. Any device with computing, storage and network connectivity can be a fog node. Analysing data close to where it is collected minimizes latency, offloads network traffic from the core network and keeps sensitive data inside the local network; the fog node is aware of the context of its sensors and can react to events quickly, and the data is reduced before being sent upstream.

In one line: sending everything to the cloud runs into little bandwidth, long latency, unreliable backhaul and too much data; fog computing processes data near the edge, cutting latency and traffic and keeping data local.一句话：全送云端会遇到带宽小、时延大、回程不可靠、数据太多；雾计算在边缘附近处理，降时延、减流量、数据留本地。
Concept + Step by step: five characteristics of fog computing

ConceptWhere fog nodes sit and what they do

A fog node is a device with compute, storage and network connectivity placed near the IoT endpoints (often in a gateway or router); it processes the data before it is sent to the cloud (p.106). Notes p.109 summarise its characteristics in five points. This was tested in the final, 2025-26 S1 Q4(c).雾节点是放在 IoT 终端附近的、有计算存储联网能力的设备（常见在网关、路由器里），在数据送到云之前先处理一遍（p.106）。讲义 p.109 把它的特点总结成五条。这一题 2025-26 S1 Q4(c) 期末考过。

Step by stepFive points, each with the "why"

  1. Contextual location awareness and low latency: fog nodes sit as close to the IoT endpoints as possible and know which sensors they serve; processing nearby makes them fast.上下文位置感知、低时延（contextual location awareness and low latency）：雾节点尽量靠近 IoT 终端，知道自己管的是哪些传感器，就近处理所以快。
  2. Geographic distribution: the services and applications that fog nodes serve need widely distributed deployment.地理上分布（geographic distribution）：雾节点服务的业务和应用需要大范围分散部署。
  3. Deployment near IoT endpoints: fog nodes are usually placed where there are large numbers of endpoints.部署在大量 IoT 终端附近（deployment near IoT endpoints）：通常有大量终端的地方才放雾节点。
  4. Wireless communication between the fog and the endpoints: one fog node must connect many endpoints, and wireless access scales most easily.雾与终端之间用无线通信（wireless communication）：一个雾节点要连大量终端，无线接入最容易扩展。
  5. Use for real-time interactions: preprocessing is done on the fog node, so upper-layer applications only need to batch-process part of the data.用于实时交互（use for real-time interactions）：在雾节点上先做预处理，上层应用只需对一部分数据做批处理。

The four benefits the lecturer stressed in class (fast, data reduced first, real time, wireless connection) all map onto these five points.老师课上强调的四个好处（快、先精简数据、实时、无线连接）都能对应到这五条里。

Pitfalls

  • "Characteristics" are not the same as "the problems fog computing solves" (b37). Do not answer with the list of little bandwidth, long latency and so on."特点"和"雾计算要解决的问题"（b37）不是一回事，别答成带宽小、时延大那一组。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) Contextual location awareness and low latency: the fog node sits as close to the IoT endpoints as possible to deliver distributed computing. (2) Geographic distribution: the services and applications targeted by fog nodes demand widely distributed deployments. (3) Deployment near IoT endpoints: fog nodes are typically deployed in the presence of a large number of IoT endpoints. (4) Wireless communication between the fog and the IoT endpoints: since a fog node deals with a large number of endpoints, wireless access is the easiest way to achieve scalability. (5) Use for real-time interactions: pre-processing at the fog nodes allows upper-layer applications to perform batch processing on only a subset of the data.

In one line: the five characteristics of fog computing are location awareness and low latency, geographic distribution, deployment near many endpoints, wireless connection to the endpoints, and use for real-time interactions.一句话：雾计算五特点：位置感知低时延、地理分布、靠近大量终端、与终端无线连接、用于实时交互。
Concept + Step by step: division of work between edge, fog and cloud

ConceptTiers by time sensitivity (p.110–113)

Edge (mist / edge) computing pushes fog one step further, into the IoT endpoint devices themselves: endpoints with compute power do initial analysis and filtering themselves (p.110). Edge, fog and cloud complement each other rather than replace one another (p.111): edge and fog are the first line of defence, filtering and analysing data so that not every event has to go to the cloud. Where data is processed depends on how urgent it is (p.113):边缘（mist / edge）计算：把雾再往前推，直接放进 IoT 终端设备本身，有算力的终端自己做初步分析和过滤（p.110）。边缘、雾、云互补而不是互相取代（p.111）：边缘和雾是第一道防线，过滤和分析数据，免得每个事件都去问云。数据去哪处理，看它多急（p.113）：

Time sensitivitySent to
Most sensitiveEdge, or the fog node closest to the device边缘或离设备最近的雾节点
Can wait seconds to minutes可以等几秒到几分钟Aggregation node
Not sensitiveCloud: historical analysis, big data analytics, long-term storage云：历史分析、大数据分析、长期存储

Option by option

  • A. Edge node: wrong. It is kept for the most urgent data.A. 边缘节点：错，留给最紧急的数据。
  • B. Nearest fog node: wrong. It is also for the most urgent data.B. 最近的雾节点：错，同样是给最紧急的数据。
  • C. Aggregation node: correct. p.113: "seconds or minutes … aggregation node".C. 汇聚节点：对，p.113 原文 "seconds or minutes … aggregation node"。
  • D. Cloud: wrong. The cloud handles historical data where time does not matter.D. 云端：错，云处理的是不在乎时间的历史数据。

Memory hook: the more urgent, the closer to the device: milliseconds at the edge / fog, seconds to minutes at the aggregation node, non-urgent data to the cloud.记忆：越急越靠近设备：毫秒级在边缘 / 雾，秒到分钟在汇聚，不急的上云。

In one line: C. Data that can wait seconds to minutes goes to the aggregation node.一句话：选 C：能等几秒到几分钟的数据送汇聚节点。
Concept + Step by step: altitudes of the three orbit types

ConceptAltitude decides everything

Satellites are classified into three types by altitude (notes Part C p.10): GEO (Geostationary Earth Orbit) 35,863 km; MEO (Medium Earth Orbit) 8,000–18,000 km; LEO (Low Earth Orbit) 500–1,500 km. The higher the orbit, the larger the area of ground the satellite sees and the slower it goes round, but the weaker the signal and the longer the delay. GPS uses 24 MEO satellites (p.9). The lecturer stressed in class: GEO is about 36,000 km above the earth, so earth stations must use high-gain antennas.卫星按高度分三类（讲义 Part C p.10）：GEO（地球静止轨道，Geostationary Earth Orbit）35,863 km；MEO（中轨，Medium Earth Orbit）8,000–18,000 km；LEO（低轨，Low Earth Orbit）500–1,500 km。越高，看到的地面越大、绕一圈越慢，但信号越弱、时延越大。GPS 用的是 24 颗 MEO（p.9）。老师课上强调：GEO 离地约 36,000 km，所以地面站必须用高增益天线。

Option by optionThe four options

  • A correct: all three numbers match p.10 exactly.A 对：三个数字和 p.10 完全一致。
  • B is wrong: GEO has a single altitude, 35,863 km; 20,000 km is a little above the MEO range given in the notes (8,000–18,000 km) (beyond the slides: GPS satellites at about 20,200 km are usually counted as MEO too); 100 km is too low — atmospheric drag would bring the satellite down quickly.B 错：GEO 只有一个高度 35,863 km；20,000 km 比讲义给的 MEO 范围（8,000–18,000 km）还高一点（课外补充：GPS 卫星约 20,200 km，通常也归为 MEO）；100 km 太低，大气阻力会让卫星很快掉下来。
  • C wrong: GEO is right, but the MEO and LEO ranges are both too low; the notes' lower limit for LEO is 500 km.C 错：GEO 对，但 MEO、LEO 的范围都写低了；讲义 LEO 下限是 500 km。
  • D wrong: 42,000 km is the GEO orbital radius measured from the earth's centre (6,370 + 35,863 = 42,233 km), not the altitude above the ground.D 错：42,000 km 是 GEO 到地心的轨道半径（6,370 + 35,863 = 42,233 km），不是离地高度。

Memory hookRhyme

"Low one thousand, medium ten thousand, geostationary thirty-six thousand": LEO is of the order of 1,000 km, MEO of the order of 10,000 km, GEO about 36,000 km."低一千、中一万、静止三万六"：LEO 约 1,000 km 量级，MEO 约 10,000 km 量级，GEO 约 36,000 km。

In one line: GEO 35,863 km, MEO 8,000–18,000 km, LEO 500–1,500 km, so A; 42,000 km is the orbital radius, do not confuse them.一句话：GEO 35,863 km，MEO 8,000–18,000 km，LEO 500–1,500 km，选 A；42,000 km 是轨道半径，别混。
Concept + Step by step: orbits classified by shape and inclination

ConceptThree dimensions that describe an orbit

Notes Part C p.10–11 describe a satellite orbit along three dimensions: altitude (GEO / MEO / LEO, see c1), shape and inclination. This question asks about the last two.讲义 Part C p.10–11 用三个维度描述卫星轨道：高度（GEO / MEO / LEO，见 c1）、形状（shape）和倾角（inclination）。本题问后两个。

DimensionClassesKey point
ShapeCircularCentre at the earth's centre; constant altitude圆心在地心，高度不变
ShapeEllipticalThe earth's centre is at one focus of the ellipse; the altitude varies地心在椭圆的一个焦点上，高度时高时低
InclinationEquatorialThe orbital plane is the equatorial plane轨道面就是赤道面
InclinationPolarPasses over both poles经过南北两极
InclinationInclinedAll other inclinations其他所有倾角

Step by stepWhy classify this way

  1. Shape decides whether the satellite's distance from the ground changes: on a circular orbit, signal loss and delay stay constant; on an elliptical orbit the satellite moves slowly near apogee, so it can stay over a region for a long time.形状决定卫星离地距离是否变化：圆轨道上信号损耗、时延都稳定；椭圆轨道在远地点走得慢，可以在某地区上空停留较久。
  2.
