Inclination decides which latitudes the satellite passes over: an equatorial orbit always stays above the equator, so high-latitude regions see it at a very low elevation angle; a polar orbit passes over both poles on every revolution, and as the earth rotates underneath, a few revolutions sweep the whole globe.倾角决定卫星能飞过哪些纬度：赤道轨道永远只在赤道上空，高纬度地区仰角很低；极轨道每圈都经过两极，地球在下面自转，几圈下来可以扫过全球。
  3. GEO = circular orbit + equatorial orbit + 35,863 km. All three conditions are needed; otherwise the satellite would not be "stationary" relative to the ground (p.15).GEO = 圆轨道 + 赤道轨道 + 35,863 km，三个条件缺一不可，否则卫星相对地面不会"静止"（p.15）。

Beyond the slides(not in the notes)

Polar orbits are often used for earth imaging and weather satellites; highly inclined elliptical orbits (such as the Russian Molniya orbit) serve high-latitude regions that GEO covers poorly.极轨道常用于对地成像、气象卫星；高倾角椭圆轨道（如俄罗斯的 Molniya 轨道）用来照顾 GEO 覆盖不好的高纬度地区。

Pitfalls

  • An elliptical orbit has "one focus at the earth's centre", not "its centre at the earth's centre".椭圆轨道是"一个焦点在地心"，不是"中心在地心"。
  • Inclined orbits are "all orbits other than equatorial and polar ones"; do not give only two classes.倾斜轨道是"除赤道、极轨道以外的其他轨道"，不要只答两类。

ExamHow to write it in English

By shape: (1) circular orbit, with the centre of the circle at the earth's centre; (2) elliptical orbit, with one focus at the earth's centre. By inclination: (1) equatorial orbit, directly above the earth's equator; (2) polar orbit, passing over both poles; (3) all other orbits are called inclined orbits. (A GEO satellite uses a circular equatorial orbit at 35,863 km.)

In one line: by shape, circular (centre at the earth's centre) and elliptical (one focus at the earth's centre); by inclination, equatorial, polar and inclined.一句话：形状分圆（圆心在地心）和椭圆（一个焦点在地心）；倾角分赤道、极轨道和倾斜轨道。
Concept + Step by step: elevation angle and coverage angle

ConceptTwo angles locate the satellite

Notes Part C p.12–13: the position of a satellite in the sky is described by two angles.讲义 Part C p.12–13：卫星在天空中的位置用两个角度描述。

  • Elevation angle θ: standing at the earth station, the angle from the horizontal (the tangent to the earth's surface at the antenna) up to the centre of the antenna's main beam (with the antenna pointing straight at the satellite). θ = 90° is directly overhead; θ = 0° is along the horizon.仰角 θ（elevation angle）：站在地面站，从水平线（地表在天线处的切线）抬头到天线主瓣中心（天线正对卫星）的夹角。θ = 90° 是正头顶，θ = 0° 是贴着地平线。
  • Coverage angle β: how much of the earth's surface the satellite can see at the minimum elevation angle, expressed as the angle subtended at the earth's centre.覆盖角 β（coverage angle）：在最小仰角下，卫星能看到的那部分地球表面有多大，用地心处张开的角度表示。

The relation between them (derived from the geometry on p.13; the notes give no formula): cos(θ + β) = R·cos θ / (R + h), where R is the earth's radius and h is the satellite altitude. The smaller the minimum elevation angle θ, the larger β.两者的关系（由 p.13 的几何图推出，讲义没写公式）：cos(θ + β) = R·cos θ / (R + h)，R 是地球半径，h 是卫星高度。最小仰角 θ 越小，β 越大。

Step by stepThe answer points, one by one

  1. Elevation angle: say clearly "from where to where": from the tangent to the earth's surface at the earth station up to the centre of the antenna's main beam pointing at the satellite. Writing only "the angle the antenna is raised" loses marks.仰角：要说清"从哪里量到哪里"——从地面站处的地表切线量到天线指向卫星的主瓣中心。只写"天线抬起的角度"会丢分。
  2. Coverage angle: the key phrase is "the part of the earth's surface visible to the satellite at the minimum elevation angle".覆盖角：关键词是"在最小仰角下卫星可见的地表部分"。
  3. Ideal minimum elevation angle = 0°: with the elevation lower limit at 0°, earth stations far from the sub-satellite point can still see the satellite, and coverage extends all the way to the satellite's optical horizon, giving maximum coverage (p.12).理想最小仰角 = 0°：仰角下限放到 0°，离星下点很远的地面站也能看到卫星，覆盖一直延伸到卫星的光学地平线（optical horizon），覆盖最大（p.12）。
  4. 0° is not used in practice: the lower the elevation angle, the thicker the atmosphere the signal passes through, and rain, fog and atmospheric absorption all increase sharply (p.21, p.23), so 5°–10° is used in practice.实际不用 0°：仰角越低，信号穿过的大气越厚，雨、雾、大气吸收都大增（p.21、p.23），所以实际取 5°–10°。
GEO, θ = 0°: cos β = 6370 / 42233 = 0.1508 → β = 81.3°
GEO, θ = 10°: cos(θ + β) = 6370 × 0.9848 / 42233 = 0.1485 → θ + β = 81.46° → β = 71.46°
Coverage diameter ≈ 2βR: about 18,000 km at 0°, about 15,900 km at 10° (≈ the 16,000 km in the table on notes p.14)GEO，θ = 0°：cos β = 6370 / 42233 = 0.1508 → β = 81.3°
GEO，θ = 10°：cos(θ + β) = 6370 × 0.9848 / 42233 = 0.1485 → θ + β = 81.46° → β = 71.46°
覆盖直径 ≈ 2βR：0° 时约 18,000 km，10° 时约 15,900 km（≈ 讲义 p.14 表里的 16,000 km）

Pitfalls

  • The elevation angle is measured at the earth station; the coverage angle is measured at the earth's centre. Do not draw them in the wrong place.仰角在地面站处量，覆盖角在地心处量，别画错位置。
  • "Ideally 0°" is for maximum coverage; it does not mean 0° is best in practice. Write both sentences to show the trade-off."理想 0°"是为了覆盖最大，不代表实际最好；两句都要写，体现权衡。

ExamHow to write it in English

Elevation angle θ is the angle from the horizontal (the line tangent to the earth's surface at the antenna's location) to the centre of the antenna's main beam when the antenna points directly at the satellite. Coverage angle β is the measure of the portion of the earth's surface visible to the satellite with the minimum elevation angle. To obtain maximum coverage, a minimum elevation angle of 0° is preferred, so that the coverage extends to the satellite's optical horizon in all directions. In practice a few degrees (e.g. 5°–10°) is used, because at low elevation the signal passes through more atmosphere and suffers larger attenuation.

In one line: the elevation angle is measured at the earth station (from the tangent to the satellite direction); the coverage angle is measured at the earth's centre (the surface visible at the minimum elevation angle); the ideal minimum elevation angle is 0°, giving coverage to the optical horizon.一句话：仰角在地面站量（切线到卫星方向），覆盖角在地心量（最小仰角下可见的地表）；理想最小仰角 0°，覆盖到光学地平线。
Concept + Step by step: GEO propagation delay

ConceptDelay = distance ÷ speed of light

Radio waves travel in a vacuum at the speed of light, c = 3×10⁸ m/s = 300,000 km/s. Propagation delay t = d / c. In satellite communication the signal goes up from one earth station to the satellite and, after the satellite relays it, down to another earth station, so the path has two legs, "up + down". Notes Part C p.16: with both stations directly below the satellite, the "round-trip propagation delay" is 0.24 s; the table on p.14 gives a GEO round-trip delay of about 250 ms. Here "round trip" means one trip via the satellite (ground → satellite → ground).无线电波在真空中以光速 c = 3×10⁸ m/s = 300,000 km/s 传播。传播时延 t = d / c。卫星通信里，信号从一个地面站上行到卫星，卫星转发后再下行到另一个地面站，所以路程是"上 + 下"两段。讲义 Part C p.16：两地都在卫星正下方时，"round-trip propagation delay"是 0.24 s；p.14 表里 GEO 往返时延约 250 ms。这里的"往返"指经卫星走一趟（地 → 星 → 地）。

Step by stepWork it out step by step

  1. What: find the path length. Why: both stations are near the point directly below the satellite, so the slant range ≈ the altitude h.做什么：求路程。为什么：两站都在卫星正下方附近，斜距 ≈ 高度 h。
  2. What: divide by the speed of light. Watch out: use km and km/s consistently.做什么：除以光速。注意单位统一用 km 和 km/s。
d = 2 × 35,863 km = 71,726 km
t = 71,726 km ÷ 300,000 km/s = 0.239 s ≈ 0.24 s

Sanity check: this matches the 0.24 s on notes p.16. If an earth station is at the edge of coverage (elevation 10°), the slant range is about 40,660 km and one trip takes about 0.27 s, so the table's "about 250 ms" is a typical value. In a phone call, a question and its answer pass through the satellite twice, about 0.48 s, which is a clearly noticeable pause.合理性检查：和讲义 p.16 的 0.24 s 一致。如果地面站在覆盖边缘（仰角 10°），斜距约 40,660 km，一趟约 0.27 s，所以表里写"约 250 ms"是个典型值。打电话"一问一答"要经过卫星两趟，约 0.48 s，能明显感觉到停顿。

Pitfalls

  • Computing only one leg, 35,863 km, and getting 0.12 s: you missed the downlink leg.只算单程 35,863 km 得 0.12 s：漏了下行那一段。
  • Reading "round trip" as a conversation there and back and multiplying by 2 again to get 0.48 s: the notes' 0.24 s means one trip ground → satellite → ground.把 "round trip" 理解成对话一来一回再乘 2 得 0.48 s：讲义的 0.24 s 指地 → 星 → 地一趟。
  • Mixing km and m: off by a factor of 1000.

ExamHow to write it in English

Path length = uplink + downlink = 2 × 35,863 km = 71,726 km. Propagation delay t = d / c = 71,726 km / (3 × 10⁵ km/s) ≈ 0.239 s ≈ 0.24 s.

In one line: uplink + downlink total 71,726 km; divided by 3×10⁵ km/s, this is about 0.239 s.一句话：上行 + 下行共 71,726 km，除以 3×10⁵ km/s，约 0.239 s。
Concept + Step by step: GEO coverage angle

ConceptStarting from the geometry on p.13 (beyond the slides)

Notes Part C p.13 only gives the figure; the formula is added for this question. Draw triangle O–E–S: O is the earth's centre, E the earth station, S the satellite. OE = R (earth radius), OS = R + h. At elevation θ = 0°, the station's line of sight to the satellite just grazes the earth's surface and is perpendicular to the radius OE, so the triangle has a right angle at E. In this right triangle, the side adjacent to β is R and the hypotenuse is R + h:讲义 Part C p.13 只画了图，公式是本题补充的。画三角形 O–E–S：O 是地心，E 是地面站，S 是卫星。OE = R（地球半径），OS = R + h。仰角 θ = 0° 时，地面站看卫星的视线正好贴着地表，和半径 OE 垂直，所以三角形在 E 处是直角。直角三角形里，β 的邻边是 R，斜边是 R + h：

cos β = R / (R + h)

For a general elevation angle the formula is cos(θ + β) = R·cos θ / (R + h); at θ = 0° it reduces to the formula above.一般仰角时公式是 cos(θ + β) = R·cos θ / (R + h)，θ = 0° 时就退化成上式。

Step by stepWork it out step by step

  1. Find R + h: the distance from the satellite to the earth's centre.求 R + h：卫星到地心的距离。
  2. Find cos β, then use cos⁻¹ on the calculator (make sure the calculator is in DEG mode).求 cos β，再用计算器 cos⁻¹（注意计算器在 DEG 模式）。
  3. Convert to a ground diameter: arc length = radius × angle (in radians), so the coverage diameter = 2βR.换成地面直径：弧长 = 半径 × 角度（弧度），覆盖区直径 = 2βR。
R + h = 6,370 + 35,863 = 42,233 km
cos β = 6,370 / 42,233 = 0.1508
β = cos⁻¹ 0.1508 = 81.3°
Diameter ≈ 2 × (81.3° × π/180) × 6,370 = 2 × 1.419 × 6,370 ≈ 18,000 km

Sanity check: β must be less than 90° (a satellite cannot see more than half of the earth), so 81.3° is reasonable. The table on notes p.14 gives a GEO coverage diameter of about 16,000 km, which is computed at a minimum elevation of 10° (β = 71.46°, diameter about 15,900 km), so the two numbers do not contradict each other.合理性检查：β 必须小于 90°（卫星不可能看到半个地球以上），81.3° 合理。讲义 p.14 表里 GEO 覆盖直径约 16,000 km，是按最小仰角 10° 算的（β = 71.46°，直径约 15,900 km），两个数不矛盾。

Beyond the slidesWhere "1/4 of the earth" comes from

Notes p.15 say one GEO covers "¼ of the earth". Geometrically, the visible spherical cap is a fraction (1 − cos β)/2 of the earth's surface: about 42% at 0° elevation and about 34% at 10° elevation (the commonly quoted "about 1/3"). The notes' 1/4 is a conservative figure; in the exam, write what the notes say. Three GEOs spaced 120° apart together cover almost the whole globe except the poles (p.15).讲义 p.15 说一颗 GEO 覆盖 "¼ of the earth"。按几何，可见的球冠面积占地球表面 (1 − cos β)/2：仰角 0° 时约 42%，仰角 10° 时约 34%（这就是常说的"约 1/3"）。讲义的 1/4 是偏保守的说法，考试照讲义写即可。三颗相隔 120° 的 GEO 拼起来覆盖除两极外的几乎全球（p.15）。

Pitfalls

  • Using cos β = R / h (forgetting to add R): this gives cos β = 0.178, and β comes out too small.用 cos β = R / h（忘了加 R）：得到 cos β = 0.178，β 偏小。
  • Calculator in RAD mode: cos⁻¹ gives 1.419, which is then taken as degrees.计算器在 RAD 模式，cos⁻¹ 得 1.419 却当成度。
  • For the diameter, multiplying β in degrees directly by R without converting to radians.直径用 β 的度数直接乘 R，没换成弧度。

ExamHow to write it in English

At 0° elevation the line of sight is tangent to the earth, so it is perpendicular to the earth radius at the earth station. Hence cos β = R / (R + h) = 6,370 / (6,370 + 35,863) = 0.1508, giving β ≈ 81.3°. The coverage diameter on the ground is about 2βR ≈ 18,000 km.

In one line: at 0° elevation the line of sight is perpendicular to the radius, cos β = 6370/42233 = 0.1508, β ≈ 81.3°, coverage diameter about 18,000 km.一句话：仰角 0° 时视线垂直于半径，cos β = 6370/42233 = 0.1508，β ≈ 81.3°，覆盖直径约 18,000 km。
Concept + Step by step: pros and cons of GEO

ConceptWhy GEO is "stationary"

A GEO satellite is on a circular orbit 35,863 km above the equator and turns at the same rate as the earth rotates, so it appears to stay fixed above one point on the equator (notes Part C p.15). Advantages (p.15): almost no motion relative to the ground, so little Doppler shift; simple tracking for earth stations; large coverage, with 3 satellites 120° apart covering almost the whole globe. Disadvantages (p.16): the signal is weak after travelling over 35,000 km; poor service to polar and high-latitude regions; long delay (round trip 0.24 s); large beams waste spectrum for point-to-point communication.GEO 在赤道上空 35,863 km 的圆轨道上，转速和地球自转一样，看上去始终停在赤道某点正上方（讲义 Part C p.15）。优点（p.15）：相对地面几乎不动，多普勒频移（Doppler shift）影响小；地面站跟踪简单；覆盖大，3 颗相隔 120° 就几乎覆盖全球。缺点（p.16）：信号走 35,000 多公里后很弱；极地和高纬度地区服务差；时延大（往返 0.24 s）；大波束做点对点通信浪费频谱。

Option by optionFind the one that is "not a characteristic"

  • A is a characteristic: the satellite does not move relative to the ground, so once the antenna is pointed it hardly needs to move.A 是特点：卫星相对地面不动，天线对准后基本不用动。
  • B is a characteristic: with no relative motion there is almost no Doppler shift.B 是特点：没有相对运动，就几乎没有多普勒频移。
  • C is a characteristic: the table on p.14 gives a GEO round-trip delay of about 250 ms (p.16 says 0.24 s).C 是特点：p.14 表里 GEO 往返时延约 250 ms（p.16 写 0.24 s）。
  • D is not a characteristic; choose it: GEO is above the equator. The closer an earth station is to the poles, the lower its elevation angle to the satellite and the thicker the atmosphere the signal passes through; it may not see the satellite at all. So high-latitude coverage is poor, which is a disadvantage.D 不是特点，选它：GEO 在赤道上空，越往两极，地面站看卫星的仰角越低，信号穿过的大气越厚，甚至看不到卫星。所以高纬度覆盖差，是缺点。

Memory hook

"A light bulb over the equator": it lights up the equatorial region well, but at the poles it sits almost on the horizon and cannot reach them."赤道上的灯泡"：照赤道附近亮，照两极几乎贴着地平线，照不到。

In one line: GEO is above the equator; at the poles and high latitudes the elevation angle is too low and coverage is poor, so D is not one of its characteristics.一句话：GEO 在赤道上空，极地和高纬度仰角太低、覆盖差，所以 D 不是它的特点。
Concept + Step by step: LEO problems, advantages and classes

ConceptWhy LEO is both good and troublesome

LEO is only 500–1,500 km high. Being close to the ground gives a strong signal and low delay; but it also means the satellite moves fast (about 7 km/s, 1.5–2 hours per orbit) and each satellite is visible for only 15–20 minutes (notes Part C p.14), so a whole fleet of satellites must take over from one another. Notes p.17 cover the problems, p.18 the advantages, and p.19 Little / Big LEO.LEO 只有 500–1,500 km 高，离地近，所以信号强、时延小；但离地近也意味着飞得快（约 7 km/s，1.5–2 小时绕一圈）、一颗只能看到 15–20 分钟（讲义 Part C p.14），所以要一大群卫星接力。讲义 p.17 讲问题，p.18 讲优点，p.19 讲 Little / Big LEO。

Step by stepThe answer points, one by one

Problems (p.17)

  1. Large Doppler shift: the satellite moves fast relative to the ground, so the received frequency is shifted and the receiver must track it. Estimate beyond the slides: a LEO at 1,000 km moves at about 7.35 km/s; at a 2 GHz carrier the maximum shift f·v/c ≈ 49 kHz, far more than the few hundred Hz seen by terrestrial phones.多普勒频移大：卫星相对地面高速运动，收到的频率会偏移，接收机必须跟踪。课外估算：1,000 km 高的 LEO 速度约 7.35 km/s，2 GHz 载频最大偏移 f·v/c ≈ 49 kHz，远大于地面手机的几百 Hz。
  2. Atmospheric drag is significant, so the orbit gradually decays and the satellite's lifetime is limited.大气阻力（atmospheric drag）明显，轨道逐渐衰退，卫星寿命有限。
  3. Multiple orbital planes, each with multiple satellites, are needed for continuous coverage.要多个轨道面、每面多颗卫星才能连续覆盖。
  4. Communication between two places often requires handing the signal over from one satellite to another.两地通信常要把信号从一颗卫星切换到另一颗。

Advantages (p.18)

  1. For the same transmit power, the received signal is much stronger than with GEO. Estimate beyond the slides: the free-space loss differs only in the distance term, 20 log(35,863 / 1,000) ≈ 31 dB.同样发射功率下，收到的信号比 GEO 强得多。课外估算：自由空间损耗只差距离项 20 log(35,863 / 1,000) ≈ 31 dB。
  2. Coverage is more local, so spectrum can be reused in different regions, which saves spectrum.覆盖更局部，频谱可以在不同地区复用，更省频谱。
  3. Suits handheld / mobile terminals, which need a strong signal.适合需要强信号的手持 / 移动终端。
  4. The price: many satellites are needed for 24-hour coverage.代价：要 24 小时全覆盖需要很多颗卫星。
Little LEOBig LEO
FrequencyBelow 1 GHzAbove 1 GHz
Bandwidth / data rateLess than 5 MHz, up to 10 kbpsUp to a few Mbps
ServicesPaging, tracking, low-rate messaging寻呼、跟踪、低速消息All Little LEO services + voice, positioningLittle LEO 全部业务 + 话音、定位

Pitfalls

  • The Little / Big boundary is the frequency of 1 GHz, not the satellite's size or altitude.Little / Big 的分界是频率 1 GHz，不是卫星大小或高度。
  • Big LEO is "Little LEO services plus voice and positioning", not a separate set of services.Big LEO 是"在 Little LEO 的基础上加上话音和定位"，不是另一套业务。

ExamHow to write it in English

Problems: (1) the satellite moves fast relative to the ground, so the system must cope with large Doppler shifts; (2) atmospheric drag is significant, causing gradual orbital deterioration; (3) multiple orbital planes, each with multiple satellites, are needed; (4) communication between two earth stations usually involves handing off from one satellite to another. Advantages: the received signal is much stronger than a GEO signal for the same transmit power; coverage is more localised so spectrum is better conserved; suitable for mobile and personal terminals. Little LEOs operate below 1 GHz with less than 5 MHz bandwidth and up to 10 kbps, for paging, tracking and low-rate messaging. Big LEOs operate above 1 GHz with data rates up to a few Mbps, offering the Little-LEO services plus voice and positioning.

In one line: LEO is close, so the signal is strong, it saves spectrum and suits handhelds; but the Doppler shift is large, there is atmospheric drag, and it needs many satellites and frequent handovers. Little LEO is below 1 GHz with up to 10 kbps; Big LEO is above 1 GHz with up to a few Mbps and adds voice and positioning.一句话：LEO 近所以信号强、省频谱、适合手持，但多普勒大、有大气阻力、要很多卫星和频繁切换；Little LEO 在 1 GHz 以下、10 kbps，Big LEO 在 1 GHz 以上、几 Mbps 并加上话音和定位。
Concept + Step by step: MEO vs LEO

ConceptMEO is a compromise between LEO and GEO

MEO is 8,000–18,000 km high (notes Part C p.10), and each satellite is visible for 2–8 hours, against only 15–20 minutes for LEO (p.14). So MEO has far fewer handovers; but being farther away, its propagation delay and required power are greater than LEO's; it needs fewer satellites than LEO (p.20). Uses: digital voice, data, fax and messaging; GPS uses 24 MEO satellites (p.9).MEO 高 8,000–18,000 km（讲义 Part C p.10），每颗可见 2–8 小时，LEO 只有 15–20 分钟（p.14）。所以 MEO 切换少得多；但离地更远，传播时延和所需功率比 LEO 大；需要的卫星数比 LEO 少（p.20）。用途：数字话音、数据、传真、消息；GPS 就是 24 颗 MEO（p.9）。

Option by option

  • A wrong: exactly the reverse. The higher the satellite, the longer each one is visible and the fewer the handovers.A 错：正好反了。卫星越高，每颗看得越久，切换越少。
  • B correct: matches the wording on p.20: "much fewer handoffs", "propagation delay … and the power required are greater than those of LEOs".B 对：和 p.20 原话一致："much fewer handoffs"，"propagation delay … and the power required are greater than those of LEOs"。
  • C wrong: MEO is higher; its delay is tens of ms, against only a few ms for LEO (p.14).C 错：MEO 更高，时延是几十 ms，LEO 只有几 ms（p.14）。
  • D wrong: GPS is precisely an MEO navigation system.D 错：GPS 正是 MEO 导航系统。

Memory hook

"Higher is steadier, higher is farther": going up, there are fewer handovers and fewer satellites (steadier), but the delay and power increase (farther)."越高越稳、越高越远"：高度往上走，切换少、卫星少（稳）；时延和功率大（远）。

In one line: MEO has far fewer handovers than LEO, but larger delay and required power, so B.一句话：MEO 比 LEO 切换少得多，但时延和所需功率更大，选 B。
Concept + Step by step: LEO visibility per pass

ConceptThe orbit parameter table on notes p.14

ParameterLEOMEOGEO
Period1.5–2 h5–10 h24 h
Visible per pass15–20 min2–8 hPermanent
Round-trip delayA few msTens of msAbout 250 ms
Coverage diameter (10° elevation)覆盖直径（仰角 10°）About 6,000 km12,000–15,000 kmAbout 16,000 km

Why is a LEO visible for only 15–20 minutes? Beyond the slides: from Kepler's third law T = 2π√(a³/μ), a LEO at 500 km has a period of about 1.57 h and a speed of about 7.6 km/s. One orbit takes just over 90 minutes, and each pass from rising above the horizon to setting covers only a small part of it, so each pass lasts only ten-odd minutes.为什么 LEO 只能看 15–20 分钟？课外补充：由开普勒第三定律 T = 2π√(a³/μ)，500 km 高的 LEO 周期约 1.57 h、速度约 7.6 km/s。一圈 90 多分钟，每次从地平线升起到落下只占其中一小段，所以每次可见十几分钟。

Option by option

  • A correct: the LEO row of the table.
  • B wrong: 2–8 hours is MEO.
  • C wrong: always visible is GEO (permanently visible).C 错：一直可见的是 GEO（永久可见）。
  • D wrong: a few seconds is far too short; however fast a LEO is, it takes over ten minutes to cross the sky.D 错：几秒太短，LEO 再快也要十几分钟才飞过天空。
In one line: each LEO pass lasts about 15–20 minutes (MEO 2–8 hours, GEO permanent), so A.一句话：LEO 每次过顶约 15–20 分钟（MEO 2–8 小时，GEO 永久），选 A。
Concept + Step by step: three factors in link quality

ConceptWhere the signal loses power on the way

Notes Part C p.21–23 list three factors that affect satellite link performance. The lecturer stressed in class that these three factors are very important; he said he "must emphasise" them. The idea is the three reasons the signal is "weakened" on its way from the satellite antenna to the earth-station antenna: distance, being off the beam centre and the atmosphere.讲义 Part C p.21–23 列出影响卫星链路性能的三大因素。老师课上强调：这三个因素非常重要，他"必须强调"。思路就是从卫星天线到地面站天线，信号沿路被"削弱"的三个原因：距离、偏离波束中心、大气。

Step by stepThe three factors, one by one

  1. Distance between the satellite antenna and the earth-station antenna: free-space loss L(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log f(MHz) + 20 log d(km). So the higher the frequency and the higher the satellite, the larger the loss (p.21, figure on p.22). Example beyond the slides: for the same GEO, Ku at 12 GHz loses 20 log 3 ≈ 9.5 dB more than C band at 4 GHz; a GEO loses about 31 dB more than a LEO at 1,000 km.卫星天线和地面站天线之间的距离：自由空间损耗 L(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log f(MHz) + 20 log d(km)。所以频率越高、卫星越高，损耗越大（p.21，p.22 的图）。课外举例：同一颗 GEO，Ku 12 GHz 比 C 4 GHz 多损耗 20 log 3 ≈ 9.5 dB；GEO 比 1,000 km 的 LEO 多损耗约 31 dB。
  2. For the downlink, the ground distance between the earth station and the satellite's "aim point": the satellite beam is aimed at a point on the ground; the centre of the coverage area receives the most power, and the power gets weaker towards the edge. So, for the same satellite, users at the edge of coverage need larger antennas.下行时地面站离卫星"瞄准点"（aim point）的地面距离：卫星波束对准地面某一点，覆盖区中心功率最高，越往边缘越弱。所以同一颗卫星，覆盖边缘的用户需要更大的天线。
  3. Atmospheric attenuation: affected by oxygen, water vapour, elevation angle and frequency. The smaller the elevation angle, the thicker the atmosphere the signal passes through and the larger the attenuation; higher frequencies suffer more (p.21, p.23). Beyond the slides: at 5° elevation the path through the atmosphere is about 5.7 times that at 30° (estimated with 1/sin θ).大气衰减：受氧气、水汽、仰角和频率影响。仰角越小，信号穿过的大气越厚，衰减越大；频率越高越严重（p.21、p.23）。课外：仰角 5° 时穿过大气的路程约为 30° 时的 5.7 倍（按 1/sin θ 估算）。
Frequency term: 20 log(12/4) = 9.5 dB
Distance term: 20 log(35,863 / 1,000) = 31.1 dB
Atmospheric path ratio (flat-earth approximation): sin 30° / sin 5° = 0.5 / 0.0872 ≈ 5.7频率项：20 log(12/4) = 9.5 dB
距离项：20 log(35,863 / 1,000) = 31.1 dB
大气路程比（平地近似）：sin 30° / sin 5° = 0.5 / 0.0872 ≈ 5.7

Pitfalls

  • The second factor applies only to the downlink; write "For downlink" in your answer.第二个因素只在下行时讲，答题时把"For downlink"写上。
  • For the first factor, write both directions: "the higher the frequency" and "the higher the satellite".第一个因素要同时写"频率越高"和"卫星越高"两个方向。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) Distance between the satellite antenna and the earth-station antenna: the higher the signal frequency and the higher the satellite, the greater the signal power loss. (2) For the downlink, the terrestrial distance between the earth-station antenna and the "aim point" of the satellite: the centre of the coverage area receives the highest power, and the power drops off away from the centre. (3) Atmospheric attenuation: affected by oxygen, water, the elevation angle and frequency; the smaller the elevation angle, the more atmosphere the signal must travel through, and higher frequencies suffer more.

In one line: distance (higher frequency and higher satellite mean more loss), distance from the aim point on the downlink (strongest at the centre), and atmospheric attenuation (lower elevation and higher frequency mean more attenuation).一句话：距离（频率高、卫星高损耗大）、下行时离瞄准点的距离（中心最强）、大气衰减（仰角低、频率高衰减大）。
Concept + Step by step: GEO free-space loss

ConceptFree-space loss formula

Free-space path loss comes from the Friis formula: L = (4πd/λ)². In dB, with f in MHz and d in km and the constants combined, it becomes:自由空间损耗（free-space path loss）来自 Friis 公式：L = (4πd/λ)²。换成 dB，并把 f 用 MHz、d 用 km 表示，常数合在一起就是：

L(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log₁₀ f(MHz) + 20 log₁₀ d(km)

Symbols: f is the carrier frequency (MHz) and d is the transmitter–receiver distance (km). Rule: each tenfold increase in f or d adds 20 dB of loss. Part A notes p.51 give the constant as 32 (rounded); this question uses 32.44. The figure on notes Part C p.22 is a plot of this formula (four parallel lines for 1, 4, 10 and 40 GHz).每个符号：f 是载波频率（MHz），d 是收发距离（km）。规律：f 或 d 每增加 10 倍，损耗多 20 dB。Part A 讲义 p.51 写的常数是 32（取整），本题用 32.44。讲义 Part C p.22 的图就是这条公式画出来的（1、4、10、40 GHz 四条平行线）。

Step by stepWork it out step by step

  1. Convert units: 4 GHz = 4,000 MHz (the formula needs MHz; plugging in 4 gives an error of 60 dB).换单位：4 GHz = 4,000 MHz（公式要求 MHz，填 4 会差 60 dB）。
  2. Compute the two log terms. Calculator tip: log 4000 = log 4 + 3 = 0.602 + 3 = 3.602.算两个对数项。计算器提示：log 4000 = log 4 + 3 = 0.602 + 3 = 3.602。
  3. Add the three terms.
20 log 4,000 = 20 × 3.602 = 72.04 dB
20 log 35,863 = 20 × 4.555 = 91.09 dB
L = 32.44 + 72.04 + 91.09 = 195.6 dB
(with the constant 32: L = 195.1 dB, also accepted)20 log 4,000 = 20 × 3.602 = 72.04 dB
20 log 35,863 = 20 × 4.555 = 91.09 dB
L = 32.44 + 72.04 + 91.09 = 195.6 dB
（常数用 32：L = 195.1 dB，也算对）

Sanity check: the figure on p.22 shows about 196 dB at 4 GHz and GEO altitude, which agrees. For comparison: at the same 4 GHz, a LEO at 1,000 km has only 164.5 dB, about 31 dB less; the same GEO at 1 GHz has 183.5 dB.合理性检查：p.22 图上 4 GHz、GEO 高度处约 196 dB，吻合。对比：同样 4 GHz、1,000 km 的 LEO 只有 164.5 dB，差约 31 dB；同一颗 GEO 用 1 GHz 是 183.5 dB。

Pitfalls

  • Plugging in f in GHz: 20 log 4 = 12.04, which is 60 dB too little.
  • Plugging in d in m: 60 dB too much.
  • Using 10 log instead of 20 log: the power ratio is proportional to the square of the distance and the square of the frequency, so it is 20 log.用 10 log 代替 20 log：功率与距离平方、频率平方成正比，所以是 20 log。

ExamHow to write it in English

L(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log₁₀(4000) + 20 log₁₀(35,863) = 32.44 + 72.04 + 91.09 ≈ 195.6 dB.

In one line: 32.44 + 72.04 + 91.09 ≈ 195.6 dB, with f in MHz and d in km.
Concept + Step by step: elevation angle and rain/fog attenuation

ConceptThe lower the elevation, the thicker the atmosphere crossed

The atmosphere is only a dozen or so km thick. When the satellite is overhead (90° elevation), the signal goes straight through the atmosphere and the path is shortest; the lower the elevation angle, the more obliquely the signal crosses the atmosphere, the longer the path, and the more it is absorbed and scattered by oxygen, water vapour, rain and fog (notes Part C p.21). The figure on p.23 shows how three kinds of attenuation, atmospheric absorption, fog and rain, vary with elevation angle: all fall quickly as the elevation angle rises and increase sharply below 10°, and rain has the largest effect.大气层大约只有十几公里厚。卫星在头顶（仰角 90°）时，信号笔直穿过大气，路程最短；仰角越低，信号斜着穿过大气，路程越长，氧气、水汽、雨、雾对它的吸收和散射也越多（讲义 Part C p.21）。p.23 的图画了大气吸收、雾、雨三种衰减随仰角的变化：都随仰角升高而迅速下降，仰角低于 10° 时急剧增大，雨的影响最大。

Beyond the slides (flat-earth approximation): the path through the atmosphere ∝ 1/sin θ. sin 30° / sin 5° = 0.5 / 0.0872 ≈ 5.7, so going from 30° down to 5° elevation makes the path about 5.7 times longer.课外补充（平地近似）：穿过大气的路程 ∝ 1/sin θ。sin 30° / sin 5° = 0.5 / 0.0872 ≈ 5.7，仰角从 30° 降到 5°，路程约长 5.7 倍。

Option by option

  • A wrong: the elevation angle has a large effect on the atmospheric path; it does not stay the same.A 错：仰角变化对大气路程影响很大，不会不变。
  • B correct: the path gets longer, and both rain and fog attenuation increase markedly.B 对：路程变长，雨衰、雾衰都明显增大。
  • C wrong: the direction is reversed.
  • D wrong: both rain and fog attenuation grow with the path length, not just one of them; and rain has the larger effect.D 错：雨和雾都随路程增大，不会只有一种增大；而且雨的影响更大。
In one line: the lower the elevation angle, the thicker the atmosphere the signal crosses, and both rain and fog attenuation increase markedly, so B.一句话：仰角越低，信号穿过的大气越厚，雨衰和雾衰都明显增大，选 B。
Concept + Step by step: three communication configurations

ConceptClassify by "who talks to whom"

Notes Part C p.24–25 divide satellite communication into three common configurations. Tell them apart by the numbers of transmitting and receiving stations: one-to-one, one-to-many, hub-to-many (two-way).讲义 Part C p.24–25 把卫星通信分成三种常见配置。区分的方法是看发射站和接收站的数量关系：一对一、一对多、中心对多（双向）。

ConfigurationRelationExample
Point-to-pointOne-to-one, two-wayTransoceanic trunk
BroadcastOne transmitting station → many receiving stations一个发射站 → 多个接收站Satellite TV
Two-way star (VSAT network)One hub ↔ many remote stations一个 hub ↔ 多个远端站Bank branches, petrol stations银行网点、加油站

Step by stepKey points of each configuration

  1. Point-to-point: the satellite provides a link between two earth stations far apart, replacing transoceanic cables; this was the original use of satellites (p.4).点对点：卫星给两个相距很远的地面站提供一条链路，替代跨洋电缆，这正是卫星最初的用途（p.4）。
  2. Broadcast: one earth station with a transmitter serves many earth stations that have only receivers. A single GEO beam covers a very large area, which makes GEO ideal for broadcasting (p.16).广播：一个带发射机的地面站，对许多只有接收机的地面站。GEO 一个波束覆盖很大，最适合广播（p.16）。
  3. Two-way star: one central station (hub) and many remote client stations. The remote stations share the satellite capacity to transmit to the hub; the hub exchanges messages with each station and relays messages between remote stations. Remote stations are usually VSATs with very small antennas (0.3–0.9 m, p.26), because the hub antenna is large and carries most of the link budget.双向星形：一个中心站（hub）和许多远端客户站。远端站共享卫星容量发给 hub；hub 和各站交换消息，并在远端站之间中转。远端站通常是天线很小的 VSAT（0.3–0.9 m，p.26），因为 hub 天线大，链路预算主要靠 hub 撑起来。

Pitfalls

  • In a star network, remote stations do not communicate directly; traffic between them is relayed through the hub (satellite → hub → satellite).星形网里远端站之间不直接通信，要经 hub 中转（卫星 → hub → 卫星）。
  • Broadcast is one-way; point-to-point and star are both two-way.广播是单向的；点对点和星形都是双向。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) Point-to-point: the satellite provides a link between two distant earth stations. (2) Broadcast: the satellite provides service between one earth station with a transmitter and a number of earth stations with receivers. (3) Two-way star (VSAT network): one central hub and many remote client stations; the clients share the satellite capacity to transmit to the hub, and the hub exchanges messages with each client and relays messages between clients.

In one line: point-to-point (two stations), broadcast (one transmits, many receive), two-way star (a hub plus many VSATs, with remote stations relayed through the hub).一句话：点对点（两站）、广播（一发多收）、双向星形（hub 加许多 VSAT，远端经 hub 中转）。
Concept + Step by step: earth-station antenna sizes

ConceptThree classes of earth station by antenna size

An earth station consists of the antenna, tracking system, receiver, transmitter, multiplexer and terrestrial links via modems; the main distinguishing feature of an earth station is its antenna size (notes Part C p.26).地面站由天线、跟踪系统、接收机、发射机、复用器和经调制解调器的地面链路组成；区分地面站的主要特征是天线大小（讲义 Part C p.26）。

TypeAntenna diameter
Large earth station10–60 m
Small earth station1–10 m
VSAT (very small aperture terminal)VSAT（甚小口径终端）0.3–0.9 m

The larger the antenna, the larger the traffic capacity. Beyond the slides: parabolic antenna gain ∝ diameter², so a 10 times larger diameter gives 20 dB more gain.天线越大，业务容量越大。课外补充：抛物面天线增益 ∝ 直径²，直径大 10 倍，增益多 20 dB。

Option by option

  • A wrong: 10–60 m is a large earth station.A 错：10–60 m 是大型地面站。
  • B wrong: 1–10 m is a small earth station.B 错：1–10 m 是小型地面站。
  • C correct: VSAT = Very Small Aperture Terminal; the name says the aperture is "very small", 0.3–0.9 m, about the size of a home satellite TV dish.C 对：VSAT = Very Small Aperture Terminal，名字就说明口径"非常小"，0.3–0.9 m，和家里的卫星电视锅差不多。
  • D wrong: an antenna of a few centimetres has too little gain to pick up the weak signal from a GEO satellite.D 错：几厘米的天线增益太低，收不到 GEO 卫星的弱信号。
In one line: VSAT antennas are 0.3–0.9 m (small stations 1–10 m, large stations 10–60 m), so C.一句话：VSAT 天线 0.3–0.9 m（小型 1–10 m，大型 10–60 m），选 C。
Concept + Step by step: satellite bands and services

ConceptThe band table on notes p.27

Frequency bandScopeMain services
L1–2 GHzMSS (mobile)
S2–4 GHzMSS, NASA, deep space
C4–8 GHzFSS (fixed)
X8–12.5 GHzMilitary, meteorological
Ku12.5–18 GHzFSS, BSS
K18–26.5 GHzBSS, FSS
Ka26.5–40 GHzFSS

BSS (Broadcast Satellite Service) is direct TV and radio broadcasting (p.8). Why Ku: the frequency is high and the bandwidth is large, and the same antenna gives more gain, so a small home dish (about 0.6 m) can receive it. The lecturer stressed in class: Ku and Ka are widely used, but suffer heavy rain attenuation, because raindrops are close in size to the wavelength (the Ku wavelength is about 1.7–2.4 cm).BSS（Broadcast Satellite Service，广播卫星业务）是电视、广播直播（p.8）。用 Ku 的原因：频率高、带宽大，同样的天线增益更高，家用小锅（0.6 m 左右）就能收。老师课上强调：Ku、Ka 很常用，但雨衰大，因为雨滴尺寸接近波长（Ku 波长约 1.7–2.4 cm）。

Option by option

  • A wrong: L band is used for the mobile satellite service, MSS.A 错：L 波段用于移动卫星业务 MSS。
  • B wrong: C band is mainly the fixed satellite service, FSS.B 错：C 波段主要是固定卫星业务 FSS。
  • C correct: Ku (and K) are used for BSS.
  • D wrong: S band is MSS and deep-space research.D 错：S 波段是 MSS 和深空研究。

Memory hook

"Low bands for mobile (L, S), C for fixed, Ku/K for broadcast"."低频给移动（L、S），C 给固定，Ku/K 给广播"。

In one line: BSS mainly uses the Ku (and K) band; L and S are mobile and C is fixed, so C.一句话：BSS 主要用 Ku（以及 K）波段；L、S 是移动，C 是固定，选 C。
Concept + Step by step: usable channel bandwidth

ConceptFDMA splits into channels first; subtract the guard band

The satellite's total capacity is first divided by FDMA (frequency division multiple access) into a number of physical channels, which are then allocated further (notes Part C p.28). Adjacent channels must be separated by a guard band: filters are not ideal and the signal spectrum "leaks" into neighbouring channels, so the guard band is a stretch of unused frequency that stops adjacent channels from interfering with each other. So:卫星的总容量先用 FDMA（频分多址）切成若干物理信道，信道里面再进一步分配（讲义 Part C p.28）。相邻信道之间必须留保护带（guard band）：滤波器不是理想的，信号频谱会"漏"到旁边，保护带就是一段空着不用的频率，防止相邻信道互相干扰。所以：

Usable bandwidth = channel bandwidth − guard band可用带宽 = 信道带宽 − 保护带

Step by stepWork it out step by step

  1. Each channel is 40 MHz, of which 4 MHz is guard band and cannot carry data.每个信道 40 MHz，其中 4 MHz 是保护带，不能传数据。
  2. Subtract to get the usable bandwidth; also compute the guard-band share.相减得到可用带宽；顺便算保护带占比。
  3. Check the total: 24 channels make 960 MHz, more than the 500 MHz total bandwidth, which means frequency reuse is used (the notes' wording: "by frequency reuse technique").检查总量：24 个信道共 960 MHz，大于总带宽 500 MHz，说明用了频率复用（讲义原话 "by frequency reuse technique"）。
Usable = 40 − 4 = 36 MHz
Guard-band share = 4 / 40 = 10%
24 × 40 = 960 MHz ≈ 1.9 × 500 MHz可用 = 40 − 4 = 36 MHz
保护带占比 = 4 / 40 = 10%
24 × 40 = 960 MHz ≈ 1.9 × 500 MHz

Beyond the slidesHow the reuse is done

The usual method is two orthogonal polarisations: fit 12 channels of 40 MHz (480 MHz) into the 500 MHz and use them once in horizontal and once in vertical polarisation, giving 24.常见做法是两种正交极化：500 MHz 里放 12 个 40 MHz 信道（480 MHz），水平、垂直极化各用一遍，就是 24 个。

Pitfalls

  • Using 500 / 24 = 20.8 MHz: the question already says each channel is 40 MHz; this works by reuse, not by splitting the band evenly.用 500 / 24 = 20.8 MHz：题目已说每信道 40 MHz，靠复用，不是平分。
  • Using 40 − 2 × 4: the 4 MHz guard band is already included in the 40 MHz; subtract it only once.用 40 − 2 × 4：保护带 4 MHz 已经包含在40 MHz 里，只扣一次。

ExamHow to write it in English

Each 40-MHz channel includes a 4-MHz guard band, so the usable bandwidth per channel = 40 − 4 = 36 MHz. (24 × 40 = 960 MHz exceeds 500 MHz, which is possible by frequency reuse.)

In one line: 40 − 4 = 36 MHz, and the guard band takes 10%; the 24 channels fit into 500 MHz through frequency reuse.一句话：40 − 4 = 36 MHz，保护带占 10%；24 个信道靠频率复用装进 500 MHz。
Concept + Step by step: FAMA, DAMA and CSC

ConceptCapacity: "fixed split" or "split on demand"

Notes Part C p.29–30. FAMA (Fixed-Assignment Multiple Access): capacity is assigned to each station in advance and stays fixed. DAMA (Demand-Assignment Multiple Access): the assignment is adjusted at any time as the stations' demand changes. The lecturer stressed in class: FAMA is assigned in advance and cannot be changed; DAMA treats part of the links as a common pool and assigns them on demand, which is more flexible.讲义 Part C p.29–30。FAMA（Fixed-Assignment Multiple Access，固定分配多址）：容量预先固定分给各站。DAMA（Demand-Assignment Multiple Access，按需分配多址）：根据各站需求的变化随时调整分配。老师课上强调：FAMA 预先分好、不能改；DAMA 把一部分链路当公共池，按需分配，更灵活。

FAMADAMA
AssignmentFixedDynamic, on demand
DisadvantagesMuch capacity sits idle when demand fluctuates需求波动时容量大量闲置Needs signalling and scheduling需要信令和调度
FDMA versionEach station's band is assigned in advance各站频带预先分好Subchannels form a pool; a pair is assigned on demand子信道组成池，按需分一对

Step by stepHow CSC works

  1. Resource pool: the subchannels in a channel are treated as a pool of available links. When two earth stations need full-duplex communication, they are dynamically given a pair of subchannels (one in each direction).资源池：一个信道里的子信道（subchannel）当作可用链路池。两个地面站要全双工通信时，动态分给它们一对子信道（一去一回）。
  2. Distributed assignment: no central station approves each request; the earth stations coordinate among themselves through the Common Signalling Channel (CSC).分布式分配：没有中心站逐个审批，由各地面站自己通过公共信令信道 CSC（Common Signalling Channel）协调。
  3. CSC frame structure: the CSC repeatedly transmits a TDMA frame of 50 time slots; the 1st is used for synchronisation, and the other 49 are permanently assigned to 49 stations.CSC 帧结构：CSC 反复发送一个 TDMA 帧，50 个时隙；第 1 个用于同步，其余 49 个永久分给 49 个站。
  4. Occupancy broadcast: after a station has chosen its subchannels, it broadcasts their numbers in its own slot; all other stations hear this and do not choose those subchannels, which avoids collisions.占用广播：某站选好子信道后，在自己的时隙里广播所选子信道的编号；其他站都听得到，就不会再选这些子信道，避免冲突。
  5. Fairness: for fair use of the subchannels, a central scheduler is still needed (last point on p.30).公平：要公平使用子信道，还需要一个集中调度器（p.30 最后一点）。

Why DAMA is better: when a station is idle under FAMA, nobody else can use its share of capacity; under DAMA, idle subchannels go back to the pool for busy stations to use.为什么 DAMA 好：某站空闲时，FAMA 下它那份容量别人用不上；DAMA 下空闲的子信道回到池里给忙的站用。

Pitfalls

  • The CSC itself is a TDMA frame, while what it assigns are FDMA subchannels. Do not mix up the two levels.CSC 本身是 TDMA 帧，而它分配的是 FDMA 子信道，两层别混。
  • The number of stations supported is 49, not 50 (see c18).能支持的站数是 49，不是 50（见 c18）。

ExamHow to write it in English

FAMA assigns capacity to the stations in a fixed manner; since demand fluctuates, capacity is significantly under-used. DAMA changes the assignment as needed to respond to demand. In DAMA-FDMA, the subchannels in a channel form a pool; a pair of subchannels is dynamically assigned for a full-duplex link between two earth stations. The assignment is done in a distributed way using a common signalling channel (CSC), which carries a repetitive TDMA frame of 50 slots: the first slot is for synchronisation and the other 49 are permanently assigned to 49 stations. A station that selects subchannels transmits their identifiers in its own slot, so other stations will not select them. A centralised scheduler is needed for fair use.

In one line: FAMA assigns fixed shares and wastes capacity; DAMA assigns on demand; DAMA-FDMA uses the CSC (a 50-slot TDMA frame, 1 sync + 49 stations) to broadcast which subchannels each station occupies.一句话：FAMA 固定分、浪费；DAMA 按需分；DAMA-FDMA 靠 CSC（50 时隙 TDMA 帧，1 同步 + 49 站）广播自己占用的子信道。
Concept + Step by step: number of stations the CSC supports

ConceptHow the 50 CSC slots are used

The common signalling channel (CSC) of DAMA-FDMA repeatedly transmits a TDMA frame of 50 time slots (notes Part C p.30). The 1st slot is used for synchronisation: all stations use it to align with the start of the frame, so they know "which slot it is now"; otherwise stations would transmit in other stations' slots. The other 49 slots are permanently assigned to 49 stations, one per station, used to broadcast which subchannels the station has chosen.DAMA-FDMA 的公共信令信道 CSC 反复发送一个 TDMA 帧，共 50 个时隙（讲义 Part C p.30）。第 1 个时隙用于同步：所有站靠它对齐帧的起点，才知道"现在是第几个时隙"，否则各站会在别人的时隙里发送。其余 49 个时隙永久分给 49 个站，每站一个，用来广播自己选了哪些子信道。

Step by step

  1. What: subtract the sync slot from the total. Why: the sync slot belongs to no station.做什么：从总时隙里扣掉同步时隙。为什么：同步时隙不属于任何站。
  2. Each station permanently holds one slot, so the number of stations = the number of remaining slots.每站固定占一个时隙，所以站数 = 剩下的时隙数。
Stations supported = 50 − 1 = 49

Sanity check: the notes say "Others are permanently assigned to 49 stations", which agrees.合理性检查：讲义原话 "Others are permanently assigned to 49 stations"，一致。

Pitfalls

  • Answering 50: forgetting that the 1st slot is for synchronisation.答 50：忘了第 1 个时隙是同步用的。
  • Answering 24 or 25 (thinking full duplex needs a pair of slots): the slots are for sending signalling, one per station; what comes in pairs are the FDMA subchannels, not the CSC slots.答 24 或 25（以为全双工要两个时隙一对）：时隙用来发信令，每站一个；成对的是 FDMA 子信道，不是 CSC 时隙。

ExamHow to write it in English

The CSC frame has 50 slots; the first slot is used for synchronisation and the remaining 49 slots are permanently assigned to stations, so at most 50 − 1 = 49 earth stations are supported.

In one line: 50 slots minus 1 sync slot gives at most 49 stations.一句话：50 个时隙减去 1 个同步时隙，最多 49 个站。
Concept + Step by step: why TDMA is more efficient than FDMA

ConceptCompare how much capacity the "overhead" takes

Both multiple-access schemes have overhead: FDMA needs a guard band (a stretch of unused frequency) between adjacent channels; TDMA needs a guard time between adjacent bursts, plus control bits such as the reference burst and preambles in each frame. Notes Part C p.35: the capacity taken by TDMA's guard times and control bits is less than that taken by FDMA's guard bands, so TDMA is usually more efficient. In the higher Ku and K bands, narrow beams also allow multi-beam reuse, which raises efficiency further.两种多址都有开销：FDMA 相邻信道之间要留保护带（guard band，一段不用的频率）；TDMA 相邻突发之间要留保护时间（guard time），每帧还有参考突发和前导等控制比特。讲义 Part C p.35 原话：TDMA 的保护时间和控制比特占用的容量，比 FDMA 的保护带少，所以 TDMA 通常更高效。在 Ku、K 高频段还能用窄波束做多波束复用，效率更高。

Example beyond the slides: TDMA frame 2 ms, reference burst 20 µs, 10 stations each with a 10 µs preamble + 2 µs guard: overhead 140 µs → efficiency 93%
FDMA: a 40 MHz channel containing a 4 MHz guard band → efficiency 90%课外举例：TDMA 帧 2 ms，参考突发 20 µs，10 站各 10 µs 前导 + 2 µs 保护：开销 140 µs → 效率 93%
FDMA：40 MHz 信道含 4 MHz 保护带 → 效率 90%

Option by option

  • A wrong: the opposite is true. TDMA needs strict time synchronisation so that each station lands exactly in its own slot.A 错：恰恰相反，TDMA 需要严格的时间同步，各站才能准确落在自己的时隙里。
  • B correct: the reason given on notes p.35.B 对：讲义 p.35 的原因。
  • C wrong: both share the same transponder bandwidth; the difference in efficiency comes from the overhead, not from the amount of bandwidth.C 错：两者共用同一个转发器带宽，效率差别来自开销，不是带宽大小。
  • D wrong: satellite communication of course needs earth stations.D 错：卫星通信当然需要地面站。
In one line: TDMA's guard times and control bits take less capacity than FDMA's guard bands, so B.一句话：TDMA 的保护时间和控制比特比 FDMA 的保护带占用更少容量，选 B。
Concept + Step by step: number of SS/TDMA modes

ConceptThe satellite acts as a switch in the sky

In the Ku and K bands, several narrow beams can each illuminate one of N areas (notes Part C p.35). Stations within one area use ordinary FAMA-TDMA; for communication between areas, the satellite must switch time slots from one uplink beam onto another downlink beam. This is satellite-switched TDMA (SS/TDMA), a form of DAMA-TDMA (p.36). At any moment, the on-board switch connects the N uplink beams to the N downlink beams one-to-one; each such connection pattern is called a mode. Notes: full connectivity needs N! modes; the satellite changes mode periodically, at most once per slot, and the modes and their durations can be adjusted by ground command.Ku、K 频段可以用多个窄波束分别照 N 个区域（讲义 Part C p.35）。同一区域内的站用普通 FAMA-TDMA；不同区域之间通信，卫星要把某个上行波束的时隙交换到另一个下行波束上，这叫卫星交换 TDMA（SS/TDMA），是 DAMA-TDMA 的一种（p.36）。任一时刻，星上开关把 N 个上行波束一一对应地接到 N 个下行波束，每一种接法叫一个模式（mode）。讲义：全连通需要 N! 种模式；卫星周期性换模式，最多每个时隙换一次，模式和时长可由地面指令调整。

Step by stepWhy N!

  1. One mode = arranging the N uplink beams onto the N downlink positions, with each downlink connected to exactly one uplink; this is exactly a permutation of N elements.一种模式 = 把 N 个上行波束排到 N 个下行位置上，每个下行只接一个上行，这正是 N 个元素的一个排列。
  2. The 1st uplink has N choices, the 2nd has N − 1 left, ... so the number of permutations = N × (N − 1) × … × 1 = N!.第 1 个上行有 N 种选择，第 2 个剩 N − 1 种……所以排列数 = N × (N − 1) × … × 1 = N!。
  3. Substitute N = 5.
N = 3: 3! = 6 (ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA)
N = 4: 4! = 24
N = 5: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 modes

Beyond the slides(not in the notes)

Strictly, N! is the total number of possible switch modes. If all you need is that "any two areas can be connected at some moment", N cyclic-shift modes already cover all N² uplink–downlink combinations. In the exam, write N! as in the notes.严格说，N! 是所有可能的开关模式总数。如果只要求"任意两个区域之间某个时刻能连通"，N 个循环移位模式就能覆盖全部 N² 个上下行组合。考试按讲义写 N!。

Pitfalls

  • Answering N² = 25 or N(N − 1) = 20: that is the number of "uplink–downlink pairs", not the number of modes.答 N² = 25 或 N(N − 1) = 20：那是"上下行对"的个数，不是模式数。
  • Answering 5 × 2 = 10 or similar: a mode is a whole permutation, not a single connection.答 5 × 2 = 10 等：模式是整体排列，不是单条连接。

ExamHow to write it in English

Each mode is a one-to-one connection of the N uplink beams to the N downlink beams, i.e. a permutation, so N! modes are required for full connectivity: 5! = 120 modes.

In one line: each mode is a permutation; full connectivity needs N! modes, and 5! = 120.一句话：每种模式是一个排列，全连通需要 N! 种，5! = 120。
Concept + Step by step: TDMA frame structure

ConceptWhy the TDMA frame is designed this way

Satellite TDMA (notes Part C p.31): transmission is a repeating frame divided into time slots, and each station gets one or more slots; stations take turns sending on the uplink in their own slots, and the satellite broadcasts what it receives to all stations, so each station must know which slot to send in and which to receive in. The difficulty is that the stations are at different distances from the satellite and their clocks are not exactly the same, so the frame must contain a "timing reference" and a "self-introduction". The figure on p.32 is the answer.卫星 TDMA（讲义 Part C p.31）：传输是重复的帧，每帧分成若干时隙，每个站分到一个或多个时隙；各站轮流在自己的时隙发上行，卫星把收到的内容广播给所有站，每个站要知道哪个时隙发、哪个时隙收。难点在于：各站离卫星距离不同，时钟也不完全一样，所以帧里必须有"定时基准"和"自我介绍"。p.32 的图就是答案。

PartItemEffect
Reference burstCarrier and bit timing recovery, coordination data载波与比特定时恢复、协调数据Gives the whole network a time reference and tells the stations where the frame starts给全网一个时间基准，告诉各站帧从哪里开始
Guard timeGap between bursts突发之间的空隙Absorbs the stations' timing errors and stops bursts from overlapping吸收各站的定时误差，防止突发重叠
Station data bursts各站数据突发Preamble + informationEach station transmits in its own slot每站在自己的时隙发送

Step by stepThe four fields of the preamble

  1. Carrier and bit timing recovery: the receiver first locks onto the burst's carrier phase and bit clock so that it can demodulate correctly. Each station's burst comes from a different transmitter, so recovery is needed for every burst.载波与比特定时恢复（carrier and bit timing recovery）：接收机先锁定这个突发的载波相位和比特时钟，才能正确解调。每个站的突发来自不同发射机，所以每个突发都要重新恢复。
  2. Unique word: a fixed bit pattern used to find exactly where the information starts in the burst (burst location).唯一字（unique word）：一段固定的比特图样，用来准确找到突发里信息开始的位置（突发定位）。
  3. Station identification: says which station sent this burst.站识别（station identification）：说明这个突发是哪个站发的。
  4. Network control and request: carries network management information or requests for more capacity.网络控制与请求（network control and request）：传网络管理信息，或请求更多容量。

Only after the preamble comes the actual information. p.33–34: on the uplink, stations transmit in different slots; on the downlink, the satellite broadcasts the whole frame back, and each station picks out the part addressed to it.前导后面才是真正的信息（information）。p.33–34：上行时各站在不同时隙发送；下行时卫星把整帧广播回去，各站挑出发给自己的部分。

Pitfalls

  • The reference burst is at the start of the frame, one per frame; the preamble is at the start of each station's burst, one per station.参考突发在帧开头，每帧一个；前导在每个站的突发开头，每站一个。
  • Guard times, the reference burst and the preambles are all overhead; this is the "guard time and control bits" in c19.保护时间、参考突发、前导都是开销，这就是 c19 说的"保护时间和控制比特"。

ExamHow to write it in English

A TDMA frame starts with a reference burst (carrier and bit timing recovery, coordination data), followed by the data bursts of the individual stations, separated by guard times. Each station's burst consists of a preamble and information. The preamble contains carrier and bit timing recovery, a unique word, station identification, and network control and request; the information field carries the user data.

In one line: reference burst + station data bursts (separated by guard times); each burst = preamble (timing recovery, unique word, station identification, network control and request) + information.一句话：参考突发 + 各站数据突发（中间隔保护时间）；每个突发 = 前导（定时恢复、唯一字、站识别、网络控制与请求）+ 信息。
Concept + Step by step: routing with inter-satellite links

ConceptTwo routing schemes

Notes Part C p.39: two users are each under a different satellite. With inter-satellite links (ISL), the information is passed directly in space from one satellite to the other; without them, the satellite first sends it down to a ground gateway, it is routed over the terrestrial network to the gateway serving the other satellite, and then it is sent up again.讲义 Part C p.39：两个用户分别在两颗卫星下面。有星间链路（ISL，Inter-Satellite Link）时，信息在太空中直接从一颗卫星转到另一颗；没有时，卫星先下传到地面网关，经地面网络路由到负责另一颗卫星的网关，再上传。

With ISLWithout ISL
PathUser A ↑ satellite 1 → satellite 2 ↓ user B用户 A ↑ 卫星 1 → 卫星 2 ↓ 用户 BA ↑ satellite 1 ↓ gateway 1 → terrestrial network → gateway 2 ↑ satellite 2 ↓ BA ↑ 卫星 1 ↓ 网关 1 → 地面网 → 网关 2 ↑ 卫星 2 ↓ B
Number of links1 up + 1 down2 up + 2 down
Ground gatewaysbehindahead

Option by option

  • A correct: one uplink into space, relay between the satellites, one downlink to the other user.A 对：上行一次进入太空，星间转发，下行一次到达对方。
  • B wrong: that is the case without inter-satellite links.B 错：这是没有星间链路的情况。
  • C wrong: the users are on the ground, so at least one up and one down are needed.C 错：用户在地面，至少要一上一下。
  • D wrong: the numbers of uplinks and downlinks must be equal; on a one-way path, every entry into space is matched by an exit.D 错：上下行数应相等，单向路径进出太空各一次。

Memory hook

Count how many times the signal "enters and leaves space": with ISL, once each; without ISL it must come back to the ground midway, so twice each.数"进出太空"的次数：有 ISL 进出各一次；无 ISL 中途要回地面一趟，进出各两次。

In one line: with inter-satellite links, 1 up and 1 down, and fewer gateways are needed; without them, 2 up and 2 down, so A.一句话：有星间链路时 1 上 1 下，还能少建网关；没有时 2 上 2 下，选 A。
Concept + Step by step: four types of handover in satellite systems

ConceptWhy MEO/LEO systems need handover

In terrestrial cellular networks, handover is almost always caused by the user moving. MEO and LEO satellites move relative to the ground (each LEO is visible for only 15–20 minutes); if the satellite itself carries the "base station", a handover is needed when the satellite flies away, even if the user is not moving (notes Part C p.40). GEO is stationary relative to the ground and hardly needs handover. This is 2025-26 S2 final Q4(b), 8 marks; the lecturer stressed in class that satellites are a very important future direction and mentioned that this question was tested in the final, so you must memorise it.地面蜂窝里，切换（handover）几乎都是用户在动引起的。MEO、LEO 卫星相对地面在动（LEO 每颗只可见 15–20 分钟），如果卫星本身带着"基站"，即使用户不动，卫星一飞走也要切换（讲义 Part C p.40）。GEO 相对地面静止，几乎不用切换。这一题是 2025-26 S2 期末 Q4(b)，8 分；老师课上强调卫星是未来很重要的方向，并提到期末考过这一题，属于必背。

Step by stepFour handovers: look at "what changed"

HandoffCauseExample
Intra-satelliteThe user moves from one sector (spot beam) to another within the same satellite's coverage用户在同一颗卫星覆盖区内，从一个扇区（点波束）移到另一个Driving across the boundary between two spot beams开车穿过两个点波束交界
Inter-satelliteThe user moves into another satellite's coverage, or the satellite itself flies away用户移到另一颗卫星的覆盖区，或卫星自己飞走The LEO overhead sets below the horizon; switch to the next one头顶 LEO 落下地平线，转到下一颗
GatewayThe satellite leaves its current ground gateway卫星离开当前地面网关The satellite switches its connection to another gateway卫星改连另一个网关
Inter-systemA vertical handover between the satellite system and a terrestrial cellular system, triggered by signal strength and QoS卫星系统与地面蜂窝系统之间，因信号强度和 QoS 发生的垂直切换Going from the countryside into a city, switching from satellite to 4G从野外进城，从卫星转到 4G
  1. Intra-satellite: the beam changes, the satellite does not.星内：波束变，卫星不变。
  2. Inter-satellite: the satellite changes. There are two causes and you must write both; "the satellite flies away" is specific to satellite systems.星间：卫星变。原因有两个，都要写，"卫星飞走"是卫星系统特有的。
  3. Gateway: the ground gateway changes. It has nothing to do with the user; it is the link between the satellite and the ground that is switched.网关：地面网关变，和用户无关，是卫星和地面之间那条链路在换。
  4. Inter-system: the network type changes, which is why it is called a vertical handover; the decision is based on signal strength and QoS.系统间：网络类型变，所以叫垂直切换（vertical handover），判断依据是信号强度和 QoS。

Pitfalls

  • Writing only "the user moves" for inter-satellite handover and missing "the satellite moves away".星间切换只写"用户移动"，漏了"卫星移走"。
  • For inter-system handover, write "vertical handover" and "signal strength and QoS".系统间切换要写出 "vertical handover" 和 "signal strength and QoS"。
  • In an 8-mark question each of the four points is worth about 2 marks: write one sentence of "name + cause" for each; do not just list the names.8 分题四点各约 2 分：每种写"名称 + 原因"一句，不要只列名字。

ExamHow to write it in English

(1) Intra-satellite handover: caused by the movement of a mobile user within the coverage of one satellite, from one sector (spot beam) to another. (2) Inter-satellite handover: caused by the movement of a mobile user from the coverage of one satellite to that of another, or because the satellite moves away. (3) Gateway handover: caused by the movement of the satellite away from its current gateway, so the satellite must connect to another gateway. (4) Inter-system handover: between the satellite system and a terrestrial cellular system; it is a vertical handover triggered by signal strength and QoS performance.

In one line: beam changes → intra-satellite; satellite changes → inter-satellite; gateway changes → gateway; system changes → inter-system (vertical handover).一句话：波束变 → 星内；卫星变 → 星间；网关变 → 网关；系统变 → 系统间（垂直切换）。
